   Vault mend and build, the union mines, citizens and the Fleet's deckhands carry and clean, the Lattice crafts, the
   Choir makes art), their faith (`FaithWork`: learning prized, mining's yield, trees desired, art desired, dumb labour
   exalted, crafting by hand, a strong bond with animals; each an active PreceptDef of the player's), a minor passion,
   or a hard worker's hauling and cleaning (Industriousness above zero). No fit, no everyday work, even where
   Hospitality would allow it. The first time they take up a kind of work they say why in one sentence
   (`Rimfolk_Pool_GuestHelpFit`, by the reason, the work and their people's ways). A postfix on `PawnCanUseWorkGiver`
   (`Patch_GuestHelpWorkGiver`, after Hospitality's own prefix) narrows its answer; their own care (Patient work) is
   never touched. Hospitality's switch and minimum skill hold.
2. **Pitching in during a crisis** (`ForGuest`, `CrisisOf`; each start and end a pure rule, worked out per map every
   250 ticks): a fire in the home area within 20 cells of them (`FightFires` and mods' own fires); someone of the colony
   downed outside a bed (Rimfolk's `JobGiver_GuestRescue` makes the game's rescue job, since its work giver only rescues
   one's own people, and never while an enemy is within 40 cells, the game's own rule); the colony's people waiting to be
   tended within a day after a raid, no enemy about (`DoctorTendToHumanlikes`, `DoctorTendEmergency`, Medicine 4 or more,
   tending only, never surgery, an animal or themselves); crops the frost harvest marked still standing
   (`GrowerHarvest`, `PlantsCut`); the food under three days (`MapFacts.FoodDays`) until four again (cooking and
   butchering, never brewing; Cooking 4 or more). In trouble they pitch in to, whatever their mood and Hospitality's
   roll, they do only that trouble's work (`Allow`) until it ends; a trouble's job still running when it ends is put
   down (a fire's and a rescue's end by themselves). Hospitality's mood line is opened by name
   (`Patch_GuestHelpWantsToHelp` on `ThinkNode_ConditionalWantsToHelp.Satisfied`), and since its guest duty puts their
   needs first (its `JobGiver_Relax` asks for them whenever joy is under 90%), Rimfolk's own step sits on the game's
   `Humanlike_PreMain` hook that Hospitality's duty offers before their needs (`Defs/Misc/Rimfolk_GuestHelp.xml`:
   `ThinkNode_GuestPitchIn`, the rescue, then `JobGiver_Work`), unless starving or exhausted. The trouble's work types
   (Doctor, Growing, Plant cutting, Cooking) are turned on in their guest's work settings while it lasts and off again
   (`WorkTypesFor`, saved so a load still turns them off). Each says why (`Rimfolk_Pool_GuestHelpCrisis`) and a message
   names who helps and with what (one a trouble a map). **With Hospitality's own helping switched off, guests still fight
   fires and carry the downed in, nothing more** (`WithHospitalityOff`): saving a life isn't chores, and the player
   switched the chores off.
3. **Thanks paid in work.** A guest the colony carried in (Hospitality's rescued guest), once set free (a notable met
   as freed), tended (KinMemory's note of a colony doctor), feasted (their people's notable feasted within three days)
   or hosted very well (Hospitality's score 0.9 or more) offers, once a visit, on a morning (6 to 11) with no trouble
   on, a day of their best-loved work (`BestLoved`: the highest passion, then the best skill; never tending, never what
   Hospitality's settings or minimum skill keep from them). That work goes on in their area for a day, beyond the cap and
   Hospitality's roll. A line over them (`Rimfolk_Pool_GuestHelpThanks`), the evening's news and their history
   (`guestHelp:thanks`, the guest and their people) keep it.
4. **Some guests won't** (`Refuse`, `RefuseGiver`). The titled (the Empire's own titles), and notables who are their
   town's head or heir or proud (the persona's Pride at 30) never do menial work (hauling, cleaning, plant cutting), and
   in trouble only pitch in to save a life (a fire, a rescue, the wounded). Each faith keeps its customs (no mining, no
   study, no dumb labour, no hunting or slaughter where killing animals is wrong, no butchering where meat is, no tree
   ever where felling is), and each people its own (the Mossborn never fell a tree, the Ashen Banner does no everyday
   work, being for hire, though it pitches in). No guest ever goes into a bedroom, barracks or cell for work, does
   surgery, prisoners' or entities' work, the colony's children's or its management, or touches the dead (corpses,
   graves, stripping, cremation), a rescue aside (`Vetoed` on the job `JobGiver_Work` chose, `Patch_GuestHelpJob`).
5. **Limits.** About three hours of everyday work a day (`CapTicks`; the trouble's and the thanks day's apart): they
   put it down with a word (`s:enough`). Under Hospitality's own line (75%) they put everyday work down (`s:unhappy`).
   Past six hours of work in a day (the cap and a trouble on top) they're overworked: only a life-saving trouble until
   tomorrow, a small bad mood for two days (`Rimfolk_GuestOverworked`, -4: Hospitality's score of the visit reads their
   mood, so it costs the colony a little at their leaving), regard lost with them if they're a notable, a line
   (`s:overworked`) and the evening's news.
6. **It counts both ways.** A guest and a colonist at the same work within six cells think a little better of each other,
   both ways, once a day each pair (`Rimfolk_GuestWorkedBeside`, +3 opinion, six days: the game's own opinion, which
   Hospitality counts toward its friends). A guest who helped and leaves as a friend (not dead, taken in or a prisoner,
   their people not at war) speaks well of the colony at home (`SpeakWell`: 1 for an hour of everyday help, 2 for four, 2
   for a trouble, 1 for a thanks day, 4 at most) with each of their people's notables (six at most, and themselves if
   one), through the notables' own regard and memory. A guest hurt at the colony's work (a new wound while at it, or one
   that ended the job: the game's own fire, a raider's shot at a rescue, an animal's bite; Rimfolk adds no harm of its
   own, so it comes at the game's rate) costs 2 regard with each of them, once a day, told as harm is (a message,
   Important).
7. **You can see it.** On Hospitality's guest tab, above Rimfolk's recruiting checklist (`GuestCheck.cs` draws both
   from its one patch, and the tab grows for either): "Let them help" (on by default; off, no work at all, even in
   trouble; their own care stays theirs), the trouble they're pitching in to, the day of thanks, today's
   hours ("Today: 1 h of 3", or overworked), what they'd help with and why ("Cooking: burning passion", "Handling: what
   the herding folk live by", a note where Hospitality's minimum skill stops it), what they won't ("No hauling:
   titled (Baron)", "Never fells a tree"), and the never line.

- **Every age.** It works the same in every age; what they say takes their people's ways (`their:tribal`, `medieval`,
  `industrial`, `spacer`, the Empire's own), never the colony's age.
- **Saved** (`GuestHelpBook`, a game component): one record per guest staying (`GuestHelpMath.MaxGuests` 30 at most):
  the switch, the day's and the visit's hours, the overworked day, the kinds of work said (`MaxTold` 12), the work types
  turned on (`MaxEnabled` 5), the thanks day, the troubles said. Let go at the pass after they leave (their farewell),
  and never saved once gone. Modelled in `Tools/save_estimate.py`.
- **The clock:** `Sched.RareGuestHelp` (tick 119 of the 250-tick cycle, only while guests are on a home map or a record
  waits to be let go).
- **Soft.** Hospitality is read by type name (its think node, its settings, its guest comp's "rescued"); the three patch
  classes stand down without it ("Hospitality isn't loaded"), and the think tree's step says no at once for anyone who
  isn't its guest.

- **Tending by skill** (0.205.1; the player: "i'd rather not have visitor tend the wounds if they're not good doctors. or they
  should only tend bruises and minor injuries otherwise", then "not if every wound is minor, but they should just treat the
  minor ones and leave the others for better doctors"). A guest with a good doctor's Medicine (8, `GuestHelpMath.TendAnyMedicine`)
  tends anything; from Medicine 4 to 7 only a patient's minor conditions (bruises, cuts, everyday ailments, as Rimfolk's
  medicine rules judge them: `MedicineChoice.Judge`), the serious ones left for a better doctor even on the same patient.
  `Patch_GuestHelpTendFit` (postfix on `WorkGiver_Tend.HasJobOnThing`) passes over a patient with nothing they may tend
  (`MayTakePatient`); while such a guest tends (`Patch_GuestHelpTendDoctor`, on `TendUtility.DoTend`), the game's choice of
  what one treatment covers (`Patch_GuestHelpTendMinorOnly`, on `GetOptimalHediffsToTendWithSingleTreatment`) is given only
  the minor conditions tendable now in its own order; nothing minor left when they reach the patient, nothing is done and
  no medicine used. The guest tab says so ("Tends only bruises, cuts and other minor ailments").

### Invited visitors are Hospitality's guests (the player's request, 10 November 2026; released 0.209.0)

The player: "visitors that you invite with diplomatic actions should also be treated as guests with hospitality". With
Hospitality loaded, those the colony invited come and stay as its guests, so its guest area, guest beds, guest tab,
recruiting rules and Rimfolk's guest help (above) apply to them; Rimfolk's purpose for the visit stays on top. The rules
are `Integrations/InvitedGuestsMath.cs` (`InvitedGuestsTests`), the game side `Integrations/InvitedGuests.cs`; the setting
"Invited visitors are guests" (`invitedAsGuests`, on, Your other mods under Hospitality, with the deeper hooks).

- **Who is invited** (`ArrivalWhy`, `Invited`): a notable (or one of their town who can travel) who took up a letter's
  invitation (`NeighbourLetters.TryVisit`: any letter that invites, a pen friend's, a gathering day's); a town's folk asked
  to the colony's feast or fair, or come to a fair it proclaimed (`Dealings.Guests`); a guest of note who wrote ahead and
  was told yes (`HappeningWorker_NotableGuest`); a feast's or a wedding's guests with their retinue (`Feasts.Arrive`); an
  envoy and attendant for a season (`Envoys.Arrive`, `Regroup`). Not invited, and Rimfolk's own as before: a hosting
  mission's guests (a dignitary, refugees, an apprentice, a choir: their people asked, and the mission counts the
  colony's own table and beds, `Hosting.Tend`); errands at the gate with their own ending (a ward's party, a match's
  escort, a parley, an oath, a ransom's messenger, couriers and riders); the strangers stories bring; and those asked to
  live here (kin invited to stay, a visitor asked to join), who join rather than visit. There is no festival's return:
  the colony's entertainers go to the town's festival by caravan and nobody comes back with them. Pen friends visit by a
  letter's invitation.
- **Handed over** (`InvitedGuests.HandOver`), once the group is on the map, when `HandOver` says so (invited, Hospitality's
  way found, the setting and hooks on, their people at peace, every one of them a person of theirs on the map): by name,
  Hospitality's incident's `CreateLord(faction, spot, pawns, map, showLetter: false, getUpsetWhenLost, duration)` (its
  `LordJob_VisitColony`, guest comps, trader status and its map component's guest list), after its own `GiveItems` (the
  food, money and wares its visitors carry). Rimfolk's letter says they came, so Hospitality's isn't shown. Taken whole,
  their group is returned; otherwise any half-made group is let go and the caller makes Rimfolk's own as before
  (`Arrivals.Invited` the game's visit at an errand's pace, the feast `LordJob_FeastGuests`, the envoy
  `LordJob_EnvoyStay`), and everything that touches Hospitality is caught and logged once.
- **How long** (`StayTicks`): the hours Rimfolk planned (a letter's guest 8 to 14, a town's folk 9, a guest of note 18 to
  26; never under 4), and Hospitality's own rule ends it (in daylight). Where Rimfolk ends the stay itself (`RimfolkEnds`:
  the feast's guests, two days; the envoy, the season of 15), a day more, so Hospitality's clock never sends them first;
  never past 16 days. Hospitality's displeasure at losing the whole group (`getUpsetWhenLost`) only where Rimfolk keeps no
  count of its own.
- **The feast on top**: its groups are found among Hospitality's too (`Feasts.Lords`, `LordOf`). Where the day takes them
  (`Feasts.Focus`: the gate, a contest, the table, indoors for the night) is kept with the feast (`GuestFeast.focus`,
  `focusRadius`, saved) and given to Hospitality's guests as the feast's own duty (`InvitedGuests.Steer`,
  `Rimfolk_FeastGuest` at the place, `Rimfolk_FeastIndoors` in danger) at each look, only while they're settled at
  their stay (walking in and out is Hospitality's). The feast's 250-tick look, which its own group gave, comes from the
  guests' pass (`GuestHelpBook`, `Sched.RareGuestHelp`, while a feast's guests or an envoy are at a home:
  `InvitedGuests.Following`, `Rare`). Settled and free to be fed and bedded count Hospitality's stay
  (`InvitedGuests.Staying`), so the feast's hosting rules feed them at its table and put them to bed (Hospitality's guest
  beds first) as before; the play-out's feast keeps them at the table by its own jobs. At first light
  (`Feasts.LeaveAll`) their stay ends as Hospitality's own does (`InvitedGuests.GoHome`, `Leave`: the transition out of
  the stay that its length sets off, with its message, its reckoning of the visit, its gift and its next visit; still
  walking in, straight to its way out).
- **The envoy on top**: found among Hospitality's groups (`Envoys.LordOf`); Hospitality's guest area and rules lead their
  day (the envoy's own common rooms were the same place in effect), indoors in danger by the stay's own duty
  (`Rimfolk_EnvoyIndoors`, `Envoys.HostedLook` every 250 ticks). The stay's hour still feeds them at the colony's table,
  beds them (the bed set aside first), seats the envoy at a council meeting and sends their letters home (`Envoys.Free`
  counts Hospitality's stay); a meal of the colony's or a night in one of its beds that Hospitality gave the envoy first
  still counts for the day. One of them up again with no group goes back the way Hospitality takes a guest in late
  (`LordToil_VisitPoint.JoinLate`, `OnGuestJoinedLate`), else a new group, Hospitality's or the stay's own. The season
  over, the envoy dead or the home lost: `GoHome`.
- **Hurt by the colony**: their own groups heard it from the game's harm trigger; for Hospitality's, a postfix on
  `Lord.Notify_PawnDamaged` (`Patch_InvitedGuestHarmed`) takes outside violence by the colony's people (never a blow in
  an agreed bout, `Outsiders.InBout`) to `Feasts.Harmed` or `Envoys.Harmed`, which end the visit as an insult and send
  them home. Deaths and arrests are seen by the feast's look and the stay's hour as before.

### Neighbours' requests and callers at the gate (the player's request, 6 November 2026)

"Do another big content update to existing mechanics": this part the neighbours and the people who come to the colony,
in the frameworks that were there (missions, data events, letter variants), at the rates there were. The pure rules in
`Missions/NeighboursFourMath.cs` (`NeighboursFourTests`), the workers in `Missions/Workers_MissionNeighbours4.cs`, the
texts in `Defs/MissionDefs/Rimfolk_Missions_Neighbours4*.xml`, `Defs/IncidentDefs/Rimfolk_Events_Neighbours4*.xml`.

- **One draw for every mission.** Every mission offer's base chance is scaled so the missions together weigh what the
  thirteen kinds offered weighed before this round (`MissionPoolWeight`, 6.8; `MissionPool.Factor` in the storyteller's
  draw and Rimfolk's own, `Happenings.cs`; the balance model the same). A new kind takes a share; one mission at a time
  as always.
- **Hands lent to a neighbour's town** (`HappeningWorker_MissionHands`, data `MissionHands`): the harvest hands' way for
  any skill. One or two of the colony's people good at it (a level, the work not disabled), the colony's caravan at the
  people's nearest town within three days, staying there `hours`; the whole stay earns the silver into the packs, a gift
  of things of the colony's era (`Loot`) and the skill's experience; half the stay half the silver, less goodwill lost.
  Builders after a storm or a fire (Construction 5, two, 36 hours), a healer for their sickhouse (Medicine 6 and
  doctoring, one, 48), a teacher for their young (Intellectual 7, one, 36), a witness at a truce or a boundary (Social 6,
  one, 12), a smith before the harvest or the sowing, or a mechanic for a hightech town's pumps (Crafting 6, one, 24). Each
  is remembered as `lentHands` (a debt of honour where those are kept). Every one's forms are by the asking people's age
  (`their:tribal` to `their:spacer`, `their:lowtech`, `their:hightech`, added to every mission's tags) and the Empire's
  own lines keep its knights, stewards and heralds.
- **A store kept** (`HappeningWorker_MissionKeep`): their carts bring grain, timber, steel or cloth to the gate
  (`Couriers.Deliver`), and when the season is up come back for as much (`Couriers.CollectGoals`), paying a quarter of
  its worth (`KeepFee`). What the stores hold then counts, the colony's own the same as theirs, as the terms say. Short,
  the colony pays the rest in silver at its plain worth (`Shortfall`, their carts take it); without the silver they take
  what there is, and remember it.
- **A young beast raised** (`HappeningWorker_MissionBeast`): a foal (lowtech peoples), a calf, a kid or a pup of a kind
  that suits the weather and the land. Their drover walks it in with them to the gate (`Arrivals.Visit`), hands it over
  there (`SetFaction`) and goes; at the end of the season their drover comes for it (the runaway's `HandBack`, its
  `Couriers.Fetch`) and pays all of it kept well (no malnutrition of 0.2, nothing sick, no wound untended) or half kept
  poorly. Dead or lost, goodwill and the memory; bonded to one of the colony's, it stays and they are glad.
- **Someone of theirs lost on the land** (`HappeningWorker_MissionLost`, the lost child's worker with its ages, finder,
  deed and memory as virtual hooks): an old one who wandered off (66 to 86) and a hunter overdue (20 to 55), found by
  whoever comes within six steps in sight, then their kin come; remembered as `foundLost`.
- **A traveller seen home** (`HappeningWorker_MissionEscortWho`, the pilgrim's escort with its ages and variant as hooks):
  a trader with the season's silver past a bandit road, a healer bound for a sickhouse, a scholar with a chest of books.
- **Goods** in the delivery framework, data only: the timber and stone of a wall (a palisade, a wall, a watchtower with
  steel and components for an industrial colony), fodder for their herds (hay and kibble in the fall and winter, hay in a
  dry summer), stores for a long road (pemmican or meals and cloth for pilgrims, meals, cloth and timber for a trek,
  survival packs and medicine for an expedition), and seed after a blight or a flood (corn, rice, potatoes).
- **In the town head's name.** The hands, the store, the beast and every delivery name the town's head by their title
  when the region's ledger knows them (`InviteForms.Host`, `{HOST}` and the tag `host`), the Empire's title for the
  Empire. No line counts the days down: the Quests tab shows the time; endings say what is happening as it happens
  (their carts coming, their drover on the road).
- **Callers at the gate** (data events, `HappeningWorker_Setting`, people of about the colony's age): a herb-gatherer (a
  lesson at their side for the colony's grower, or herbal medicine bought), drovers on the road to a fair (a young beast
  bought, handed over beside them, or a meal carried out), a seed-seller in spring and summer (a patch sown by the grower,
  or a young tree planted at the field's edge), a neighbour's patrol after bandits (fed, a drill for the best shot, or
  medicine sold), a traveller on the wrong road (a meal and the roads gone over at the table), a petitioner with a
  grievance against their own head (heard out at the table), a brewer's cart (beer bought, or brewing secrets for the
  cook). Silence sends them on; nothing gathers the colony, nobody is hurt.
- **More ways to tell the callers** that had one (`LetterVariantsDef`): the barber, the animal doctor, the undertakers, a
  captive's kin and the art collector, by the season, the age and what they find, with an ending for each answer.

### The right-click's things, done by themselves (the player's request, 7 November 2026)

"I'm not really using the right click conversation options, so please integrate them to be done automatically by pawns
when there is a good moment, while still having the gameplay impact and limits in mind." The pure rules in
`Outsiders/OutsiderAutoMath.cs` (`OutsiderAutoTests`), the look in `Outsiders/OutsiderAuto.cs`.

- **The same way as the right-click.** A colonist who does one by themselves goes through `Outsiders.WhyNot` (the menu's
  own reasons: willing, the waits, patience, the thing's own conditions), never one `OutsiderTalk.Repeat` would answer
  with "you asked me that already", and the same jobs (`Outsiders.StartTalk` and `StartGift` with `byThemselves`), so the
  scene (`OutsiderTalk.Begin`: patience spent, the ask noted), the outcome (`Outsiders.Talked`) and the record
  (`Remember`: the pair's waits, the bond, a notable's regard) are the menu's. What differs: the job is not the player's
  order (`playerForced` false, `StartJob` rather than `TryTakeOrderedJob`), so the game may call them away, a turning away
  is said in bubbles only, the meal, lesson or bout that follows is theirs too, and the outcome's everyday messages stay
  unsaid (`Talked(..., byThemselves)`, `StillTold`: a new friend, sweethearts, lovers and someone who stays are still
  told; an injury's message is the bout's own). A letter handed over keeps its message: it was ordered.
- **Which things** (`OutsiderAutoMath.Tier`, the setting `outsiderAuto`: off, free ones only, within limits by default).
  Free: news of home, getting to know them, a good word at home, faith with the same faith (always closer). Within
  limits: a meal when the colonist's food is at 45% or less with meals to spare (the guest's portion counted against
  the budget), a drink at leisure as `Beliefs.MindsDrug` and a teetotaler allow, a gift that suits them (the first of
  their visit, from three times as much, never medicine, weapons, clothes, silver, gold or a hard drug, as much as the
  budget left buys and at least 20 silver), a lesson in a skill the colonist has a passion for, a practice bout between
  two keen on it (accepted at 50% or more, one a day, both clear of `Harm.May`'s cap), courting someone already a
  sweetheart at a 50% chance or more, neither with another partner. The player's alone: a chat (`OutsiderTalk`'s talks
  of their own are one), a letter (written in the player's words), something brought (one ask per people stands at a
  time and the thing is the player's pick), an invitation to stay, courting someone new, faith with another faith, hard
  words, a duel, and the diplomacy acts.
- **The moment.** Every fourth of the outsiders' 250-tick looks (`Sched.RareOutsiderTalk`, no slot of its own), on each
  home with `StoryDanger.None` and no `MapFacts.ThreatOn`: outsiders of another faction, grown, able to talk, not busy
  (`Outsiders.Busy`), leaving, travelling in or through (a travel duty or toil), trading, in a scene or already sought by
  one of the colony's jobs; colonists grown, able to talk, of no lord, idle, wandering or at a recreation job (or in
  their recreation time), free by `PlayOuts.CanJoin` and `Interruptible`, not `NeedsPress`, not one who began one in the
  last six hours. A moment is taken at 35% a look.
- **The pace** (`PaceAllows`): 5 a day across the colony, 2 a day with one outsider, two hours between any two, four with
  the same outsider, an hour after a talk of their own with them, and never their last patience (`PatienceKept`); a
  colonist who asked them something in the last six hours leaves the next ask to someone else, so it is never pushy. The
  stores: `Budget`, a four-hundredth of the home's wealth a day, 30 to 250 silver.
- **The choice** (`Worth`, `WhoScore`, `Score`): each allowed thing with each of the six nearest free colonists, by what
  it would bring now (a good word 6 and more, getting to know them 4 or 7 near friendship, courting 5, news 4 or 1 with
  their news heard lately, faith 3, a lesson 3 and the passion, a meal 4, a drink 3, a gift 2 or 4 with a cool people,
  a bout 3) twice over, and who suits it (Social, their regard and knowing, the speaker or steward with a notable or for
  a good word, the warden of guests, the chaplain for faith, the learner's passion, the fighter, the hungrier, less for
  the shy, the walk, whoever did the last one and each they did today). The best six are checked in full; the first
  that passes begins. Three outsiders are weighed a look at most, in a shuffled order.
- **Saved**: no new collection. The book's day, count, spending, last start and bout day (`OutsiderBook.autoDay` ...
  `autoBoutDay`), and on each visit the day's count and the last start (`OutsiderVisit.autos`, `autoDay`, `autoLast`).
  Who began one lately is the session's, as for the talks of their own.
- **No new Harmony patch, no new letter, no new line**: the words are the menu's own, in the forms of their people's age.

### Camps that build, keep a day and leave things behind (the player's request, 8 November 2026)

The player's camp (a war party of three: a fire, one bedroll, a torch and four lengths of log wall, no room) and their
words: "please review all the camps, ensure they actually construct something proper, they use all the available defs
and also that the people making camp spend the time on the map in a way that makes sense ... there should be no fear of
them contesting ressources ... as long as they don't mine my machinery or valuable metals/items". The follow-ups the same
day: fell the trees in the way rather than give up a layout; pack what they carry and leave their constructions standing;
leave things behind, good or bad, by the kind and the stay.

**What went wrong.** `CampStructure.count` was 1 by default and no kind set a count on its bed: every camp of any size got
one bed. The "windbreak" was a short line of four log walls a cold layout added when the kind built nothing else, and a
hut held one bed. A site needed 80% open, standable ground, so a wooded spot was rejected and a tree under a plan dropped
the building. The kinds named Medieval Overhaul's and Outland's tent pieces, which the player doesn't have enabled.

- **The kit, by age** (`Camps/CampKit.cs`, `Defs/CampDefs/Rimfolk_CampKits.xml`, `CampKitDef`): one kit for each age (tribal,
  medieval, industrial, spacer, by the people's tech level: `CampBuildMath.AgeOf`), each role (fire, bed, tent, hut and
  door, tentwall and tentdoor, the windbreak's wall, table, seat, light, butcher, craft, stall, picket, stash) listing the
  player's active mods' pieces first (`MayRequire`, from `docs/player-mods/buildings.tsv`'s active rows) and the game's
  own last. The first that exists and whose research is within the people's age (`CampKit.Known`) is built, of the first
  listed material it can be made of. A kind's own pieces for a role come first (a shrine's spot, the smith's forge, the
  austere kinds' sleeping spots).
  | Age | Sleep | Hut | Tent | Table, seat | Light |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | tribal | bedroll (leather) | VFE Architect's log wall, else a log wall; Doors Expanded's tribal curtain, else a door | VFE Classical's tent, else small log huts | Alpha Memes' crude wooden table, VFE's sitting cushion | torch lamp |
  | medieval | bedroll (cloth) | VFE Architect's log wall; a wooden door | VFE Classical's tent, else VFE Medieval 2's cloth walls with a curtain (Doors Expanded, More Door Variants) | table, stool | torch lamp |
  | industrial | bedroll (cloth, synthread) | log walls, a wooden door | the same | table, stool | VFE Settlers' chemlamp, else a torch |
  | spacer | bedroll (synthread) | steel walls and door | the same, of synthread | steel table and stool | chemlamp, else a torch |
  Every age: a campfire, a butcher's and a crafting spot, a caravan hitching spot for the picket, a shelf for the stash
  (medieval on, its research), VFE Medieval 2's palisade as the medieval windbreak.
- **How each kind sleeps** (`CampKindDef.sleep`, `CampSleepForm`): round the fire, a bed each (the war party, mourners,
  pilgrims, the procession, penitents, drovers, tree-singers, deserters); one hut for all (settlers, refugees, the hermit,
  the herders' winter camp, the wardens' post, woodcutters, harvest hands, watchers, stranded spacers, the wounded, the
  Banner's squad); tents (hunters, prospectors, traders, the smith, healers, players, surveyors, fishers, salvagers, the
  beast show, the league's winter caravan, trainers, the salt caravan, merchants from afar, the lone healer, minstrels,
  scholars, herb gatherers, stonecutters, shearers, beast-catchers, the teacher): a mod's tent that is a bed (a tent each),
  else tents of tent walls for two, sharing their side walls.
- **The layout** (`Camps/CampBuildMath.cs`, pure, `CampBuildTests`): the fire at the middle with its ring kept free; the
  shelter facing the fire (a hut's inside `RoomSize`: as wide as its beds, at least three, one row of beds to 6 and two
  rows from 7, the doorway's column left free; a tent two wide; walls all round, one door, the inside roofed once every
  wall stands: `Enclosed`, `Inside`); a bed for every sleeper the shelter doesn't hold, round the fire, the far side
  first; a windbreak behind those beds on cold nights; the stash's corner; a table for every four (three at most) for a
  stay of a day and a half or more, a seat on each long side (`TablesFor`); the butcher's spot for those who hunt, the
  crafting spot for a stay of two days or more, the stall on the colony's side, the kind's spot, a light for a small
  camp, two from six, three from ten (`LightsFor`), the picket by the stash for a camp with beasts. Each piece at the
  first of a few fitting places with least to clear, all within ten cells of the fire.
- **The site** (`CampSite.TryFind`, `Layout`): ground clear of the colony (its home area, zones, plans, things), open or
  wooded; each cell's fate (`CampBuildMath.Fate`): free, cut (a bush), fell (a tree; the logs are theirs), haul (a chunk
  or a cheap thing nobody owns), mine (plain rock with no overhead rock within eight cells), or never (the colony's, an
  ore, water and soft ground, someone else's building, a sown or marked plant, anything of value, under the mountain).
  The layout is tried at the spot and a few cells round it, every way round, the complete one with least to clear taken;
  where no shelter fits, they sleep round the fire. A blueprint goes over grass, bushes, trees and chunks (the game's own
  clearing); one over rock or a tree no building goes over waits (`CampPlan.waiting`) until they've mined or felled it;
  only the never-cells drop a piece.
- **The day** (`Camps/CampDay.cs`, `CampDayMath`): night from ten to six in their own beds (each claims one:
  `Camp.BedFor`); a meal in the morning, at noon and at supper (at other hours only when starving), at
  their table's seats, else by the fire (below 55% hungry, so no meal is half wasted); work from seven to noon and one to five, by the kind's callings
  (`CampKindDef.works`) then what each is best at (`CampDayMath.Order`): wood (any wild tree outside the colony's reach,
  a tree or two a day, the woodcutters more), the hunt (armed as the game arms hunters, the kind's rate), a catch where the
  water has fish (Odyssey's or Vanilla Fishing Expanded's; the fishers' own trips besides), plain rock (stonecutters,
  prospectors, the smith, surveyors, settlers, wardens, the Banner's squad), wild plants with food or medicine in them,
  something simple made at their crafting spot from what's in their stash (a recipe the spot knows, within their age,
  worth 200 or less; into their stash), mending their own buildings below 80%, hauling. Supper is cooked at their fire
  from their own meat, what they gathered and their provisions. From seven in the evening they sit by the fire: a word
  between two of them each hour (`Rimfolk_Pool_CampEvening`, by their age) with the game's chat, and with colonists who
  come by as before. Enemies at their camp: those with weapons defend it; an allied people fights beside the colony; the
  war party and a camp standing guard as before; anyone else goes.
- **What they take** (`Camps/CampTakeMath.cs`, `CampTake.cs`, one rule asked by every felling, hunt, gathering, mining,
  clearing and fetching): wild trees, wild beasts (the game's fair game, never one marked), wild plants, plain rock and
  chunks, all clear of the colony. Never the colony's (buildings, machinery, furniture, stockpiled or forbidden things,
  crops, animals, anything in its home area or zones), no mineable that isn't plain rock, decided by its yield (not a
  resource lump, and a stone chunk or nothing, or worth no more than plain stone: so the mods' ores are covered), nothing
  worth more than plain stone. Their own goods, and what their work left, are theirs. The prospectors' finds are their
  dig's, made of nothing on the map, as before.
- **Packing and what stays** (`Camps/CampPack.cs`, `CampPackMath`): going in their own time (the end of the stay, asked,
  moved on, declined, hunger, crowding, unpaid, their own quarrel, the weather, neighbours gone in grief) they pack for
  three hours (one for the weather or hunger; at night they sleep on and pack in the morning; settlers off with the
  colony's caravan pack as they go): bedrolls, tents, tables, stools uninstalled one by one (`Rimfolk_CampPack`, a progress bar) and
  carried in their packs; then the rest of their goods go with them. Constructions (walls, doors, huts and tents of
  walls, the fire pit, the spots, the hitching spot, the torches) stay standing, nobody's (`CampLeaves.Standing`), fires
  put out, roofs on. Three kinds say otherwise (`leaves`, `leavesWhy`): the tree-singers ("their ways leave nothing on the
  land but the saplings they plant") and the penitents ("take up their few things and sweep the ground behind them")
  take theirs down, as do deserters ("so that nobody can follow them"); the Banner's squad hands its post to the colony
  that hired it (`Employer`). Driven off, fleeing or fighting, they leave what they can't carry. The leaving message says
  what still stands.
- **What a stay leaves** (`CampPackMath.Leaves`, each from what happened, each where it lies, named in the leaving
  message; `CampKindDef.leftovers` narrows it: the tree-singers only a gift, deserters nothing):
  | Leftover | When | Where |
  |---|---|---|
  | a woodpile | in their own time, not sour, 25 logs or more left at the stash: 4 in 5 | by the old fire, the colony's |
  | hides | the same, 10 or more of their kills' hides: 2 in 5, 4 in 5 when warm | at their camp's edge nearest the colony |
  | a cairn | the same, 4 or more chunks of the rock they mined: 3 in 5 | by the old fire |
  | a gift | a warm stay (unease under 35, warmth 3 or more): a quarter and more with the warmth, 3 in 5 at most | a gift of their people's own (`ThingRoles` Gift) at the camp's edge |
  | refuse | a sour stay (3 in 5), or a long crowded one (6 days and 6 people: 3 in 10) | filth and ash round the old fire |
  | offal | 2 or more butchered and a hurried or sour going: half | blood and meat at the butcher's spot; half again (the budget) a predator of the land walks in |
  | embers | hot and dry (26 degrees, no rain) and a hurried or sour going: a quarter | half again (the budget) the grass by the fire catches |
  | a lame beast | a camp with beasts, in its own time: about a third | left with the colony, a bruised leg |
  The predator and the fire are the game's own, through the shared budget (`HarmKinds.CampLeft`, "what a camp left
  behind", system `campLeft` on with the camps; base rate 0.0015 a colonist-year from the balance model at 4000 runs,
  its pass about 0.32; the average colony of six stays at 0.459 hurts a colonist-year with the budget).
- **Words.** The letter that brings them says how they'll sleep (`CC_Camp_Facts_Shelter_*`) and the work they mean to do
  (`CC_Camp_Facts_Work`); a camp's lines can ask for what it built (`[shelter:hut]`, `huts`, `tents`, `tentbeds`,
  `ring`); every kind's settled and leaving lines were read against what's now built and done (windbreaks, bedrolls in
  tents, a round house, a hermit's garden nobody made, a struck camp whose walls stand). No camp word says there was no
  room; the diary and the why say the colony's land reaches everywhere a camp could go.
- **Saved**: the plans' room and waiting; the day's new counts and the stay's totals, the packing's ending and hour
  (`Camp.ExposeDay`, `ExposePack`): no new collection. The plans model in `Tools/save_estimate.py` holds up to 90 a camp.
- **Performance**: one job-giver pass per pawn as before; the searches (rock, plants, a catch) each wait hours after
  coming up empty; the layout is worked out once, when a camp is made, from a cell cache.
- **Catalogue**: `Tools/mod_pool.py` writes `docs/player-mods/buildings.tsv` (every building by what it's for, its age,
  stuff, cost, research and work); rebuilt from the player's files and the 8 November save, every other table came out
  the same but `mods.tsv`'s inSave for Harvest and Haul (in the earlier save, not this one).

### Camps side by side, bands against a camp, old camps' sites (the player's requests, 8 November 2026)

The player's words: "my current map is quite huge, so i don't mind a fair amount of camps, would like to see where this
goes. perhaps camps can also get attacked by enemy factions for example. maybe i can set a setting slider for different
levels of amount of camps possible", and later the same day: "they could even move into structures from previous camps
and these places become contested spots". Their map is 275 by 275.

- **How many camps** (`campCrowd`, What's on, world events, under Camps; `Camps/CampCrowdMath.cs`, `CampCrowds.cs`). Four
  named levels; Usual is how camps always came.
  | Level | Daily chance | Rest after one leaves | At once (most) | A band against | A year, 275 by 275 (model) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | Rare | 0.03 | 22 days | 1 | 1 camp in 16 | about 1 camp |
  | Usual | 0.05 | 15 days | 1 | 1 in 9 | 1.5 |
  | Many | 0.12 | 5 days | 2 | 1 in 8 | 4.6 (0.36 on the land on average) |
  | Crowded | 0.30 | 1 day | 4 | 1 in 6 | about 14 (1.1 on the land on average, up to four) |
  The daily chance is before a remote home's more (`TravelLand.CampChance`, up to 60%); the rest before a hospitable or
  remote home's less. The year's figures are from a simple model (stays of three to seven days, every open day tried).
  The map caps the count (`CampCrowdMath.Cap`): under 45,000 cells (200 by 200) one, under 57,000 (225) two, under 70,000
  (250) three, more (275 and up) the level's full count; one fewer when less than three tenths of the map's every third
  cell inside its margin is ground a camp's fire could stand on, clear of the colony (`CampSite.OpenShare`, once a day),
  one only under an eighth. The blocker's "here" stays for a land of one camp; "full" is new for a land that takes more.
- **Side by side.** `CampHome.camps` (a list, saved as `camps`) replaces the one camp; an older save's `camp` is read
  into the list as it loads (`CampHome.ExposeData`, LoadingVars). Camps keep `CampCrowdMath.Apart` (32 cells, both reaches
  and twelve between) between fires, and from every old site (`CampSite.TryFindIn` through `CampCrowds.Apart`): their own
  site, their own fire. Two peoples at war never camp on the same land (`CampCrowds.AtPeaceHere` in `Prepare`, `StartKind`,
  a returning camp, a war party's rest, and the war party that comes to help: its fighters would hunt the other camp),
  unless one came to attack the other. What reads "the camp here" names the one it means: a camp's letter its own
  (`campId`), a question its stranger's camp (`CampTracker.About`: the camp being dealt with, else the stranger's, else
  one that fits), the World page a card for every camp, the camp dilemmas one by the day among those that fit (the same
  all day, so a question and its answer agree), the fire's smoke for each, the market trips, couriers and carries by
  the camp of whoever does them, a war party's rest and a hamlet's settlers' camp when the land has room
  (`CampTracker.RoomFor`). `VisitingAt(map, fits)` picks the first that fits for what can be about any of them.
- **Bands against a camp** (`Camps/CampRaid.cs`, pure `CampRaidMath.cs`). As a camp settles, one roll whether a band comes
  in its stay (`FateChance`: the level's share; a contested site's 1.6 times, at most 0.3; none for stays under a day and
  a half), and when: between the end of its first day and six hours before it would go. At that hour, if nothing puts it
  off (danger on the map, packing, a hazard; up to twelve hours), a people that may (`MayAttack`: at war with the camp's
  people, humanlike, with a combat group, not the colony nor its ally, not gone; one at war with the colony too only while
  the storyteller sends fights, two days past the last big threat, and no truce) is picked (the one that held the site
  before three times as likely, the colony's enemies a little less, by age). Its fighters are the game's own combat group
  of their people (their kinds and their age's gear; Rimfolk's peoples' kits come with their kinds), eight at most, of
  about the camp's armed strength (`Points`: 0.75 to 1.35 times, 80 to 900 points; one at war with the colony too never
  past 0.6 of the colony's threat points). They walk in at the edge nearest the camp and farthest from the colony and
  gather there two or three hours (`LordJob_CampRaid`: the game's staging toil), then go for the camp (the game's defend
  duty at its fire, 20 cells), hold it a while if they win (an hour, half a day for a claim), and run when half of them
  are down (the game's rule). One at war with the colony is told to the storyteller as a raid, so none comes on top of it.
- **The colony's choice**: a camp's letter in a threat's colour (`Rimfolk_CampLetterDanger`), its words by the band's age
  (a war band, a company of armed men, a gang with rifles, a strike team) and how word goes by the colony's (a runner;
  the radio when both ages have it and the colony a comms console). Send our fighters to stand with them (word goes that
  help comes; the player drafts whoever they send, nobody fights unless sent); send word only; stay out (the default).
  Word by a runner is the quickest free grown colonist sprinting to the camp's fire; the camp acts when they get there.
  Warned, the campers stand by their fire if strong enough (`Stand`: armed strength against the band, three quarters of
  it, under half with help coming; a camp of fighters always), else pack an hour and go before the band comes (ending
  "warned", no waiting for morning). Not warned, they find out when the band is within 22 cells, and stand or run then.
  Standing is `LordToil_CampGuard` (added last to the camp's group, so saved groups keep their toils' places): the grown on
  the game's defend duty at their fire, the animals about the camp.
- **How it ends** (`Outcome`): the band down or fled, the campers won (they take up the band's dropped weapons, forbidden
  to the colony and beside one of the band, and tend their hurt with the game's own tending); the campers down or fled,
  or half of them down and outnumbered (`CampersBreak`), lost: they flee with what they carry, their dead lying where they
  fell, their camp left as the 0.167.0 leaving rules leave it; gone in time, the band takes the empty camp; ten hours and
  neither, held, and the band goes. One letter tells it. Fought beside them (a drafted colonist within 30 cells of the
  fire while the band was on it, or near the band anywhere after answering help): 10 goodwill (5 if the camp still fell),
  their people remember it (`sidedWith`), the band's people too (`tookSides`), and holding their camp they carry a gift of
  their own goods (`ThingRoles` gift, 80 silver's worth and 20 more for each of the band down, six at most) to the gate.
  Word in time: 3 goodwill and `warned`. Harming a band at peace with the colony costs goodwill with them by the game's
  own rule, as the letter says.
- **Old camps' sites** (`Camps/CampGround.cs`, pure `CampGroundMath.cs`). A camp that leaves constructions standing,
  nobody's, leaves a site (`CampGrounds.Left`, from `Finish`): its layout as it was (the beds' places too), a name ("the old
  camp by the water", "in the trees", "under the rocks", else "the old camp of the woodcutters", with the way it lies from
  the colony when another has the same name), and who held it (people, kind, days, and left, driven off by whom, or sent
  on by the colony), the newest six of each; six sites a home. A new camp takes one over (`Choose`: the level's reuse
  chance, 0.5 to 0.8; a kind that pitches anywhere and leaves its constructions standing; `Worth`: fire pit or shelter
  standing, four in ten of its constructions, beds' places for the kind's fewest, nothing the colony's, nothing of the
  colony's near, no camp near; the people who held it before three times as likely), as many as its beds take
  (`People`). Arriving, they take over what stands (`TakeOver`: the game's own buildings, their faction set, in their
  group's keeping; mended by their own mend work), build anew what is missing of its shelter, fire, windbreak, lights and
  table, a bed in each place (their own kind's where it fits), and say what they took over. Nothing is carried for what
  stands. A site is let go once nothing of it stands, the colony claims it with the game's own claim (told once), or
  builds up to it; or it stands for camps to come back to.
- **Contested spots**: two peoples held it or someone was driven off (`Contested`). A band against a camp on a contested
  site is likelier and is likelier of a people that held it ("a claim", its words); one that took it from a camp holds it
  half a day and goes, and goes into its history. Two for one site (`TogetherChance`: never at Rare, 0.05 Usual, 0.12
  Many, 0.18 Crowded, half again contested), an hour to three after the first moves in: at war, a band of the second
  people comes against it (warned and shown as any band); else, with room for another camp, the second camps elsewhere,
  its leader saying why as they arrive, the first camp's message telling it.
- **World page**: a card for each camp (with the site it holds and a band against it), then the line on why no other has
  come or that one could, the room at the level, the diary, and the old sites with their history.
- **Dev actions** ("Rimfolk"): another camp here now beside those here; a band against a camp now (any camp, any people
  that may); leave an old camp's site here now (a kind's layout, its constructions standing nobody's); a rival to an old
  site (held: a band for it; free: a camp moves in and a second party comes); the camps, sites and bands to the log.
- **Saved**: `CampHome.camps`, `campRaids`, `grounds` (and each site's plans and holders, each band's fighters and
  helpers), the camp's site, fated hour, guard and rival (`Camp.ExposeCrowd`), a plan's `reuse`; modelled in
  `Tools/save_estimate.py`. No new Sched slot: bands are watched on the camps' quarter hour, the fated hour on the camp's.
- **Not done**: no harm kind (the band is a fight of the game's own, told to the storyteller when it is the colony's
  enemy; colonists fight only when sent); no inspect line on the map (the World page carries it); the Banner's squad
  (Peoples/) still waits for no camp at all.

### A beast is no reason to go: real attacks only (the player's report, 10 November 2026; released 0.206.2)

The player's words: "camps packed up after an animal taking revenge after being attacked, animal and other more
arbitrary attacks should not get the camp to leave".

**The cause.** A camp read danger as the game's own "any hostile threat to the colony on the map" (`MapFacts.ThreatOn`,
`GenHostility.AnyHostileActiveThreatToPlayer`). A wild beast the camp's hunters shot at turns manhunter for revenge
(`Pawn_MindState.Notify_DamageTaken`), and a manhunter is a threat to the colony, so the next hour `CampLife.Ends` took
it for a raid: unless armed campers stood within 22 cells of it, `Leave("raid", true)`, and they fled at once ("With
raiders about ... they wanted no part in the colony's fight"). A packing camp went the same way, and a manhunter pack,
an insect or a predator about the colony did the same to every camp on the land. Beside it, the group's own trigger
(`Trigger_PawnHarmed` with the colony as the instigator's faction) scattered a camp on any harm the colony did, a
colonist's shot at a manhunter that struck a camper included.

- **The rule** (`Camps/CampHarmMath.cs`, pure, `CampHarmTests`): who did it, from what the game knows (`CampHarmFacts`:
  something did it, the colony's, the game's own crossfire rule, out of their mind, a beast, an insect, of no people, of
  the hives, at war with the camp's people, at war with the colony). `By` names it: an accident (nobody did it), the
  colony meaning it, a stray of the colony's (a shot meant for an enemy of both, as `Faction.IsMutuallyHostileCrossfire`
  has it, or a colonist or camper out of their mind, as the game's own goodwill rule has it), raiders, the camp's own
  foes, a beast (wild, of the hives, or out of its mind: hunting, manhunting, taking revenge; the colony's own beast gone
  manhunter too), an insect (wild or of a hive), or other (a wild man, someone of a people at peace with both). Real
  (`RealAttack`): the colony meaning it, raiders, foes. The group scatters at once (`Scatters`) only for the colony
  meaning it; raiders and foes are read by the camp each hour as before (defend their fire, or go).
- **The group** (`Trigger_CampHarmed`, `Camps/CampHarm.cs`): the game's own harm signals (`Trigger_PawnHarmed.SignalIsHarm`),
  the instigator, the one hurt and what was aimed at, asked of `Scatters`. It stands where the old trigger stood in
  `LordJob_Camp` and in the war party's group (`WarCamp.cs`), so saved groups keep their triggers' places. Back from a
  fight once no real danger is left (`CampHarm.RealThreatOn`).
- **The hour** (`CampLife.Ends`): danger is `CampHarm.RealThreatOn` (the game's threat test first, then each active
  threat through the rule); a camp defends its fire only against real attackers near (`EnemyNear`); packing goes on with
  a beast about; a band's check (`CampRaids.OnlyBandsOn`) counts no beast as another danger.
- **Fought off, kept clear of, and the camp stays** (`Camp.Fend`, every 250 ticks while a threat is on the land, one of
  them is attacked in melee, or they are already at it): the nearest beast, insect or wild man hostile to them within 22
  cells of their fire or 9 of one of them (`CampHarm.Menace`, `FendOff`). Those who fight (`Fights`: grown, able to
  fight, armed) stand by their fire on the guard toil (the game's defend duty, 16 cells, as against a band); one
  message says so ("A {THING} has come at the camp ... who can fight stand by their fire to drive it off, and the rest
  keep clear of it"). The rest run from it with the game's own flight when it comes within 9 cells (`Runs`,
  `FleeUtility.FleeJob`, 14 cells). Once none is near and no real danger is on, back to their day (`StopFending`, the
  guard's at-ease memo); the guard's own 14 hours let it go too. A hunter keeps after the beast they hunt, as the game
  has it, and anyone it reaches fights back (the game's melee reaction). What it does to them shows as the game shows it.
- **Worry**: the only rule that already weighed harm, settled neighbours losing one of theirs (`Camp.HoldingLosses`: 15
  unease, maybe grief and moving on), stays as it was. No new rule was added.
- **Saved**: `Camp.fending` (a value, `ExposeHarm`). No new collection, no new Sched slot.
- **Not run here**: the beast's revenge and the camp's stand at its fire; a camper struck by the colony's shot at a
  manhunter staying put.

### Camps in the coldest winter: winter folk (the player's request, 10 November 2026; released 0.207.0)

The player's words: "i haven't had any camps probably becauser it was just freezing cold all the time, i'd like a
handful of camp events that can also come in the coldest winter".

**What kept them away.** Three gates, all on the cold side. The day's try was put off by the hour and then shut while it
was below -30 °C outside (`CampWeatherMath.TooExtremeToCome`, the blocker "weather"), whatever the people could wear. On
milder days a camp came only if every one of them, dressed in layers bought within a plain cloth parka's worth and a
half, would be safe (the game's own range, ten degrees past comfortable) through the stay's coldest hour less three
degrees, over four to ten days of a winter: a cloth parka and a tuque reach about -44 °C, so a run of hard nights shut it.
And a camp that stood packed up below -35 °C (`TooExtremeToStay`). The two seasonal kinds that come in winter (the
herders' grazing, the league's winter quarters) come only from Rimfolk's peoples of that calling.

- **Winter folk** (`CampKindDef.winter`): the flat floor of the cold is not theirs (`CampWeatherMath.TooExtremeToCome(temp,
  true)`, `TooExtremeToStay(temp, true)`: the heat is the same for everyone). Whether they come is the game's own limit
  for each of them as they are dressed (`WouldStop` over the stay's coldest night, as for every camp), and they pack up
  only when the cold starts to hurt most of them (`Exposed`, `PackUp`). Every other kind keeps its gates exactly as
  they were: below -30 °C they stay away, and the same game limit holds for them. The blocker lets a day past the floor
  stay open only while a winter kind fits the weather (`k.winter && k.FitsWeather(map)`). The two kinds that were winter
  camps already, the herders' winter grazing and the league's winter quarters (Peoples/), are winter folk too, in the
  same winter clothes.
- **Cold enough** (`CampKindDef.coldBelow`, `CampWeatherMath.ColdEnough`): a winter kind comes only while the coming week's
  warmest hour (`CampWeather.Usual`, the stay range over seven days, worked out once an hour) stays below its mark; the
  caravan only while snow falls (`inSnow`, `CampLand.SnowNow`). `CampKindDef.FitsWeather` holds the floor, the snow and
  the mark, and every way a camp comes asks it: a new camp (`Prepare`), a camp coming back (`CampReturns.Pick`) and a
  rival party (`CampRaid`).
- **Their winter clothes** (`CampKindDef.wearSet`, a `CampWearDef`, `Rimfolk_CampWear_Winter`; or `wears` of a kind's own;
  `CampWeather.WearOwn`): put on first whenever the stay is colder than they are comfortable in, each entry for their
  people's age, the first def they can wear (their size, age and shape), of the first material listed that it takes;
  what can't be worn with it comes off. Their own gear, so neither the price cap nor the tribes' rule on furs holds them
  back; anything still short is made up as for any camp. The letter says what they wear.
  | Age | Coat | Also |
  |---|---|---|
  | tribal | Vanilla Apparel Expanded's pelt coat, else a parka, of heavy fur, bearskin, wolfskin, sealskin (Odyssey) or foxfur | VFE Tribals' heavy tribalwear; Ideology's tailcap or broadwrap |
  | medieval | a parka of muffalo, sheep or alpaca wool | VFE Medieval 2's mantle; Vanilla Christmas Expanded's warm hat, else a tuque; Vanilla Apparel Expanded's boots |
  | industrial | Vanilla Christmas Expanded's warm jacket, else a wool parka | the warm hat or tuque, boots, Vanilla Apparel Expanded's scarf and gloves |
  | spacer | a parka of synthread or devilstrand | the same |
  A child gets the game's kid parka (Biotech). All from the active rows of `docs/player-mods/apparel.tsv`, by `MayRequire`.
- **The five kinds** (`Defs/CampDefs/Rimfolk_CampKinds_Winter.xml`), each with a fire, wood stacked by it and kept
  burning (the camp's upkeep), a shelter for the cold (a hut, tents, or beds drawn in round the fire behind a windbreak,
  as the layout does for frosty nights), its people's own words by their age, three asks, good turns and a story:
  | Kind | Comes | Lives | Asks |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | ice fishers (a family) | frozen water with fish under it (Odyssey's thin ice, fishing open to the colony), the week below 2 °C | a hut on the shore; cut a hole in the ice and fish through it by day; mend lines by the fire; a dog | buy their catch at the gate, send a colonist out on the ice with them (Animals), an evening at their fire |
  | fur trappers (tribal to industrial) | below 8 °C | a hut; hunt, stretch pelts at the butchering spot, furs laid out; a dog and a pack beast | a bundle of furs, a colonist on the trapline, a hot supper for a pelt (they ask) |
  | a snowbound caravan | while snow falls, below 5 °C, for a day and a half to three | tents, the trader's stall, pack beasts at the picket with hay, bales carried to the stall; a dog | the colony's roof on a stormy night (they ask), their road stores, an evening at their fire |
  | herd followers | a wild herd on the land, below 5 °C | beds round the fire behind a windbreak; hunt the herd, dress the kills, ready their gear; dogs | a colonist after the herd with them, their hides, cooking for meat (they ask) |
  | pilgrims of the long night | winter, below 8 °C | beds round the fire behind a windbreak, a vigil by it; a pack beast | a coat for their eldest, keeping the long night with them, the colony's roof on a stormy night (they ask); a blessing; a carved sun left at the gate after a good stay |
- **Ice fishing** (`Camps/CampWinter.cs`): need `ice` (`CampLand.IceTargets`: ice over a water body with fish, well clear of
  the colony; the water body keeps its frozen cells, as the game's own `GetWaterBodyType` reads the water under the
  ice), work `icefish` (`Camp.IceFishJob`: a cell of ice to kneel on and beside it the hole, an open hole that hasn't
  frozen over first, within 30 cells, clear of the colony and its zones; open water when no ice is left). The job
  (`Rimfolk_CampIceFish`, the Odyssey fishing effect) cuts the hole and keeps it open while they fish
  (`CampLand.WorkTick`: the game's own `RemoveTempTerrain`, every second); the catch is the game's own from the water
  under it (`Fished(..., ice)`), into their stash. The game's freezing closes the hole again (below -7 °C, ice all round).
- **A night under the colony's roof** for any kind with a "shelter" request of its own (`Camp.Shelters`), not the
  watchers alone: the stormy evening's letter, the beds lent, given back in the morning and on leaving.
- **Words**: a camp's lines can ask for `[snow]` (snow falling), `[blizzard]` (hard snow) and `[ice]` (water frozen
  somewhere on the land; `CampLand.IceOn`, read once an hour); the league's winter lines tagged `[snow]` can now be
  picked. Facts tags `them:camp:IceFishers`, `Trappers`, `SnowboundCaravan`, `HerdFollowers`, `WinterPilgrims`.
- **Saved**: nothing new (the hole is the map's own terrain; the shelter's day was saved already).
- **Not run here**: any winter camp on a map; the clothes on each age's people and how far they carry them; the hole
  cut and kept open, the catch through it, and the hole freezing over again; the caravan's night in the colony.

## Harm from everyday life

The player's harm rule (3 November 2026) lets Rimfolk hurt its people when it is flavourful or makes the game more
interesting, at the game's own rate, always from something on the map, and shown. The harm review
(`docs/harm-review-proposals.md`) proposed 94 ways for its systems to go badly; the player picked "my top ten, then more"
on 6 November 2026. Every one of them goes through one service, `Harm/Harm.cs` (pure part `Harm/HarmMath.cs`, tested in
`Tools/Tests/HarmTests.cs`), which keeps the review's shared rules. The first part built the service and the three hurts
of work (1.2.1, 1.2.2, 3.2.1, below); the other seven of the top ten are built on it.

### The shared rules

- **One setting, leaning with the storyteller.** "Hurts from everyday life" (How hard, `everydayHurts`, 0 to 200%,
  100 by default; the light-touch preset sets 50%) multiplies every rate. It leans with the storyteller's own numbers
  (`HarmMath.Lean`): the geometric mean of a threat term (0.35 at no threats, 1 at the usual 100%, up to 1.25 at twice
  it) and a disease term (one over the disease interval, between a half and 1.25; diseases off count as a half). A
  game with no threats and diseases half as often comes to about two fifths, the hardest about a quarter more. `Harm.Scale` is the two together.
- **The shared cap** (`HarmMath.Bar`, `Harm.May`): at most one Rimfolk-made hurt per colonist in three days (the last
  one's tick saved in `HarmBook.lastHurt`, by thingIDNumber, pruned past three days), and none while downed, in a sickbed
  or in need of one (`Harm.Sickbed`: in a medical bed or resting, bleeding, or ill with something that can kill; a small
  thing still to be tended, a strained back or last week's cut, is not a sickbed), pregnant, or already fighting (drafted, a social fight or a rage, at an
  attack, hurt or attacking within the hour). Babies never; children only `HurtClass.Mild` (a scrape, a cold), never an
  injury, a bout or a fight.
- **Nothing kills outright.** A wound lands only on a hand, an arm, a foot, a leg or the torso (a crack on one of their
  bones), never a vital part, the head or the neck, and never takes more than the part has left but one point
  (`HarmMath.SafeSeverity`). The game's own fights and illnesses still may, as they always could.
- **The game's own hurts.** A wound is the game's own injury (`Bruise`, `Cut`, `Burn`, `Crush`, `Crack`, `Scratch`), sized
  by the body's own damage factor (the tough take half), shown as the game shows a hit (the red flash, blood for a cut or a
  crush, a puff of smoke for a burn), then bled, tended, infected and scarred by the game as any wound. Ailments are
  Rimfolk's own (`Ailments/`); fights the game's social fight.
- **Named before the choice.** Where a choice brings the risk, its card says so in words, never numbers: a decree's card
  and letter carry `Harm.DecreeLine` (`DecreeDef.hurts`).
- **Each under its own system.** The drills' bouts need "Answers play out on the map"; working through it needs the
  everyday ailments; the setting at nothing stops all of them. No mood is added: being hurt brings the game's pain and the
  ailment's own mood, nothing on top.

### The service, for the next builders

`Harm` (static) in `Harm/Harm.cs`:

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| `Harm.On`, `Harm.Setting`, `Harm.Lean`, `Harm.Scale` | the setting above nothing; its value; the storyteller's lean; the two together |
| `Harm.PassOf(kind)`, `Harm.ScaleFor(kind)` | a kind's pass within the shared budget now (below); the scale times it, for a chance the game works out itself |
| `Harm.Chance(kind, baseChance)`, `Harm.Roll(kind, baseChance)` | a kind's base rate after the scale and its pass, and one roll of it (no cap) |
| `Harm.Roll(pawn, kind, baseChance, cls)` | the cap for that pawn and class, then the kind's roll |
| `Harm.May(pawn, cls)`, `Harm.Bar(pawn, cls)` | whether the cap lets them take a hurt of that class now, and if not why (`HurtBar`) |
| `Harm.Injure(pawn, wound, where, low, high, kind, cls)` | one of the game's wounds (`HurtKind`) on a part (`HurtWhere`), sized low to high, under the cap; returns it or null |
| `Harm.Ail(pawn, hediffDef, severity, kind, cls, replaces)` | a hediff (an ailment, the game's flu) under the cap, optionally in place of another; returns it or null |
| `Harm.Fight(a, b, kind)` | the game's social fight between two grown-ups the cap lets fight, recorded for both |
| `Harm.Note(pawn, kind)` | a hurt that came another way (a bout's hard blow, a brawl), counted for the cap (`kind` null: the cap only) |
| `Harm.SystemOn(system)`, `Harm.BudgetReport()` | whether a kind's system is on in this game; the budget for the dev tools |
| `Harm.DaysSince(pawn)`, `Harm.Pregnant(pawn)`, `Harm.Fighting(pawn, now)` | the cap's parts, for a caller's own checks |
| `Harm.DecreeLine(decreeDef)` | the decree's line for its card and letter, or null |

`HurtClass`: `Mild` (children may), `Injury`, `Bout`, `Fight` (grown-ups only). Every roll and every hurt names its
kind (`HarmKinds`, below). The caller rolls its own base rate
through `Harm.Roll`, gives the hurt through `Injure`, `Ail` or `Fight` (each checks the cap again and records it), says
it on the map (a bubble through `Speech.Say` or `CouncilGameComponent.Speak`, one sentence) and tells it through
`Tell.Message` at `Importance.Important` (harm is never held back) in two wordings or more (`TextVariants.Vary`). A hurt the caller can't give through the service (the outsiders' practice
bout, a feast's wrestling and sour night) is counted with `Harm.Note`; the feasts read `Harm.Scale` and `Harm.May` through
`Feasts.HarmScale` and `Feasts.MayBeHurt`.

`HarmBook` (a game component) holds the saved part (`lastHurt`; `drillDay`, a home's last evening drill; `kindLast`, the
budget's memory; `waiting`, parts 4 and 5's hurts still to come; `turning` and `calm`, the hunts' game) and runs the hour (Sched
`RareHarm` 67): one tenth of the colonists each 250 ticks, the first slice also the colony's part.

### The shared budget (7 November 2026)

The player asked whether more kinds of hurt make colonists hurt more often or only more variously, and chose: "yes, a
shared budget please". Rimfolk's everyday hurts, every one that goes through the service (the beasts' stampede, the
feasts', the schemes' and the pilgrims' included), together stay at what the kinds built before the budget came to, and
new kinds take turns within it instead of adding to it. The pure rules are `Harm/HarmBudgetMath.cs` (`HarmBudgetTests`);
the game's side is `Harm.PassOf`.

- **Each kind registered once** (`HarmKinds`): a key (saved), a label, the system it sits under (`Harm.SystemOn`: its
  setting, and for a soft integration its mod) and its base rate (hurts per colonist-year in an average colony of six at
  100% and the usual storyteller, coming on its own, before the cap: the balance model measures it). The 18 kinds built
  before the budget are its founding ones; harm part 4's and part 5's are not (the guest's night is two kinds, Rimfolk's
  visitors and Hospitality's guests, so a game without Hospitality keeps none of the budget for it).
- **The budget** is the founding kinds that are on, their base rates together (about 0.46 a colonist-year).
- **The pass**: a kind's chance is its base rate times the setting and the storyteller's lean (as before) times its
  pass, its variety times the budget over the kinds on weighed by their variety (`HarmBudgetMath.Passes`). So the kinds'
  base rates times their passes always come to the budget: with only the founding kinds on and none come lately, every
  pass is 1 (the hurts as they were); with all of part 4 on, each passes at about half its rate. No kind passes at more
  than twice its own rate.
- **Variety** (`HarmBudgetMath.Variety`): a kind that has just hurt someone weighs a quarter of its rate, back to all of
  it evenly over thirty days (two quadrums), so it passes less often for a while and the others a little more; the mix
  varies instead of the commonest kind coming again and again. Its memory is `HarmBook.kindLast` (a kind's last tick,
  pruned past thirty days: a handful of entries).
- **The same as before in everything else.** The pass knows nothing of the setting or the storyteller, so "Hurts from
  everyday life" and the lean scale every kind exactly as they did; the cap and its exclusions (downed, a sickbed,
  pregnant, fighting, babies never, children only the mildest) are untouched, and nothing here kills outright. A system
  switched off takes its kinds out of the budget, leaving the rest as they would be without it. Prevention still counts:
  a well-run colony meets fewer of the new kinds and its total falls a little below its old one, a neglectful one rises a
  little (the rates below).
- **One roll an occasion.** The pass multiplies the chance of the occasion's hurt, once: a hunt's head that can turn takes
  its turn when the hunt marks it (`HuntsBite.Marked`; not up, it stays calm under its hunters, `HarmBook.calm`), not on
  each shot, so the budget's share is the hunt's; the ailments of the land and the work, which never had the setting's
  scale, take the pass alone (`AilmentTracker.Lean`).
- **A later kind plugs in** with one line in `HarmKinds` (its key, label, system and base rate from the balance model,
  `founding` false, added to `All`), a case in `Harm.SystemOn` if its system is new, its rolls and hurts naming it, and its
  source in the balance model's harm mode (`Tools/Balance/HarmSim.cs`, `PartFourDay` shows the pattern). The budget shares
  itself among however many kinds are on (100 now the review is built, each at about 31% of its own rate: the later kinds
  are smaller on the whole than the first).
  The model prints each kind's measured base rate beside the registry's, flagging any a quarter off.

### Drills that bruise (1.2.1, decrees)

With "Answers play out on the map" on, the drills decree (`hurts` Drills) pairs everyone of the colony who can fight into
practice bouts in the open each evening between five and eight (`DrillBouts.cs`): grown-ups only, free and not pressed
(`PlayOuts.CanJoin`, `Interruptible`, not `NeedsPress`), the yard or the open middle of the colony (`PlaySpots.OpenCell`),
two places side by side for each pair, clear of the others. The militia drills (`hurts` Muster) call one pair, three
evenings in four (`HarmMath.MusterEvening`). Not in bad weather or danger; once a day at a home (`HarmBook.drillDay`).
The first of the pairs calls it (`Rimfolk_Pool_DrillCall`, by age), each pair walks to its places (`JobDriver_DrillBout`,
the job `Rimfolk_DrillBout`), a word to begin (`Rimfolk_Pool_DrillBegin`) and six pulled swings each, the game's lunge and
sound, no harm. One bout in 25 (`HarmMath.DrillBlowChance`, the outsiders' sparring rate; a marshal in office halves it)
has one blow land for real, decided at the start on one of the pair the cap lets take a bout: a bruise or a cut of 6 to 9
by the colony's means (sticks and wrestling: a bruise; blunted blades and shields, the bayonet drill: a bruise or a cut on
an arm; stun batons and training rounds: a burn on the torso; `DrillBouts.BlowOf`). The hurt one says so
(`Rimfolk_Pool_DrillHit`), the other says sorry (`Rimfolk_Pool_DrillSorry`), the news tells it (`CC_Harm_DrillBlow`,
`CC_Harm_MusterBlow`, a NegativeHealthEvent), and the game's doctor tends it. A bout done with nobody hurt ends with a
word (`Rimfolk_Pool_DrillEnd`). Either one leaving ends it for both; danger ends it at once. The decree's hourly practice
goes on as before. About one real injury per five-day drills decree in a colony of ten, the militia about half that
(`HarmMath.DrillBlowsPerDecree`). Since the player's decision 13 (6 November 2026) the drills are one decree in the
colony's age's form: militia drills for a tribal or medieval colony, drills for an industrial or spacer one (see
"Decrees that mean distinct things"); each keeps its own bouts and risk lines.

### Tired hands (1.2.2, decrees)

Under long hours (any work), a harvest push (`hurtsAt` Field) or a building season (`hurtsAt` Heavy), each with `hurts`
TiredHands, the hourly look counts the hours each colonist is found at the work the decree drives (`HarmMath.WorkOf`: the
stove and the forge, the bench, building and mining, hauling, the field). From the sixth hour in a day, a long day, the first
hour they're found right at it (carrying the load, or standing at the bench, the stove, the wall or the plants rather
than walking to them, so the slip shows where the words put it) has one roll: one in 150 (`TiredHandsChance`, the everyday work ailments' rate), twice below 30% rest, once more for
a second work decree driving it, half for the tough, half in a spacer colony. A slip is one of the game's wounds of 3 to 6
(5 to 8 in a spacer colony) by the work and the colony's means (`HarmMath.WorkSlip`): a cut at the bench, a crushed hand
at an industrial colony's machine, a fabricator's burn; a burn at the stove, fire pit or forge; a crushed foot under a
stone or a crate (a hand at a machine); a load dropped on a foot; a sickle's cut. The job stops, a load drops at their
feet, a line is said (`Rimfolk_Pool_WorkSlip`, tagged by work and wound), the news tells it (`CC_Harm_Slip_<work>`), and
the hurt one goes to the doctor as the game sends anyone with a wound to tend. The review's "one or two per decree in a
colony of ten" was a miscount against its own anchor: at one in 150 long days, a five-day decree in a colony of ten brings
about a third of a slip when everyone sleeps, about twice that when nobody does (`TiredHandsPerDecree`). The anchored rate
was kept.

### Decrees that mean distinct things (the player's decision 13, 6 November 2026)

In the player's save drills and militia drills were declared the same day and both ran ("militia drills (2 times) ...
and drills" in the annals); the review named more overlapping pairs. Each was looked at for what it does
(`DecreeMath`, pure):

- **One idea, one decree, in the form of the moment.** Where two decrees are one idea, only the form it takes now is
  listed (`DecreeWork.FormNow`, `HiddenNow`): the drills by the colony's age (militia drills, the muster of a tribe or a
  village, for a tribal or medieval colony; drills, all day, for an industrial or spacer one), rationing by the moment
  (famine bread, smaller portions and a share for the hungry, while a famine or a drought lies over the region and the
  colony's own stores aren't low; plain rationing otherwise). A form in force stays itself until it ends, and the page
  shows it.
- **Overlapping pairs don't run together.** Festival days and a feast day (both celebrations that raise standards),
  quiet hours and days of rest (both rest and slower work), on guard and a curfew (sleep in shifts, or everyone abed by
  ten): with one in force the other can't be declared, and its card says why (`DecreeMath.Excludes`,
  `CC_Decree_Overlaps`, `DecreeTracker.CannotEnact`). An idea's two forms exclude each other the same way. One faith for
  the colony and every faith its evening (the fourth round, below) are the council's two ways with its faiths, and are
  kept apart the same way.
- **Kept apart.** Rest when ill and quarantine may run together: one heals the sick, the other keeps the well from
  catching it. Austerity (no new wishes) and rationing (food) never overlapped, nor shared meals (talk) and festival
  days (rest and music).
- **Older saves.** A decree in force that is an idea's form not listed now carries on as the listed one for what was
  left of it, never longer than that form runs (`DecreeTracker.CarryOn`, `DecreeMath.CarriedEnd`, the first hour after
  a load): militia drills in an industrial colony become its drills; with both forms in force the listed one goes on and
  the other ends quietly. Rationing's forms only lose a duplicate (famine bread declared for a famine since gone stays
  itself). A petition for a form not listed is let go quietly. The drills' bouts and the militia's muster keep their
  risk lines (`hurts` Drills and Muster, "Drills that bruise").

### Working through it (3.2.1, ailments and health stories)

With the everyday ailments on, a strained back or a sprained ankle that is untended and out of bed counts its hours of
heavy work (hauling, building, mining) each day. From the fourth hour in a day, the first hour they're found right at it
has one roll for that ailment (once each, in session memory): one in ten. Not while the rest-when-ill decree holds. A strained back tears: `Council_Ail_TornBack`
(Rimfolk's own ailment, in the strain's place; 3 to 5 weeks, sharper pain, half the carrying, half as long in bed,
tending helps; its own mood in place of the strain's, a hint with the strains). A sprained ankle gives: a fall, a bruise
of 3 to 5 on the leg, or a crack of 2 to 4 on its bone one time in three; the sprain stays. Either way the load drops,
they sit down hard for a few seconds (the game's wait), say so (`Rimfolk_Pool_WorkedThrough`), a doctor of the colony
within talking range has a word (`Rimfolk_Pool_DoctorsWord`), and the news tells it with the ailment's doctor's note
(`CC_Harm_TornBack`, `CC_Harm_AnkleFall`, `CC_Harm_AnkleCrack`). Prevent it with bed rest, the work tab, the rest-when-ill
decree or a tending.

### Ailments of the land, the work and the age (the player's request, 6 November 2026)

Eight everyday ailments and three serious illnesses, each from something the hourly look finds on the map
(`AilmentChecks.Sample`, which holds its counted causes as the bits of a long now; the pure rules in
`Ailments/AilmentCauseMath.cs`, tested in `Tools/Tests/AilmentLandTests.cs`), each the game's own hediff with stages and
tending, the serious ones its immunity race with a hidden incubation (`Rimfolk_Hediffs_Ailments_Land.xml`,
`Rimfolk_Hediffs_Illnesses_Land.xml`; moods, hints and lines in the files of the same name).

| Ailment (names by age) | Cause on the map | Course | Prevention | Rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Swimmer's itch (pond itch) | an hour's swim (the game's `GoSwimming`) in still water: a lake, a pond, a marsh, not a river or the sea | 2 to 4 days, a wash shortens it | swim in the river | 4% a day, children half again |
| Trench foot (marsh foot) | 4 hours outdoors in water, marsh or mud below 10 °C, the line moved by their own cold shift | 1 to 2 weeks, less in bed, tending helps | a bridge or path over the wet, short shifts | 1.5% a day |
| Sandfly fever (three-day fever) | 2 hours outdoors in an arid land from 18:00 to 5:00 at 20 °C or more | about 3 days whatever is done | indoors after dusk | 3% a day, not again within 30 days |
| Jungle rot | a cut, scratch, stab or bite untended for 6 hours in a wet land at 25 °C or more outside | about two weeks, a few days tended, industrial best | wounds tended the same day | 8% a day with such a wound |
| Rabbit fever (hunter's fever) | 2 hours butchering a small wild animal (body 0.5 or less) | about a week, a few days tended, industrial best | a skilled butcher (Cooking) | 1.2% a day |
| Metal fume fever (founder's ague) | 4 hours smithing or smelting in a closed room of 60 cells or fewer | 1 to 2 days, less in bed | a big or open smithy | 2.5% a day |
| Stump sores | 8 hours walking or at heavy or bench work on a limb of the old kinds (weaker than natural, made before the spacer age) | 3 to 6 days, much less in bed | a lighter day after a long one | 3% a day |
| Mechanite fever (machine fever) | a part or implant of the spacer age put in while one of the colony, or a first dose of luciferium | 1 to 3 days, less in bed | none: it's the mechanites | 1 in 4, once a part |
