  once it carries nothing. One 250-tick pass (`Sched.RareHauling`, only while someone carries) and a per-tick look only
  while a spot waits to be looked at again.
- **Not checked here**: none of it could be run in the game. The riskiest parts are the take-over from a save (the
  standalone's XML read without the mod), the pre-init action on every `StartCarryThing` (it returns at once for any
  other job), the run's job from the inventory (the game's own support for it, not seen with frames), the cover for the
  other builders (it may hold them back a while when a runner is stuck: an hour at most), and the hand-over to Pick Up
  And Haul (its comp read by name).

### Everything else work makes (the player's request, 7 November 2026)

"They should always take any 'produced' item or resource into their inventory when they have space, to later store
it, for any possible item creating or harvesting interaction in the game and mods" (explicit: no proposal round). The
code is `Hauling/WorkProducts.cs` and its hooks `Hauling/WorkProductPatches.cs`; the pure rules are in `HaulMath.cs`
("Everything else work makes", `HaulTests`). Delivery is harvest and haul's own: the same kind of work by skill or by
work giver, full and worth a trip, the longest hold, before needs, never instead of rest, Pick Up And Haul's unloading.

- **Bills** (`WorkProducts.PocketBill`). The game's last toil of a bill (`Toils_Recipe.FinishRecipeAndStartStoringProduct`)
  makes the products (`GenRecipe.MakeRecipeProducts`), counts them for the worker's records
  (`RecordsUtility.Notify_BillDone`) and then places them by the bill's store mode: drop on floor near the worker, or
  the first product in the hands to the best stockpile or the picked one (`HaulAIUtility.HaulToCellStorageJob`) and the
  rest near the worker, or on the floor when no cell takes it. Rimfolk wraps that toil's init action to know the
  worker is finishing (`WorkProducts.finishing`), and in a postfix on `Notify_BillDone` (last, so other mods counting
  see every product) takes the products off the list before the game places them: only for a bill taking them to a
  stockpile (`HaulMath.BillPockets`: best or picked; never drop on floor, a mod's own store mode, a bill the player
  ordered, surgery (`Bill_Medical`) or a building's own production (`Bill_Autonomous`, the mech gestators), nor a project
  of 10,000 work or more, whose first product the game names in a tale), only kinds that may go in, only what a store
  cell takes (in the picked stockpile for that mode), and only as many as fit; a partly fitting stack is split. The game
  then places or carries the rest its own way, so "too heavy to carry" is as before. The quests that count what is made
  (`QuestManager.Notify_ThingsProduced`) are told of what went in, before it goes in (merged into a stack already
  carried, the piece is gone). A picked stockpile is remembered by one of its cells per kind (`HaulLoad.into`); the
  delivery finds a cell in that slot group or its storage group (`Carrying.StoreCellFor`), else the best storage (where
  the game's haulers would take it anyway), and such a kind never goes through Pick Up And Haul's unloading, which knows
  only the best. A "do until" bill would make more while the products ride in a pocket (the game counts the hands,
  `RecipeWorkerCounter.GetCarriedCount`, not inventories): postfixes on `RecipeWorkerCounter.CountProducts` and the stone
  block and butchering counters add what pawns owe to storage of it (`WorkProducts.CarriedFor`, by the bill's own
  `CountValidThing`; with "count equipped" the game counts inventories itself; with a stockpile to count in, only what
  goes there).
- **Everything else, one generic catch** (no hook per mod). Three hooks set whose job runs a toil or a tick
  (`JobDriver.TryActuallyStartNextToil`, `DriverTick`, `DriverTickInterval`: prefixes and finalizers that put the one
  before back; `[ThreadStatic]`, so other threads see none). While one is set, an item made (`ThingMaker.MakeThing`) or
  dropped out of a building's container (`GenDrop.TryDropSpawn`, the egg box's eggs) is noted for that job; a part split
  off a stack (`Thing.SplitOff`: a hauler's handful) and anything dropped out of a pawn's hands or inventory, a corpse or
  anything else is never one. Only for a work job (a work giver gave it), not ordered, of a pawn that carries, and not a
  job one of the sources of their own covers (plants and sowing, mining, the deep drill, shearing and milking, taking
  down and floors, Odyssey's fishing, bills, Rimfolk's delivery, Pick Up And Haul's unloading) nor building work. Two
  moments take it: the carry step (the material run's hook on `Toils_Haul.StartCarryThing` adds a pre-init action)
  about to put such a thing in the hands while one of the job's targets is a storage cell takes it into the inventory
  instead, whole or not at all, and ends the job there (`EndJobWith(Succeeded)`: the preInit loop stops when the toils
  are cleared); and the job's end (a prefix on `Pawn_JobTracker.CleanupCurrentJob`, before the game drops what the hands
  hold) takes what still lies loose within 4 cells of the pawn and some storage takes, as far as it fits, the first that
  doesn't fit carried in the hands on the delivery. Not while drafted, downed or in a mental state, nor for a job that
  errored. At most 40 things a job; the note goes with the job.
- **Families and settings** (What's on, Carrying and hauling; each needs "Pawns carry what their work drops"):
  `haulBills` (bills), `haulBuildings` (a job whose first target is a building: the fermenting barrel, the egg box,
  Anomaly's bioferrite harvester and the entity on its holding platform, the mods' barrels, presses, processors,
  beehouses and apiaries), `haulOtherWork` (any other work job: a skull extracted for Ideology, the mods' work; taking
  a mechanoid apart and removing a mechlink are orders, so they go as before), and a mod's fishing job by its name
  (`HaulMath.FishingName`) under the existing `haulFishing`.
- **What stays where it is** (`WorkProducts.PocketableDef`, `Allowed`): medicine (the doctors' to reach), weapons (Simple
  Sidearms, in the player's list, reads a weapon in the inventory as a sidearm), what dissolves (`CompDissolution`:
  wastepacks), what the weather ruins or hatches (`CompTemperatureRuinable`, `CompHatcher`: fertilized eggs, wort),
  Biotech's xenogerms, genepacks, embryos, ova and mechlinks (used where they lie), corpses, minified things and chunks
  (by their setting). Meals (`HaulMath.MealsToPocket`): all while nobody is hungry, else only past what the hungry need
  and the meals in reach don't cover (a working paste dispenser feeds all); a load with meals is held two hours at most
  (`HaulMath.HoldHours`), and the book's pass sends it at once while someone is hungry and the meals in reach don't feed
  them all (`HaulMath.MealsWanted`). The same work for a load is also the same work giver (`HaulLoad.givers`): emptying
  egg boxes and barrels is hauling work, which no skill names.
- **The player's mods** (`docs/player-mods/`, the raw defs, and the sources read where they were to hand): the Vanilla
  Expanded Framework's item processors (`IP_RemoveProduct`, Vanilla Brewing and Cooking Expanded's barrels and presses,
  VFE Settlers and Classical), its pipe processors (`PS_PickUpProcessor`), Medieval 2's apiary
  (`VFEM2_TakeHoneyOutOfApiary`) and the Processor Framework's emptying (`EmptyProcessor`) make the product, place it
  and carry it to a storage cell with the game's carry step, as the fermenting barrel does; the Processor Framework's
  last product of an emptied processor is left on the ground (its job ends first), and the job's end takes it. VEF's
  draining of a marked tank (`PS_DrainFromMarkedStorage`) and Anomaly's bioferrite extraction leave it beside the pawn.
  Alpha Bees' beehouses, Tabula Rasa's producers, Rimefeller's autoclave, Dubs Bad Hygiene's emptied latrines and septic
  tanks and the other mods' producers are caught the same way if their work makes an item as these do; their code
  wasn't to hand. Vanilla Fishing Expanded's and PokéWorld's fishing go by the fishing switch.
- **Saved**: two lists more in each load (`givers`, `into`, modelled in `Tools/save_estimate.py`), emptied with the load.
  The notes of what a job made aren't saved: a job loaded mid-way goes the game's way. No Sched slot, no new pass.
- **Not checked here**: none of it could be run in the game. The riskiest parts are the three hooks on the job driver's
  hot paths (a prefix and a finalizer each, nothing else), the job ended from the carry step's pre-init action, the
  products taken off the game's list in `Notify_BillDone` (a mod reading the list after it sees fewer), and interplay
  with Common Sense and Gastronomy (a restaurant waits up to two hours for meals in a cook's pocket).

### Reserved slots on shelves, and making room for them (the player's report, 10 November 2026; making room released 0.205.3)

The shelf reserves (`Building/ShelfReserves.cs`, the setting "Reserved slots on shelves", `shelfReserves`, behind the
deeper hooks; Almanac Management, "Reserved slots"): a shelf keeps slots for kinds the player picks (an item, any of a
group, the best of a group at hand), each for a stack of its own, while the colony has some on the map; the other slots
take anything. The pure rules are `Building/ShelfReserveMath.cs` (Tools/Tests `ShelfReserveTests`): `Fill` and `Missing`
(which slots are empty), `MayTakeSlot` (a new stack only while a slot stays free for every empty one waiting), `MoveOut`
(what must go: a kind kept off for now, past its cap, then room for the slots waiting, of what the shelf holds most of,
the smallest first), `SpaceFor` (per stack), `Best`. The game side: `ShelfReserves.State` from `Look` (two seconds at
most, at once when what the shelf holds changes); `Patch_ShelfReserveCell` (`StoreUtility.NoStorageBlockersIn`,
`MayStore`), `Patch_ShelfReserveAccepts` (`Building_Storage.Accepts`: a stack that must go no longer belongs, so haulers
take it to the next place that will have it), `Patch_ShelfReserveHaulCount`, the gizmo and its window and picker.

The player's report: "when i have a reserved slot in a shelf for meals, that slot is however currently being occupied by
something else, i can't send a "haul" command on a meal, since it thinks there are no free slots. it should recognize
that it can free up the reserved slots and then haul the food there". A full shelf's cells are full for the game's store
search, so a forced haul of the waiting kind found no cell ("Cannot haul simple meal x4: No empty, accessible spot
configured to store it"), and a stack marked to move out that no other storage took never left. Fixed both ways
(`Building/ShelfMakeRoom.cs`), behind the same setting and the deeper hooks:

- **On their own** (`Patch_ShelfMakeRoomAuto`, a postfix on `HaulAIUtility.HaulToStorageJob`): when the game's haul
  finds no storage for a stack the reserves mark to move out, and a reserved kind waits for room on that shelf, a hauler
  sets it down on a free cell beside the shelf (the game's own haul aside, `HaulAIUtility.CanHaulAside`). Only as many
  as the shelf is short of: the slots waiting that the usual hauling would fill (some of the kind loose in the home
  area, or in storage below the shelf's priority: `ShelfReserves.Coming`; a kind kept only in storage as good as the
  shelf never comes, so nothing is set down for it), less the free slots and the stacks already on their way out
  (reserved by someone), `ShelfReserveMath.ShortOfRoom`. The usual hauling then brings the waiting kind into the freed
  slot. It never loops: the stack set down isn't put back while it would take the slot kept for the waiting kind
  (`MayStore`, `MayTakeSlot`), and once that kind is in, the shelf is full again. A stack kept off for now or past a cap
  with nowhere to go stays, as before, unless a kind waits for its room.
- **Ordered** (`FloatMenuOptionProvider_RimfolkShelfRoom`, found by the game like every provider): right-clicking a
  stack the game's own haul finds no cell for, with a colonist who hauls, offers "Make room on the shelf and haul simple
  meal x4 there" when a reserved shelf (the best storage first, then the nearest) is full, has an empty slot of that
  kind, allows it and is better storage than where it lies (`ShelfReserveMath.MayMakeRoom`, the game's rule for a haul).
  `Patch_ShelfMakeRoomMenu` (a postfix on `FloatMenuMakerMap.GetOptions`) takes out the game's "Cannot haul X: No empty,
  accessible spot" line for that stack, so the working line stands in its place; a colonist who doesn't haul sees only
  the game's line. Which stack goes (`ShelfReserveMath.RoomFrom`): one the reserves mark to move out (counting the
  ordered kind as waiting when it isn't yet, say it lies outside the home area), the least worth of them; else the stack
  of least worth of no reserved kind; never a stack of a reserved kind the reserves don't mark, so no slot is emptied
  for another; only stacks the colonist can reach and reserve. Taken, two jobs: the stack off the shelf to its best
  other storage (the game's search from unstored, never the same shelf; a container by the game's haul to a container),
  else set down beside the shelf; then the game's `HaulToCell` of the ordered stack into the freed cell, queued next and
  reserved at once with the stack, so nobody fills the cell in between. The order is looked at again when it is taken.
- **The job's words**: `Rimfolk_MakeRoomOnShelf` (`Defs/Misc/Rimfolk_ShelfReserves.xml`), the game's
  `JobDriver_HaulToCell` with its report: "making room on the shelf for the simple meal." (the stack queued to come in)
  or "for meals" (the first kind waiting). No message: the menu's line and the job's report say it.
- Nothing saved, no Sched slot, no new setting. Keys in `Languages/English/Keyed/Rimfolk_Stores.xml`
  (`CC_Shelf_MakeRoomHaul`, `CC_Shelf_MakingRoomFor`, `CC_Shelf_TheKind`); the window's and the setting's explanations
  say it. Tests: `ShelfReserveTests` (`MayMakeRoom`, `RoomFrom`, `ShortOfRoom`, that it never loops, the seams).
- **Not checked here**: none of it could be run in the game: the menu's line in place of the game's (its label matched
  by the game's own words), the queued haul starting after the first job and its reservations held between, the haul
  aside's cell beside a shelf, the stack set down being left alone while the slot waits, and LWM's Deep Storage cells.

## The trade screen (the player's requests, 7 and 8 November 2026)

"I still don't really like the new trade interface, i'm thinking more of a totally redone one by you, not an adjusted
vanilla one. where I can see whether I'm buying/selling above/under market price, what are really good deals both ways,
easier sorting & overview etc." Every trade now opens in Rimfolk's own window (`Trade/TradeWindow.cs`,
`Trade/Window_RimfolkTrade.cs`, the rules in `Trade/TradeWindowMath.cs`), on the game's own deal; the game's screen,
with the 0.150.0 and 0.151.0 parts below, stays one click away.

- **Opening in place of the game's.** Every opener (`JobDriver_TradeWithPawn` for a trader, a visitor or Hospitality's
  guest on the map, `TradeShip.TryOpenComms`, `CaravanArrivalAction_Trade`, `CaravanVisitUtility`, the caravan met on
  the road, transport pods at a town) does `WindowStack.Add(new Dialog_Trade(...))`, and the game's constructor already
  sets the trade up (`TradeSession.SetupWith`, a caravan's `Notify_StartedTrading`). So one prefix on `WindowStack.Add`
  (`Patch_TradeWindowOpen`) swaps the window and keeps the game's: nothing about the trade is made twice. Only the
  game's own class (a mod's subclass is left), only silver (a trade in favor, the Empire's tribute collector, keeps its
  own screen: its honour is its own), never gifts (gifts-only and gift mode stay the game's: a gift has no prices to
  read, and the game's own switch empties the deal anyway). The deeper game hooks and *Rimfolk's own trade window*
  (`tradeWindow`, What's on, Trade screen, on) turn it off.
- **The switch, both ways.** "Game's screen" (top right) takes this window off and adds the very `Dialog_Trade` the
  game made, let through the prefix once; the counts live in the game's `TradeDeal`, so they stay. On the game's screen a
  small button right of its sort menus (where its search box would be; it draws that at the foot) comes back, the
  game's screen taken off with `TryRemove` so its `Close` (which hands a trader's quest over) waits for the trade's end.
  The switch matters for Trade Helper, whose panel is drawn on the game's screen only. "Give gifts" goes to the game's
  screen in its gift mode.
- **Two lists, sell and buy** (since the player's request of 9 November 2026, "Two lists, sell and buy" below): the
  colony's goods to sell and the trader's to buy, side by side where the window has room, else as two tabs. The first
  window was one table with sides (the colony's count and what the trader pays left of the game's own count control,
  what it asks and its count right of it, thirteen columns dropped in a set order when narrow); the player found its
  columns many and its two directions confusing, and the names cut.
- **The game's deal underneath.** Each price is `Tradeable.GetPriceFor` (the price shown is the price paid; nothing is
  priced here), each count is set within the game's `GetMinimumToTransfer` and `GetMaximumToTransfer` by its own
  `CanAdjustTo` and `AdjustTo` (an arrow one, Shift ten, Ctrl a hundred, a double arrow all or none, a number typed;
  each list's control one way, below), with the game's own "won't trade" and Ideology's "won't sell into slavery" in its
  place. Accept is the game's: its question
  when the trader is short of silver ("ConfirmTraderShortFunds", the rest let go as a gift), then `TradeDeal.TryExecute`
  (the negotiator, the ideoligion's word on organs, the goods handed over by pod or into the caravan, the faction told),
  the trade sound and the caravan's inventory. The one step done first here is the game's own check that the colony can
  pay, with its own message, since `TryExecute` flashes the silver of a `Dialog_Trade` it looks up and there is none.
  A caravan's mass, speed, food days, foraging and visibility are the game's calculators drawn by its own strip
  (`CaravanUIUtility.DrawCaravanInfo`), over every good rather than the ones a search shows. On close, as the game's
  screen does, a trader with a quest hands it over; on opening, the game's word about a negotiator who can't talk or
  hear well. So Vanilla Trading Expanded's prices, its contracts and any mod that patches `Tradeable` or `TradeDeal`
  keep working; a mod that patches the game's own count control (`TransferableUIUtility.DoCountAdjustInterface`) works
  on the game's screen, not in the two lists.
- **Two baselines for every price.** The market value a piece (`Tradeable.BaseMarketValue`: the thing's own, with
  quality and hit points) and the price's share of it, in the row's tooltip; and under each price its mark against the
  usual price, the advice's own (`TradeNote.usualSell`/`usualBuy`, the game's 60% and 140% of worth moved by the
  negotiator and difficulty, Vanilla Trading Expanded's market divided out; for people and animals, which the advice
  doesn't read, `TradeAdvice.UsualFor`). Against the value a sale is always under and a purchase over; against the usual
  a better trader shows: green 7% to the good side, orange 7% to the bad, an arrow up or down saying which way. With
  VTE's history, the market now against usual and against the 30 days' average, and the 30 days drawn, on the market
  card beside the row's tooltip.
- **Grades a side at a time** (`TradeWindowMath.Rate`, tested): the price against the usual, 1 as usual and more better
  (a sale's price over it, a purchase's usual over the price); a step of 0.05 up or down for VTE's market reason
  (`TradeMarketMath.Hint`: a sale at a 60-day high or of a falling good, a buy at a low or of a rising one, up; the
  other ends, down) and for the colony's record (better than its best of the last 15 days, up; a tenth worse, down). A
  fifth better is great, 7% good, within 7% fair, worse poor. A purchase the advice doesn't mark worth buying (no need
  and no bargain on a stock it keeps) and a sale of what the colony is short of or keeps all of are held at fair. Three
  bars and a word, so the colour is never the only sign; each list shows its own side's grade ("good"), the tooltip
  why: the market's and the record's reason, the cap, and the advice's own reasons. People aren't graded.
- **Best deals and the summary** on the right: the top five sells and buys graded good or great, each a click from its
  row in its list (the filters cleared if they hide it, its tab shown, the row lit for a moment). Then the deal: what is sold and bought, at market
  value and at what share of it; the net silver as the game counts it; against the usual prices ("about 12% better for
  you"; `DealSums.VsUsual`, the deal at this trader's prices against it at the usual, as a share of the latter); both
  ways by market value; a side short of silver; the old screen's food days at home and VTE's banks; and VTE's warning
  for each good this trade may move (`TradeMarket.ImpactLine`'s own words). Each side's silver now and after the trade at
  the foot right, lit when the game says the silver won't do.
- **Sorting and overview.** Every header but the count's sorts its list on a click and again the other way
  (`TradeWindowMath.Order`: names from A, numbers the highest first, a row without that side last either way, ties by
  name), within each kind; each list's last sort is kept for the session. A search (the game's own widget), a chip for
  each kind this trade has with its count (food, medicine, raw materials, manufactured, weapons, apparel, art and books,
  drugs, animals, people, other; read from the game's def and categories, so every mod's goods find theirs), and "only
  in the deal". What the trader won't deal in goes last, greyed, as on the game's screen. The foot: Fill suggested and
  Clear suggested (the basket's own, `TradeScreen.Fill(null)`), Reset, Accept, Cancel.
- **Never without a trade screen.** If the window can't be made, the game's screen opens; if anything throws while it
  draws (every group and scroll view closed in a `finally`), the error is logged once and the game's screen takes the
  trade over on the same counts. Nothing is saved in the game; the sort is session memory, the lists' layout and tab
  the settings'.
- **The game's screen keeps its parts** (below): the sorts, the marks (which stand down inside Rimfolk's window, where
  the game's own row icons are drawn), the basket's buttons, the readouts and the market card. Trade Helper (its source
  isn't public) draws only there. Hospitality gives its guests a trader kind of its own (`TraderKinds_Guests.xml`), so a
  guest is traded with as any trader on the map, and opens Rimfolk's window unless Hospitality makes a screen of its own
  kind (its code isn't among the player's files, only its defs). Pick Up And Haul's files touch no part of a trade.

### Two lists, sell and buy (the player's request, 9 November 2026)

"i quite like the new trading ui, but i find it still a bit confusing. could buy and sell be split into different tabs
or some other setup? where I have separate lists can can organize it more easy. does that make sense? because now i have
a lot of different columns and i think it could be more clear if the two directions are somehow separate. also the name
of the item doesn't even always fit." The plan told to the player, as built (`Trade/Window_RimfolkTrade.cs`, the rules in
`Trade/TradeWindowMath.cs`):

- **Two lists.** *Ours to sell*: every good the colony has within the trade (`CountHeldBy(Transactor.Colony) > 0`, what
  the trader won't take included and greyed), with what the trader pays; *Theirs to buy*: every good the trader has,
  with what it asks. A good both have is in both, its one count read in each. Side by side, the sell list on the left as
  the colony's side is on the game's screen, where each list has room for all its columns (`TradeWindowMath.SideBySide`:
  586 pixels of rows a list, so a table of 1216: 1920 and 1600 wide in both looks); else two tabs, Sell and Buy. The
  button at the lists' right ("Lists: by width", "side by side", "tabs") opens the player's choice; side by side chosen
  holds wherever the name, the price and the count fit (400 pixels of rows a list: 1280 wide, not the window at its
  least), its tooltip saying when the window is too narrow. The choice and the tab are kept with the settings
  (`PageMemory` "trade.lists" and "trade.tab", written when changed), and the tab turns to a best deal's list when it is
  clicked. Each list's title has how many goods it shows and how many are in the deal its way.
- **Six columns a list** (`TradeWindowMath.ListColumns`, the same widths both ways): the picture (`UiKit.ItemPortrait`,
  framed in its quality's colour, the game's own words on it, the info card's button at the column's end) and the whole
  name, wrapped to as many lines as it needs, the row as tall (`RowHeight`: 40 at least, else the name and 8); how many
  there are (ours, theirs); the price with its mark against the usual (an arrow up or down and how far, green better for
  the colony, orange worse, "usual" within 2%); the deal's tag (its bars and one word: great, good, fair, poor); the
  need (the advice's word; headed "Keep" in the sell list, red when the trade sells into what is set aside); and the
  count. A narrower list gives way in a set order (`Fit`): the need, then how many, then the deal; the name, the price
  and the count stay. The kind column is gone: each list is grouped under kind headings (`Grouped`: the kinds in their
  order, food first, each with how many it shows; what the trader won't deal in last under "Not traded here").
- **The tooltip has the rest** (`RowTip`, made only while pointed at, over the row but its picture, its card's button
  and its count): how many there are, the market value and mass a piece, the game's own reckoning of the price, its
  share of the value and the usual, the grade's reasons (market, record, cap) and what the grades mean, and the advice.
  The market card (`TradeMarket.Hover`, its own setting) shows beside it over the whole row, not only the price: VTE's
  market in words, its last 60 days drawn, its news, the colony's record; with the card off, the market's words go into
  the tooltip. So the price trend, the market's "usual / avg" and the price's "70% of value" leave the row.
- **One way a list.** The game keeps one count a good (positive buys, negative sells) and its own control moves it both
  ways; in two lists that would let the sell list buy, and a number typed in one list's box fight the other's. Each
  list's control goes its own way (`OneWay`; the rules `ThisWay`, `Stepped`, `CountFor`, tested): the arrows point where
  the goods go, as the game's do (right to the trader, left to the colony), so in the sell list ">" sells one more, ">>"
  all of it, "<" takes one back and "<<" none; in the buy list "<" buys one more, "<<" all, ">" and ">>" back. Ten with
  Shift and a hundred with Ctrl (`GenUI.CurrentAdjustmentMultiplier`), a number typed into the list's own box, a good of
  one piece with single arrows, all within the game's own limits and set by its `CanAdjustTo` and `AdjustTo`; an arrow
  that can't move the count is greyed. A good in the deal the other way shows "Buying 5" or "Selling 5" in place of the
  count, and a click takes it out of the deal so it can go this way. Where the trader won't deal in it, or the
  negotiator won't sell into slavery, the game's own words, as before. A row in the deal its way has a thin edge in that
  way's colour.
- **Sorting.** Each list its own sort for the session, the name from A at first: its headers (name, how many, price,
  deal, need), and a menu at the count's heading with every sort, the columns' and those they leave out (market value,
  with VTE's history its market and trend, mass). The rows sort within their kind. The search and the chips filter both
  lists; "only in the deal" shows what goes each list's way.
- **Kept as it was:** the silver box, the best deals and this deal on the right, the foot, the caravan's strip, the
  market window, gifts and the game's screen both ways, Accept and its checks, the fall back to the game's screen; both
  looks (Sell and Buy as the kit's tabs) and the frame.
- **Nothing heavy per frame.** A row is read once a trade (`Read`): its price words and marks, its need's word, its sort
  keys, its tooltip's id and its market card's key. A list's lines are made when the filters, a sort or (with "only in
  the deal") the counts change; a name's height is measured once for a width (`Measure`); only the lines in sight are
  drawn. The headings' words are made with the columns, the chips' tooltips with the chips, and words without arguments
  are translated once.
- Keys in `Languages/English/Keyed/Rimfolk_TradeWindow.xml` (the old Kind, Market, Trend and Mass headings and their
  tooltips gone; Value, Market, Trend and Mass are the sort menu's words). Tests `Tools/Tests/TradeWindowTests.cs`: the
  grouping, the lists at 1920, 1600, 1280 and the least in both looks, the columns of each, the rows' heights, the one-way
  counts, the rows drawn from what was read. The Almanac's *the trade screen* in prose (keywords unchanged). Nothing saved
  in the game; no Harmony patch, no Sched slot, no new setting.
- **Not verified without the game:** the lists at the player's own screen and interface scale; a name wrapped in its
  column and the row's height for it (Small's line height as the game measures it); the arrows' glyphs in the kit's
  narrow buttons; the number box's focus inside a scroll view with two lists; the game's small icons beside an animal's
  or a captive's name in the room kept for them; the market card over the whole row beside the tooltip; a mod that
  patches the game's count control (none known in the player's list) no longer reaching Rimfolk's lists.

### The game's screen and the advice (0.150.0)

The game's own Dialog_Trade, for every kind of trade, made quicker to read without taking it over; its advice, reserve
and basket are what Rimfolk's window reads too:

- **Sorts are defs, not patches.** The game lists every `TransferableSorterDef` in its two "Sort by" menus, so the five
  new sorts are defs (`Defs/Misc/Rimfolk_TradeSorts.xml`) with comparers (`TradeSorts.cs`), the highest first: trader
  pays, trader asks, price per kg, best deal, suggested first. The menus are shared with the caravan and transport pod
  windows, which have no prices; a small transpiler on the menu's list (`Patch_TradeSortMenu`) leaves Rimfolk's sorts out
  there, and without the deeper hooks they fall back on market value.
- **The advice is read, not invented** (`TradeAdvice.cs`, once a trade opens): the plan ahead's stock rows, food days
  and shopping list, the blueprints' materials (`Making.BuildingWants`), the record of use, the journey being packed,
  wishes open, promised and kept, the drug policies, the research under way, and Vanilla Trading Expanded. Only what the
  colony has and uses counts as a need, so every age gets its own advice; a bargain fills a stock the colony already
  keeps, never a new one.
- **The reserve, in one rule** (`TradeAdviceMath`, pure and tested): keep the need and as much again, the need being a
  season's use by the record or a floor by kind and headcount, plus what is set aside. Food by days, weapons and
  clothes by spares (one a kind for every three people). Only a surplus worth a word (a tenth of the stock, 40 silver)
  is marked.
- **The price against the usual,** not against market value alone: a trader usually pays 60% of a thing's worth and
  asks 140%, moved by the negotiator and the difficulty, so 1 is "as usual" for any negotiator and a fifth better is a
  good sale or a bargain. With Vanilla Trading Expanded the worth is the good's own (its market's change divided out),
  so its demand and surplus show as good sales and bargains.
- **The basket is suggest-only:** buys first (each need answered once, the cheapest for what it gives), paid by the
  colony's silver and its sales; then sales as far as the trader's silver and the buys go; chosen again on what was sold
  if the trader runs short. It sets counts with the game's own `AdjustTo` and nothing else; the game's Accept trades.
- **Readouts only where the game has none:** silver after the trade in the price columns the silver row leaves empty,
  food days after a trade at home; a caravan's mass and food days after the trade are already the game's.
- **Other mods.** Vanilla Trading Expanded (read by name in `Integrations/VanillaTrading.cs`) patches no part of the
  screen: it moves a good's market value, so every price already carries its market. Its contracts and banks are read
  from its TradingManager; its switch for the vanilla value is set back at once, as its own windows do. Trade Helper's
  source isn't public (its workshop page and a stack trace show a postfix on the dialog's DoWindowContents drawing a
  side panel in 300 pixels it adds); Rimfolk draws inside the game's own layout, beside its buttons and in empty
  columns, never in that panel, and with it loaded leaves out the silver after the trade.
- No letters, messages or saved state: the basket's memory lives with the open trade.

### Price history and the colony's record (the player's request, 7 November 2026)

"Does vanilla trading expanded influence price developments? could you in that case have things like price history,
price compared to market price and other helpful and informative data." It does, three ways: the colony's own trades
(every three days, a chance of the market worth traded of a good over 1,000 silver, down for a sale, up for a
purchase, by 1% to 10% and more past 1,000 silver), its news, and a slow daily drift back toward the vanilla value. It
also keeps one price a day of every good it trades (`PriceHistoryAutoRecorder.records`). Rimfolk reads that, adds no
economic mechanic, and keeps one small record of its own:

- **Read, not modelled** (`Integrations/VanillaTrading.cs`, by name): `priceHistoryRecorders` and each one's `records`,
  `thingsAffectedBySoldPurchasedMarketValue` (the colony's trades VTE hasn't reckoned yet), the private `allNews` and
  each news' `AffectedThingDefs()`, `priceImpact` and `priceImpactStartTick`, and the setting
  `playerTransactionImpactMultiplier`. The vanilla value goes through VTE's own `outputOnlyVanilla` switch, set back in a
  `finally` in one place. "So many days ago" is the price that many records back, as VTE's terminal reads it.
- **The rules are pure** (`Trade/TradeMarketMath.cs`, tested): against the usual and the 30 days' average; the change
  over 7 and 30 days (over what there is when the history is shorter); the 60 days' high and low, "at" one within 2%
  where ten days or more spread a tenth; a notable move a tenth in a week (3 days at least) or a fifth in a month (10
  days at least). VTE's rule for the colony's trades becomes words only: "may" from a chance of a tenth, "likely" from
  two in five, "almost surely" from four in five, "sharply" from three of its steps; a trade against what was traded
  lately "evens it out", and where the earlier trades still outweigh it they are named instead.
- **Where it shows.** A card (an immediate window, Super layer) beside the mouse on either price of a row, on the left
  so the game's own price tooltip keeps the right, after the tooltip's own pause; a 28 by 14 line in the row's icons for
  a notable move only (`Patch_TradeRowMark`); the Market window from a button in the silver row's empty name area (drawn
  with the row's icons so the silver's own tooltip stops short of it, with a fallback after the row); a sixth sort,
  `Rimfolk_PriceChange`, left out of the menu without VTE's history and, like the rest, out of the caravan and transport
  pod windows. The marks' tooltips gain the market's reasons (`MarketHint`) for a sale or buy already marked, never a
  mark of their own. Nothing is drawn in Trade Helper's side panel.
- **The colony's record** (`Trade/TradeRecord.cs`, `TradeBook`, saved): taken in a prefix on the game's
  `TradeDeal.TryExecute` (the hook `Epithets/CouncilRecords.cs` already had for the negotiator's count; the counts are
  gone after it) and written in its postfix only if the trade went through. Nothing in Rimfolk recorded goods or prices
  before: the faction memory notes a trade's total worth and a sold captive, nothing a piece. Silver trades only, never
  gifts, people or animals; rows of one good, way and quality merged at the average price; the last 5 lines of a good
  (a thing and its stuff), 50 goods, the one traded longest ago going first; about 25 KB at the cap
  (`Tools/save_estimate.py`). Works without VTE.

## Weapons you can judge at a glance (the player's request, 9 November 2026)

"I struggle with ... judging how good a weapon actually is ... a real rating, maybe a number like 5.6 ... redo the whole
details tab for weapons ... my weapon mods themselves, like the inventory mod I'm using, the sidearms mod, the offhand
mod, so that they are all integrated." The plan is `docs/design/weapons.md`. Step 1 (0.182.0) built the rating
(`Weapons/WeaponRateMath.cs`), the tags (`WeaponTagMath.cs`) and the review of every weapon in the player's mods
(`docs/weapons/`). Step 2 (points 5 to 7) brings it into the game; step 3 (points 8 and 9, below) suggests the best weapon
for each colonist and lets them ask for one, and Rimfolk's card opens first.

- **One reading for the review and the game.** What a weapon's defs say is plain data (`Weapons/WeaponReadMath.cs`,
  pure): `WeaponDefFacts` (its verbs and projectiles, tools and the maneuvers they strike with, abilities, comps and mod
  extensions as class names and simple fields, its own stat values, the stuff's factors, and for the weapon in hand its
  unique and persona traits and whom it is coded to). `WeaponRead.Full` turns facts into the rating's inputs, rates them
  (the best firing mode, the melee rating as "in melee", by skill and by trait), gives the table, the tag facts, the tags
  and the line in plain words (`WeaponWordsMath.cs`, moved from the review). `Tools/WeaponReview/Inputs.cs` is now only
  the JSON to facts; regenerating the review gives `docs/weapons/weapons.json` and `README.md` byte for byte, so the
  game's rules are the review's for all 747 defs.
- **The live def as facts** (`Weapons/WeaponLive.cs`): its stats by the game's own stat workers for the weapon in hand
  (`StatRequest.For(thing)`) or a def, stuff and quality (`StatRequest.For(def, stuff, quality)`): accuracy at the four
  distances, `RangedWeapon_Cooldown`, the warm-up and range multipliers, `MeleeWeapon_CooldownMultiplier` and
  `MeleeWeapon_DamageMultiplier` (quality, stuff, Odyssey traits' stat changes and other mods' patches all in them); a
  projectile's damage and piercing by its own `GetDamageAmount` and `GetArmorPenetration` with the weapon's
  multipliers, stopping power as the game launches it. Types' names as defs write them (the game's without their
  namespace, a mod's in full; `DamageWorker` and `Verb` themselves as unset). A comp's and an extension's simple public
  fields by reflection (Vanilla Expanded Framework's heavy weapon read under the review's names). A unique weapon in hand
  (`CompUniqueWeapon.TraitsListForReading`): each trait's burst count and speed factors, extra stopping power, damage it
  turns the shot into and extra damage applied as `Verb.BurstShotCount`, `TicksBetweenBurstShots`,
  `Projectile.Launch` and `Verb_LaunchProjectile` do, its stat changes named; its ability is the thing's own comp's
  props, which the trait sets. A persona weapon (`CompBladelinkWeapon`, Royalty's and Vanilla Persona Weapons
  Expanded's): its traits' equipped stat offsets count as passives, moods and needs are named. Biocoding: who it is
  coded to, named, the rating unchanged. A def is rated in its stuff (steel where it takes metal, else wood, else
  granite blocks, else the game's default), at normal quality from a def's card.
- **Kept, nothing per frame.** By def, stuff and quality; by the weapon itself only where it has unique or persona traits
  (an hour of the game's time, then read again); a colonist as a fighter and their rating of a weapon an hour. All
  forgotten with a new game (`CouncilGameComponent`). The card works out what it says for a colonist once every two
  seconds; tooltips are made only while hovered.
- **For a colonist** (`WeaponForMath.cs`, pure): their real `ShootingAccuracyPawn` and `MeleeHitChance` read back
  through the game's curves into the skill level they stand for (sight, hands, bionics, traits and gear in them), the
  weapon now in their hands' offsets taken out (`StatWorker.StatOffsetFromGear`), their `AimingDelayFactor`,
  `RangedCooldownFactor`, `MeleeCooldownFactor` and `MeleeDamageFactor`, their race's own natural attacks. Why it
  differs, in steps that add up: their skill alone, then each trait whose stat offsets or factors work on this kind of
  fight (careful shooter, trigger-happy, brawler and any mod's), then the rest ("body and gear"). What stops them:
  incapable of violence, biocoded to someone else, a Vanilla Expanded heavy weapon without its trait (Tough), armour
  (an exoframe) or gene; what lets them carry one is named. A brawler holding a gun is told.
- **The info card** (`WeaponInfoCard.cs`): a pass-through postfix on `ThingDef.SpecialDisplayStats` adds entries in
  its own `StatCategoryDef` (`Rimfolk_WeaponRating`, display order 0, above the game's basics): the rating (its band,
  rough or not), each sub-rating, the line in plain words, each tag in its colour with why and its rule, the effects
  (counted and named, listed in the report pane), and for a weapon a colonist holds or carries, their own rating with
  its steps. A postfix on `Dialog_InfoCard.DoWindowContents` draws "Rimfolk's weapon card" with the badge at the foot,
  left of the close button (the card's private `thing`, `def` and `stuff` read by field references).
- **Rimfolk's weapon card** (`WeaponCardWindow.cs`, a `FramedWindow`, key "WeaponCard", least 440 by 460, a dialog that
  may cover the bottom bar, one at a time): the badge, band and role; the line; the tags as chips (`WeaponUi.cs`: each in
  its category's colour on the window's ground with its mark, Rimfolk's TrendUp, TrendDown and Warning icons and a star,
  diamond and dot drawn once at first use, so colour is never the only cue; the why on the tooltip); the sub-ratings as
  meters; the chart (damage per second by distance against no armour, flak, marine armour and mechanoids, the four
  distances the rating weighs marked, the values under the mouse; a melee weapon's four bars); the situations, best for
  and weak when marked; the effects with their sign and counted or named; the key numbers (a gun's damage, piercing,
  stopping power, range, aim, cooldown, burst, cycle, accuracy, blast and scatter; a blade's blows with the share the
  game gives each); then a colonist (the one who holds it, one selected with it, the last chosen, or picked from the
  map's colonists): their rating, the steps, the notes, and what they hold and carry, each rated for them, a click
  opening its card. In Rimfolk's look or the game's, with the kit.
- **The gear tab** (`WeaponGearTab.cs`, "Ratings on the gear tab"): the game's `ITab_Pawn_Gear.DrawThingRow` gives up
  56 pixels at a weapon row's end (a prefix narrows `width`) for the badge and the card's button; Nice Inventory Tab's
  rows (`NiceInventoryTab.EquippedItem.Draw`, the weapon in hand and Dual Wield's off hand) and cells
  (`NiceInventoryTab.InventoryItem.Draw`, the inventory and sidearms) get them on their corners, their `Item`, `pawn`
  and `Geometry` read by name; the button's click is caught in a prefix, before the row's own click opens the game's
  card. Each Nice Inventory Tab patch returns no target without the mod and stands down on purpose
  (`StandsDownWhy`), so "check myself" doesn't list it as failed.
- **A button on a weapon on the map** (`WeaponGizmo.cs`): a pass-through postfix on `ThingWithComps.GetGizmos` for a
  spawned weapon the rating reads, its label "Weapon card (6.1)".
- **The weapon mods, by name** (`WeaponMods.cs`; their DLLs read in the player's upload, never run): **Simple
  Sidearms** (`SimpleSidearms.rimworld.CompSidearmMemory.rememberedWeapons`, each pair's `thing` and `stuff`): the
  inventory's weapons are its sidearms, the remembered marked; the sensible pair is the best gun and the best melee
  weapon held or carried, a sidearm only within its default preset's weights (2.7 and 1.9 kg; the player has no
  settings file, so it runs on them), a one-use launcher never the gun. **Dual Wield** (`DualWield.Ext_Pawn_EquipmentTracker.TryGetOffHandEquipment`,
  `Ext_ThingDef.CanBeOffHand` and `IsTwoHand`, `DualWield.DualWield.Settings`' six penalties): each hand rated with its
  penalties as `VerbProperties.AdjustedCooldown` and `AdjustedAccuracy` apply them while both hands hold a weapon
  (cooldown +20% off hand and +10% main hand, accuracy -10% each, plus 5% and 0.5% per skill level under 20), both
  hands together (their fight values added, guns with guns, blades with blades). **RunAndGun** (`RunAndGun.RunAndGun.settings`:
  `accuracyPenalty`, `movementPenaltyHeavy` and `Light`, `forbiddenWeapons` and `selectedWeapons` read as its own
  code reads them, so with no settings file of the player's every gun is allowed and counts heavy): allowed on the
  move or not, and the rating on the move. **Melee Animation** (`AM.Tweaks.TweakDataManager.TryGetTweak`,
  `AM.AnimDef.GetExecutionAnimationsForPawnAndWeapon`, `AM.Core.Settings.EnableExecutions`, the tweak's
  `MeleeWeaponType` long for duels): animated or not, the execution moves open to it at the colonist's Melee, friendly
  duels. Its lasso is apparel, not a weapon's, and is left out.
- **Settings** (How you're told, Weapons; each on): `weaponRatings` "Weapon ratings" (the master; needs the deeper game
  hooks), `weaponGearTab` "Ratings on the gear tab", `weaponCard` "Rimfolk's weapon card". No saved game data, no Sched
  slot.
- **Text:** `Languages/English/Keyed/Rimfolk_Weapons.xml`. The tags' labels and reasons and the line in plain words are
  English, made from the numbers by the pure math (one place, shared with the review); the rest is keyed. The Almanac's
  "judging a weapon" (Defending).
- **Tests:** `Tools/Tests/WeaponLiveTests.cs` (331 checks): eight of the base game's weapons (assault rifle, sniper rifle,
  chain shotgun, charge rifle, frag grenades, knife, longsword, zeushammer) built as the live reader builds them rate as
  `weapons.json` has them (rating, role, every sub-rating and situation, tags and their reasons, the line, the table,
  rough or not, the specials, the rating by skill); quality and stuff; unique traits (burst, speed, stopping power,
  damage, EMP rounds) and persona traits; biocoding; the curves read backwards; a colonist's rating and its steps
  against the review's careful shooter and brawler; the held weapon taken out; Simple Sidearms' pair; Dual Wield's
  factors and the pair; RunAndGun; the chart; the colours; and the seams.

### Step 3: the best weapon for each colonist, and colonists who ask (points 8 and 9)

The player: "maybe recommended weapons on the pawn inventory page ... or that the pawns sometimes propose", and "it just
should be nuanced ... not just the blank values in mind, but also like special abilities, passive effects, situational
use". Released 0.184.0.

- **The choice, pure** (`Weapons/WeaponPickMath.cs`, tested in `Tools/Tests/WeaponPickTests.cs`). Each colonist with each
  weapon the colony has is scored: their own rating (`WeaponForMath`: skill, traits, body; the weapon's abilities,
  passives and specials are in it), plus 0.15 or 0.3 for a minor or burning passion for its kind, plus the situations they
  meet (a weapon's situational sub-ratings over its own overall, weighed by their mix of fights), less 0.8 for a hunter
  with a weapon they can't hunt with (the game's rule: a gun or bow that harms and doesn't explode), plus 0.4 for one their
  faith holds noble. The mix: the colony's situations together at most half (`ColonyShare`), a hunter's hunts and a
  doctor's or crafter's light weapon (its "sidearm" rating) a quarter each, 0.6 in all at most; the situations move a score
  by 2 at most. Never scored: a weapon the game refuses them (`EquipmentUtility.CanEquip`: coded or bonded to another, a
  second persona weapon, a role's rule), one too heavy for them (Vanilla Expanded's heavy weapons without Tough, an
  exoframe or the gene), one their faith despises, a gun for a brawler or someone incapable of shooting; nothing for
  someone incapable of violence. A brawler holding a gun, or anyone holding a weapon they mustn't, counts as empty-handed.
- **The colony's fights** (`ColonySituations`): the raids met lately, a raid weighed in full for 30 days, half to 60, a
  quarter to 120: the share that were mechanoids (times 0.5), armoured (flak or better on the torso, sharp armour 0.4 or
  more; times 0.4), crowds (ten or more, or a tribe's; times 0.3) and sieges (times 0.25); a defense line drawn on a home
  map is a gate held (0.15). Rimfolk keeps its own record (`WeaponPickBook.raids`, the last 12, from a hook on
  `IncidentWorker_Raid.PostProcessSpawnedPawns`); the game's own raid letters (`Find.Archive`, ThreatBig with a people)
  fill in what it doesn't have (raids before this, mechanoid clusters, other mods' raids), read by their people (mechanoids,
  a tribe's crowd, the armour of their age: 0.2 medieval, 0.4 industrial, 0.7 spacer).
- **The threshold**: 0.6 of a point (`Threshold`). Near the middle a point is about a third more damage for a gun and a
  fifth more for a blade, so 0.6 is about a fifth more for a gun and a ninth more for a blade, three times the rating's
  rounding and the mix's wobble: a revolver to a bolt-action (0.4) or a longsword to a uranium one (0.3) isn't suggested;
  a bolt-action to an assault rifle (0.9), an assault rifle to a charge rifle (0.9), a knife to a longsword (1.2) are.
  Another kind than the one in hand asks 0.5 more (without Simple Sidearms; with it the other kind is a sidearm); leaving
  their own bonded persona weapon unused asks 1.0 more, and the line says what it costs (and that a jealous persona would
  sour their mood). A colonist asks only for twice the threshold (1.2).
- **One assignment for the colony** (`Assign`): weapons from storage first (and, without Simple Sidearms, a better one a
  colonist carries in their own inventory, which with it is a sidearm it switches to itself), greedily the biggest
  worthwhile gain, one weapon per colonist; then, while the colony's total rises, two colonists exchange what they were given, one takes a
  better weapon left over, or one left without takes another's while that one takes a leftover (three rounds at most).
  Alike weapons (one kind, stuff, quality, coding) are weighed once. Tested against the best total by brute force on 300
  random colonies: the best in nearly all, never under three quarters of it, never one weapon to two. Then trades between
  two colonists (each gains 0.3, the other kind 0.5 more, the two 0.8; or, since the follow-up below, one gives up some for
  the colony; never a bonded weapon), the most worth first. Then Simple Sidearms (loaded): a weapon of the other kind than the one they will hold, within its default weights
  (2.7 kg a gun, 1.9 kg a blade, never a one-use launcher, never a gun for a brawler), when it beats what they carry of that
  kind (or an empty slot, 3.0) by the threshold. Then Dual Wield (loaded): for someone keeping a one-handed weapon with
  nothing in the off hand, one of the same kind that may go there, when both hands together (`WeaponForMath.PairTogether`,
  its penalties in) beat it alone by the threshold. With Simple Sidearms the weapon in hand is set against the best of its
  kind they carry. (Since "A full kit for every colonist", below: an empty sidearm slot, an empty off hand and empty hands
  are the kit's, filled first; the sidearm pass only betters a sidearm they carry.)
- **Why, in a line** (`Reasons`): two reasons, the strongest first, then what it costs. Their skill (12 or more, on a
  weapon that rewards skill, `SkillGain` 1.35 or more and more than what they hold: "her Shooting 14 makes its accuracy
  count"; 5 or less, on a forgiving one where theirs asks a good shot: "it forgives his Melee 4"), the trait that adds most
  (the steps of their own rating), the fights the colony meets where it is a point better than what they hold (its EMP for
  mechanoids, its piercing for armour), a hunter's clean kills, a doctor's or crafter's light weapon, a passion for a kind
  new to their hands, their faith's favour, an effect the weapon in hand lacks (an ability, EMP, a stun, fire, piercing,
  stopping power), simply better when nothing else says why. "Charge rifle: +1.4 for Ana: her Shooting 14 makes its
  accuracy count, and it pierces the armour your last raids wore." The words are keyed (`CC_WeaponPick_Why_*`); a gain is
  the score's difference for them, a badge their own rating.
- **In the game** (`Weapons/WeaponPick.cs`): a home map's grown colonists (not slaves or quest guests); the weapons they
  hold and carry and Dual Wield's off hand; what lies in storage they may take (a stockpile or shelf, not forbidden, not
  burning; an outfit stand's weapon, to be taken in hand only), the 16 best kinds of gun and of blade by their own rating,
  as many of each as there are colonists. Each colonist's own rating of each kind (`WeaponForMath.RateFor`, one rating,
  kept an hour), Dual Wield's pair for a one-handed main weapon (kept an hour). A weapon a colonist can't walk to is taken
  out for them and the choice made again. The choice is kept per map and made again once an hour, half a second after an
  order or "not now", or two seconds after what they hold or carry or how many weapons there are changes (looked at once a
  second). The reasons are made once with the colonist's rating steps (`WeaponLive.ForColonist`). The drawing reads the
  kept choice and checks each suggestion still stands (the weapon still lies there, isn't theirs, the trade's two still
  hold what they held).
- **The orders**, real jobs walked out on the map: the game's `Equip` (a persona weapon that would bond shows the game's
  own warning first), Simple Sidearms' `EquipSecondary` (its own `CanPickupSidearmInstance` asked first, its reason on the
  greyed button), Dual Wield's `DW_EquipOffhand`, a weapon from their own inventory put down and picked up (or, should Simple
  Sidearms be loaded, its own switch `equipSpecificWeaponFromInventory`), and a trade (`Rimfolk_SwapWeapons`,
  `Weapons/WeaponSwapJob.cs`): the one ordered walks to the other, and when they meet each hands the other what they hold
  (called off if either stops holding it, the other is down, drafted, asleep or not themselves, or may no longer carry it);
  Simple Sidearms' memory told by name as its own equip job tells it. A button is greyed with why when it can't be done
  now (no path, burning, reserved, down, Simple Sidearms' refusal). "On the way" while the job runs.
- **Where it shows** (`Weapons/WeaponPickUi.cs`, "Weapon suggestions"): the game's gear tab, under the comfortable
  temperatures (a postfix on `ITab_Pawn_Gear.TryDrawComfyTemperatureRange`, so the tab's scroll height follows): "Suggested
  weapons", a line each (three at most): the weapon's picture, "Better for Ana: charge rifle (+1.4)", the reasons under it,
  Equip (or As sidearm, Off hand, Trade), with Simple Sidearms "As sidearm" for a weapon in hand light enough, and "not
  now"; the tooltip has the whole line, what it costs and where it lies, a click opens the weapon's card. Nice Inventory
  Tab: a row of its own in the equipment box since the follow-up below (first a mark on the box's title, which the player
  didn't find). The weapon card: "Who
  should carry this", the three colonists it suits best by the same scores, with what it adds over what they have of its
  kind, a click choosing them below. The Defenses page (`UI/DefensePanel.cs`, after the advice): "Weapons for each
  colonist", a card per colonist with what they hold and its rating for them, each suggestion with its badge, gain and
  reasons and its button, "Not now" or "Show again"; under the heading what the choice weighs ("Each colonist's own rating,
  with the fights you meet: mechanoids, armoured raiders.") and how many weapons lie in storage; at the heading "Equip all
  suggested (n)", which only gives the orders, each colonist's after what they were told already (never one that would
  bond a persona weapon).
- **Colonists who ask** (`Weapons/WeaponAsks.cs`, "Colonists ask for better weapons"): at their slice's hourly look, a
  colonist whose best suggestion is a weapon lying in storage (in hand, as a sidearm or in the off hand, never a trade)
  with a gain of 1.2 or more; in their free time (a recreation hour, a joy job, idle) in the home area, awake, able to talk,
  not drafted, downed or in a mental state, no threat on the map or enemy near; at most once in five days each, once a day
  in the colony, the same weapon not again for fifteen days, not while set aside; then a 12% chance (about a third of
  their free days once the waits are over). The weapon's place is read at that moment ("in the stockpile", "on the shelf",
  "on the outfit stand": the slot group's building, its label). The line (`Rimfolk_Pool_WeaponAsk`, one sentence each)
  is tagged for the reason (mechanoids, armoured, crowds, siege, choke, skill, trait, hunting, passion, noble, worker,
  special, sidearm, offhand, better) and kind; only a line for the reason is said (else one for "better"); the colony's age
  picks the words where they differ (a tribe's walking metal ones and hard coats, the middle ages' iron walkers and plate),
  the speaker's tone the voice. A quiet row in This week (How people are, counted nowhere) while it still lies there for
  three days: "Ana would rather carry the charge rifle in the stockpile (+1.4)", its reasons under it, a click opening
  her gear tab, "Look" the Defenses page at the view.
- **Not now**: per colonist, ten days (`WeaponPickBook.notNow`): their suggestions don't show or take a weapon in the
  colony's choice, and they don't ask. On the Defenses page "Show again" brings them back.
- **Kept with the game** (`WeaponPickBook`, a GameComponent; an older save gets an empty one): the raids (12), "not now"
  (ended ones pruned daily) and each colonist's last ask (one each; of those gone, fifteen days). Modelled in
  `Tools/save_estimate.py`. Its clock: every 250 ticks at `Sched.RareWeaponPicks` (47), a tenth of the colonists each turn
  (each once an hour): their ratings of the kinds the choice weighs worked out ahead (so the hourly choice reads kept
  ones), then their look for a weapon to ask for; timed as `Pass.RareWeaponPicks`; nothing with both settings off.
- **Rimfolk's card first** (the player: "can the rimworld weapon card be the default screen when opening stats/info of a
  weapon?"; `Weapons/WeaponCardFirst.cs`, "Open Rimfolk's weapon card first", on; only while "Weapon ratings" and
  "Rimfolk's weapon card" are on): a prefix on `WindowStack.Add` that lets every window but a `Dialog_InfoCard` pass
  untouched; a new info card about a weapon the card can show (a weapon itself, or a weapon's kind with its stuff, read
  from the card's `thing`, `def` and `stuff`) opens as Rimfolk's weapon card instead, while playing. What stays the
  game's: a card opened while the game's card is being drawn (a prefix and finalizer on `Dialog_InfoCard.DoWindowContents`
  mark it: its links and its back button move within it), the game's card asked for from Rimfolk's card (its button "All
  the game's stats", let through once), anything else. The game's card's button "Rimfolk's weapon card" closes it when
  opening Rimfolk's with the setting on. A kind's card says how it is rated: "Its kind as made, for a colonist of Shooting
  8 · normal quality, steel".

### The weapon you can see, and trades for the colony (the player's follow-ups, 9 November 2026)

The player, with a picture of Nice Inventory Tab's gear view: "can the rimfolk item ui also please always have an image of
the item included? it can have a prominent spot because they look cool" and "where do i see the weapon recommendation in
this ui mod?"; then "pawns should also propose to switch weapons if there's more value to gain, e.g. a low shooting pawns
is blocking the best weapon, even if the weak pawn gets an even worse shooting score. also it should perhaps also give a
warning if a pawn has a lucky weapon and would lose it, but that should not block the exchange altogether". Released 0.186.0.

- **The item's picture** (`UiKit.ItemPortrait`, `UI/UiKitItems.cs`, the apparel card's too): the thing as it
  looks, by the game's own `Widgets.ThingIcon` (its stuff's colour, its style or its faith's look, a unique or persona
  weapon's own graphic, the variant a random graphic picked for this very thing, any mod's graphic), a kind by
  `Widgets.DefIcon` in its usual stuff; on a dark tile framed in its quality's colour. The game has no colours for quality
  (`QualityUtility` has none, in 1.6 or 1.7), so Rimfolk's look gives its own (`UI/ItemPortraitMath.cs`): awful brown, poor
  grey, normal light, good green, excellent blue, masterwork violet, legendary gold, each 4.5:1 or better on the window's
  ground and Nice Inventory Tab's, 3:1 on a raised card (tested). A large tile (64 and up) is framed twice and names its
  quality on a strip at its foot; its tooltip is the label. A graphic a mod can't give leaves the tile empty, warned once.
  The weapon card's head: the picture 96 to 128 pixels (a fifth of the card), beside it the badge, band and role, how it is
  rated and the line in plain words. Small pictures wherever the card lists weapons: what a colonist holds, carries and has
  in the off hand, what each one in "Who should carry this" holds now; and on the Defenses page.
- **The suggestions in Nice Inventory Tab's equipment box** (`Weapons/WeaponNiceTab.cs`, read from its decompiled build,
  all by name, standing down without it or a member it reads): the box (`ITab_Pawn_Gear_Patch.equipment_alt_groupbox` in
  its alternative layout, the one in the player's picture, `equipment_legacy_groupbox` in its first) holds a scrolling list
  (`GroupBox.Childs[0]`, a `VScrollLayout`) of rows of fixed height that it lays out itself (`Widget.Update`) and scrolls
  when they are taller than the box. Rimfolk puts a row of its own in that list, under the last thing held (weapons,
  sidearms, belts) and above the inventory's cells: one of its `LabelWidget`s with no text (it draws nothing itself) given
  the suggestions' height (`Widget.SetFixedHeight`), so the box makes room as for its own rows and nothing overlaps or is
  cut. A postfix on `ITab_Pawn_Gear_Patch.Recache(Pawn)` (each frame, after its own recache, before it draws) checks the
  row's place and height (a short list of references, `WeaponNiceMath.Place`) and lays the box out again only when either
  changed (Nice Inventory Tab adds its rows back after an equipment change, so the row is seen out of place and moved); a
  postfix on `LabelWidget.Draw`, for Rimfolk's row only, draws the suggestions inside its scroll view, so they scroll and
  clip with its rows. Widths (`WeaponNiceMath`): at its first tab width (760) a row is 363 pixels, 349 with the scroll bar;
  at its narrowest (560) "Not now" becomes a cross with its words on the tooltip, so the widest acts still fit (tested).
- **A suggestion's row**, the same on Nice Inventory Tab's box (in its own colours: `Assets.ColorBGD`, `ColorBG`,
  `ColorStat`, `BuffColor`, `PenaltyColor`, `ColorBGL`, read by name) and under the game's gear tab's list (in the game's look,
  its buttons; `WeaponPickGearTab.Row` with a `SuggestLook`): a dashed, softly tinted frame and a small "Suggested" tag
  ("Asked for" when the colonist, or in a trade the other, asked lately), so it never reads as a weapon held; the weapon's
  picture in a tile as wide as Nice Inventory Tab's own rows' pictures (1.2 its height); its name with its quality, its
  rating for them (the badge) and the gain ("+1.4", a loss in a trade "-0.5"); why in one line, cut to fit (the whole line,
  what it costs and where it lies on the tooltip); its buttons, real orders as before: Equip, As sidearm (Simple Sidearms),
  Off hand (Dual Wield), "Trade with Bautista", Not now; or "on the way"; a warning line when it gives up something that
  matters (a lucky weapon, an heirloom, a bonded persona weapon, a hunter's hunts). A click on the picture or the words opens
  the weapon's card. Three rows at most (in hand, a sidearm, the off hand). The title's mark is gone.
- **When there's nothing to suggest** ("Say when there's no better weapon", on, under Weapons): one quiet line in the box
  (and under the game's list): "No better weapon in storage", its tooltip what was compared (what they hold and its rating
  for them, how many weapons lie in storage, the fights weighed, the least gain), a click the colony's view on the Defenses
  page; "Weapon suggestions set aside for Ana for now" (a click brings them back), or that they don't fight.
- **Compare** on Nice Inventory Tab's weapon rows: a row has no room for a word more (its label, its own buttons, its
  bars and its numbers fill it), so the rating's badge on its picture opens Rimfolk's card to compare, as the small button
  beside it does (both clicks caught before the row's own), its tooltip saying so.
- **How much each colonist fights** (`WeaponPickMath.FightWeight`, `PickColonist.Fights`, from 0.2 to 1): their best of
  Shooting and Melee against the colony's best (two fifths), their time drafted (the game's `TimeDrafted` record) against
  the colony's most (seven twentieths), their fights (the game's records: kills of people, mechanoids and entities, ten
  shots' worth each, and shots fired) against the colony's most (a quarter); a hunter's hunts add a tenth; a doctor or
  crafter is weighed at four fifths; with no hour drafted or fight in the colony yet the skill stands in. At 0.5 or less the
  line says they rarely fight. The colony's assignment weighs each gain by it (greedy, exchanges and moves), so of two who'd
  gain alike the best weapon goes to the front line; each must still gain enough for themselves.
- **Trades for the colony** (`WeaponPickMath.Trade`): better for both as before, or one gives up some: the one who gains
  gains 1.0 or more (`SwapGainer`, the other kind 0.5 more), the colony gains 0.8 or more (`SwapColony`), each one's gain or
  loss by how much they fight, and the one who gives up some still holds something better than bare hands. A weak shot
  holding the best gun: a good shot's +1.9 against a rarely fighting doctor's -0.6 is worth 1.72, suggested; +1.0 against
  -1.0 between two who fight alike is worth nothing, not suggested (tested, with random colonies: nobody left without a
  weapon who had one, no weapon to two, trades in pairs). A trade is weighed against what storage gave its two: worth more,
  it replaces that, and storage is shared again among the rest. The line says both sides: "Charge rifle to Ana (+1.9),
  Bautista takes her revolver (-0.6): the colony gains, and Bautista rarely fights."; the one who gives up some has no
  reasons of their own, the colony's are theirs.
- **A lucky weapon or an heirloom, never a bar** (`PickColonist.Keepsakes`): Rimfolk's lucky-item quirk on a weapon
  (`Quirks/LuckyItems.cs`; its mood comes with any weapon of its kind on them, so another of the kind keeps it, and with
  Simple Sidearms the weapon set down is kept as a sidearm when it fits its weights) and an heirloom carried
  (`Lives/Legacy.cs`, the heir's comfort or anyone's), read only while those moods are on. Giving one up costs a little in
  the choice (0.04 of a point for each point of mood between having it and not, at most 0.4: a lucky weapon's +3 and -4 is
  0.28), where it weighs one weapon or trade against another (another autopistol keeping the luck may win over a slightly
  better rifle), never against the threshold or a trade's rules, so it never stops a suggestion on its own; the line
  always says it, with the real numbers:
  "Bautista would be upset to give up his lucky autopistol (mood -4 without it, +3 with it)". Persona bonds stay as before.
- **Trades proposed by the colonists** (`WeaponAsks.cs`, "Colonists ask for better weapons", pool
  `Rimfolk_Pool_WeaponTrade`): when a colonist has no stored weapon to ask for, their best trade that stands where one of
  the two gains 1.2 or more, the asks' own waits and chance; then said to the other once the two are together
  (`Together.When`, up to four hours), both safe and both weapons still in their hands as the words say. The one who gains
  asks ("Bautista, that charge rifle would do more in my hands, will you take my revolver?"), the one who gives up some offers
  ("You should have this charge rifle, Ana, I can barely aim it.", tagged for a low skill or rarely fighting only when so),
  two who both gain propose it; every age, every tone, one sentence each. Nobody asks for a suggestion that gives up their
  own lucky weapon or heirloom; the other may still propose the trade, its line warning of it. The inbox's quiet row: "Ana
  proposed a trade to Bautista: her revolver for his charge rifle (+1.9)", its act the trade's order; the gear tab's row is
  tagged "Asked for". A trade proposed is kept as the colonist's last ask (with the other's id, `WeaponAskNote.other`).
- **Tests**: `Tools/Tests/WeaponShowTests.cs` (the qualities' colours, the card's tile, Nice Inventory Tab's widths at every
  tab width it allows, the room the box makes, where the row goes, the seams); `WeaponPickTests.cs` (how much each fights,
  trades for the colony, a lucky weapon and an heirloom, the trades' pool in every age).

### A full kit for every colonist (the player's request, 9 November 2026)

The player, with a picture of Avila's gear in Nice Inventory Tab (an autopistol and a belt, no melee weapon, and the quiet
line "No better weapon in storage"): "the mod should also recognize if a pawn has no melee/ranged sidearm equipped and then
offer one from the inventory. the pawns should always have a ranged and melee weapon, assuming they have no restrictions,
and suggest/equip them accordingly. also offhand if they have capacity & compatibility". Released 0.189.0.

- **The kit** (`Weapons/WeaponKitMath.cs`, pure, tested in `Tools/Tests/WeaponKitTests.cs`): with Simple Sidearms every
  colonist who can fight carries one ranged and one melee weapon, one in hand and the other as a sidearm; with Dual Wield, a
  weapon in the off hand where their hands, the weapons and the mod's rules allow it and it adds something. Without Simple
  Sidearms the kit is the one weapon in hand (a vanilla colonist holds one), without Dual Wield there is no off hand. Each
  slot is filled (the weapon in hand of its kind, or a sidearm Simple Sidearms remembers; a one-use launcher never counts),
  missing, or not for them and why (`KitView`, `KitBar`).
- **Restrictions decide the kit, and it never fights them:** incapable of violence, no kit; incapable of shooting or a
  brawler, melee only; a kind their Ideology role bars (the game's `RoleEffect_NoRangedWeapons` and `NoMeleeWeapons`,
  `PickColonist.RoleNoRanged` and `RoleNoMelee`, now also in `WeaponPickMath.Score`), none of it; a weapon the game refuses
  them (`EquipmentUtility.CanEquip`: coded, bonded, a race's rule as Humanoid Alien Races adds it, a role's), one their
  faith despises, a heavy weapon they can't carry, never (each `PickOption.Cant`); a sidearm only within Simple Sidearms'
  weights (its default preset: 2.7 kg a gun, 1.9 kg a blade), never a one-use launcher or one on an outfit stand (its job
  takes it from the ground), and never one its own `CanPickupSidearmInstance` refuses them now (asked of each stored weapon
  light enough, `PickOption.SidearmCant`: its weight modes, slots and their free room as set); an off-hand weapon only where
  Dual Wield's `CanBeOffHand` allows it, not `IsTwoHand`, of the main hand's kind (both hands fire or swing together), never
  beside a two-handed main weapon and never with a hand or arm missing (its own `HasMissingArmOrHand` rule, read from the
  game's missing parts).
- **A missing kind is a gap, filled even under the usual threshold** (0.6), but never with something nearly useless: the
  least is 2.0 for them (`Floor`, twice bare hands, `WeaponPickMath.Unarmed`; their own score with skill, traits, passion
  and the fights you meet; "poor" on the rating's scale runs up to 3.5), a shooter's blade must beat their gun's own blows
  (its "in melee" rating, a rifle's butt about 3.0) by 0.3 (`OverBash`), and an off-hand weapon must add 0.3 to both hands
  together over the main hand alone (`OffHandAdds`, Dual Wield's penalties in). The weapon chosen is the best for the part
  it plays (`RoleScore`, never the minimum): in hand, their own score; a sidearm half its "sidearm" situation over its
  overall (light and handy), a quick blade a fifth of a point more (a shooter's melee sidearm), a gun a tenth of its
  "kiting" situation over its overall (a melee fighter's gun to finish or kite with). With nothing in hand and both kinds
  missing, the kind they would rather hold (a gun when they shoot at least as well as they fight hand to hand) goes in
  hand, the other as a sidearm.
- **Where it comes from:** storage (as before; forbidden weapons are read too, never suggested or taken, only asked for and
  named where nothing fills a slot, `ForbiddenFills`); their own pack (a weapon Simple Sidearms doesn't remember, which its
  own unloading would carry to storage, `WeaponMods.Unremembered`, read as its `FirstUnloadableThing` reads its memory:
  kept as a sidearm, no walk, `PickKind.Keep`, a third of a point in its favour when choosing); another colonist's spare
  (`Spares`: a weapon they carry beyond their own kit, each kind they don't hold keeping its best; never a lucky weapon, an
  heirloom, a bonded weapon or a one-use launcher, none from someone set aside; `PickKind.Spare`, a third of a point against
  it when choosing, so storage comes first).
- **The colony's choice fills the kit first** (`WeaponPickMath.Assign`): those with nothing in hand are served first in the
  greedy, take any weapon sensible for them, and no exchange leaves them unarmed (a move that arms one always wins, taking if
  need be a weapon given as another's upgrade; tested against brute force with the kit first, then the most gain); the
  weapons the other empty slots would take are kept from everyone's upgrades (`Reserve`), those whose off hand is to be
  filled keep their main hand this round, those whose sidearm's kind follows their main hand trade only for the same kind.
  Then the empty slots are filled for real, each one's worth by how much they fight (`FightWeight`), so the front line is
  served first when weapons are short; then upgrades and trades as before, then a sidearm they carry bettered. A trade may
  arm someone holding a weapon they mustn't use.
- **Shown:** the gear tab's row (`WeaponPickGearTab.Row`) gets the missing case: tagged **Missing**, its headline what is
  missing and how it is filled ("No melee weapon: steel hatchet as a sidearm"; the rating is the badge beside it, the
  Defenses page's head says "(3.8)"), the same picture, rating and reasons ("she has nothing for close work, and it's
  light enough to carry beside her autopistol"), the right button (Equip, As sidearm, Off hand, **Keep as sidearm**, **Take
  from** whom). The quiet line is honest about the kit: an empty slot nothing fills is said, "No melee weapon in storage for
  Avila" (both kinds: "No weapon in storage"), under the rows too (Nice Inventory Tab's row height follows,
  `WeaponNiceMath.Height`'s `gapLine`), its tooltip what was looked at and why each was left out (`Looked`, `KitLeftOut`:
  forbidden, the game's refusal, past the sidearm's weight, Simple Sidearms' refusal, one-use, on an outfit stand, too weak
  for them, no better than the gun's butt, adds too little in the off hand, not allowed there, two-handed, going to someone
  else); "No better weapon in storage" when the kit is full. The Defenses page: each colonist's kit at a glance under their
  name (`WeaponKitWords.Chips`: ranged, melee and with Dual Wield the off hand, each its picture and rating for them,
  missing, or a dash with why on the tooltip), how many kits are full, and **Fill every kit (n)**, which only gives the
  orders (`WeaponPick.DoKit`). The weapon card's "Who should carry this": who lacks its kind first ("she has no melee
  weapon (+3.0)").
- **Colonists fill a gap themselves** (`Weapons/WeaponKitSelf.cs`, "Colonists fill an empty weapon slot themselves",
  `weaponKitSelf`, on): at their hourly look on the suggestions' own slice (`Sched.RareWeaponPicks`, no new slot), in their
  free time at home and safe (`WeaponAsks.FreeAndSafe`: not drafted, downed, asleep or in a mental state, no threat on the
  map or near), at most once a day each (`WeaponPickBook.fetched`, saved, pruned daily), a colonist with an empty slot the
  choice fills from storage starts a real job of their own accord (`StartJob`, not an order): the game's `Equip` into an
  empty hand only, Simple Sidearms' `EquipSecondary`, Dual Wield's `DW_EquipOffhand`; a weapon already in their pack is
  remembered at once. Never in place of a weapon they hold, never forbidden, never what something stops now
  (`WeaponPick.WhyNot`: a path, burning, reserved, Simple Sidearms' refusal), never a persona weapon that would bond, never
  one their faith despises (out of the choice). The game's apparel policy covers apparel only, so it has no say over
  weapons. A line as they pick it up (the job's finish action, on success; `Rimfolk_Pool_WeaponKitTake`, tagged hand,
  sidearm, offhand or keep and the kind, every age and tone). Off, an empty slot is only suggested.
- **Colonists who ask** gain a reason, "kit" (`Rimfolk_Pool_WeaponAsk`, every age, ranged, melee and the off hand: "I've
  nothing for close work, can I take the knife in the stockpile?"), under the same waits and chance, whatever the gain;
  only when they don't fill it themselves (the setting off, or something they can't take on their own: a forbidden weapon,
  one on an outfit stand for a sidearm, one in place of what they hold, a persona weapon). A forbidden weapon asked for has
  a quiet row in This week whose act allows it.
- **Simple Sidearms by name** (`WeaponMods`): its memory read (`rememberedWeapons`, each pair once, the one in hand first),
  told of a sidearm kept (`GetMemoryCompForPawn`, `InformOfAddedSidearm`), its refusal asked (`CanPickupSidearmInstance`).
  A spare handed over (`Rimfolk_TakeSpareWeapon`, `JobDriver_TakeSpareWeapon` in `Weapons/WeaponSwapJob.cs`): the one
  taking it walks to the one who carries it, who hands it over from their pack, into an empty hand or else the pack; both
  memories told by name.
- **Saved:** `WeaponPickBook.fetched` (colonist: tick, a day), modelled in `Tools/save_estimate.py`. No new Harmony patch,
