  survivors near a river (half of them, `SaltRiver`) river folk, a band led by a learned one (Intellectual 10)
  scholars, a league of the spacer age an enclave, faithful who broke away in an industrial or spacer world pilgrims; a
  lean with no river in reach is let go. Release B's pace and caps unchanged. The Almanac's page *pilgrims, scholars,
  the enclave and the river folk*. Fixed on the way: a caller of a calling (`HappeningSetting.people` `calling:`) could
  be a Hospitality guest of any people already on the map, standing in under that people's name.
- **Their gear, their kinds of people and their gifts** (`Tools/Tests/PeoplesGearTests.cs`, "peoples' gear: ";
  docs/design/peoples.md, the section of that name). No kind has `apparelColor`: each people's base kind dyes its
  signature pieces by name (`specificApparelRequirements` with an `apparelDef` and a `color`), a civilian kind picks its
  signature garment by `alternateTagChoices`, the rest comes from wider tags and money by role. Soldiers wear a common
  kit (`apparelRequired`), a religious habit is shared but not its cut or age, civilians vary. A mod's tags and pieces
  only with `MayRequire` on it, every name in `Tools/Tests/PeopleGear.txt`; medieval and tribal peoples off
  `IndustrialBasic` (Vanilla Apparel Expanded's modern clothes). `inventoryOptions` for what they carry, never on a
  trader. `xenotypeSet` a real mix of Biotech's, Vanilla Races Expanded's, Alpha Genes' and the xenotype mods' kinds of
  people, three in four or so baseliners. `PeopleKindExtension` (gifts: a class of A RimWorld of Magic by its trait's name,
  or a psylink, with Vanilla Psycasts Expanded a path by name) given by `Patch_PeopleGifts`, a postfix on the game's
  `GenerateNewPawnInternal` (fresh pawns only, the deeper game hooks on); `PeoplesGearMath` (one roll against the shares,
  never more than 60% of a kind, the psylink's levels, the class's setting). Pawns already in a game keep theirs.
- **Their stories, sayings and touchpoints** (`Tools/Tests/PeoplesLoreTests.cs`, "peoples' lore: "; docs/design/
  peoples.md, the section of that name). A founding story in each faction's description (its middle paragraph), and
  `PeopleExtension.honours`, `fears`, `sayings` shown on the people's card (`PeopleLore`, a lines section in the card's
  story slot; a saying picked by the faction's id, so it reads the same). Their voices in the existing pools by
  `their:CALLING` (letters' condolences and warnings, messengers, `Rimfolk_VisitorLines`, `Rimfolk_Pool_OutsiderSays`),
  three talk pieces each, `Rimfolk_Pool_PlayDisputation`. Touchpoints, each only from a people of its calling:
  `HappeningWorker_OrderNurse` (a fever: the hospitaller goes from bed to bed by `VisitorServices.Dose` with
  `Rimfolk_OrderNursed`), `HappeningWorker_LongWalk` (a file of pilgrims at the graves, a walk together or food carried
  out), `Rimfolk_Evt_Disputation` (data only: an evening gathering with the fellow as guest), `HappeningWorker_EnclaveSalvage`
  and `DilemmaEffect_EnclaveSalvage` (salvage by drop pod at the trade spot, by `PeoplesLoreMath.SalvageGoods` of the
  colony's age; a runner on foot for a colony without radio), `HappeningWorker_RiverNets` (boatmen on the dry bank by the
  water), the league's camp `Rimfolk_Camp_LeagueWinter` (winter, trading, guards if asked, the Waystone Book) and the
  winter herd's young beast. A camp's gift (`CampGift`) may now be `young` (a young beast of the camp's own grazing kinds,
  the colony's, handed over at the gate on the farewell walk) and kept for a good stay (`maxTension`: no walk to the gate
  without it). Faiths gain a soft meme or structure each where thin, checked against the memes' exclusion tags. Arising
  names gain a third form carrying their ways. Nothing saved, no clock, nobody hurt.
- **Release D: the Lantern Wardens, the Quiet Bell, the Circuit of Tamers and the Wheel** (`Tools/Tests/PeoplesDTests.cs`,
  "peoples, release D: "; docs/design/peoples.md, the section of that name; the first four of `docs/design/peoples-next.md`).
  `Rimfolk_Wardens` (medieval, tribal parent, calling `hunters`), `Rimfolk_QuietBell` (medieval, tribal parent,
  `sextons`), `Rimfolk_Tamers` (industrial, outlander parent, `tamers`), `Rimfolk_Wheel` (industrial, outlander parent,
  `salvagers`), each arising in every age (`ariseAges` 0~3), drawn only from the player's active mods
  (`docs/player-mods/`). Every age: `Peoples.AgeOf` (an arisen people keeps the age of what it came from,
  `PeoplesDMath.PeopleAge`), `PeopleKindExtension.ageArms` (a kit's weapon tags for other ages and what it may cost,
  `AgeArms.Arm` as a pawn is made) and `PeopleGift.ages`. Callers (`Peoples/PeoplesD.cs`, `PeoplesD2.cs`): the Wardens'
  hunt on a legend, nemesis or alpha on the land (`HappeningWorker_WardensHunt`, `DilemmaEffect_WardensHunt`: the game's
  assault-things lord, the colony's shot on the game's hunt; the kill seen in `HappeningTracker.Notify_Killed`, the
  carcass skinned by `JobDriver_PeoplesWork` and its butchering split, `PeoplesD.Divide`; given up after two days, they
  walk home), the pelt-buyer, a lantern for one a beast took; the Bell at the enemy's dead (a subclass of the
  undertakers' worker, `DilemmaEffect_BellForTheDead`'s goodwill with the dead's peoples), its funeral at a fresh grave,
  the void's signs (Anomaly); the tamer's bout (`JobDriver_TamerBout` by the Fighting-type spar's rules, `HarmKinds.TamerBout`
  through `Harm.Roll`/`Injure`), eggs swapped or sold, a stray brought home; the Wheel's fixer (a subclass of the
  tinker's worker), its scrap-runners (`PlayCarry.Scrap`), a mechanoid wreck stripped half and half (`StripJob`). The hunt
  and the bout are visits of the happenings' tracker (`Visit` kinds `wardenHunt`, `tamerBout`). The Wheel's towns move
  (`WheelTowns.Daily` from `RegionBook.Daily`: on each town's own day of 30, two to five tiles by `Arising.TryTownTile`,
  never with a map, a caravan or a quest on it). Asks, the patch (four world events, the undertakers, the tinker and the
  vet prefer them: `Undertakers.People`, `Tinker.People`), release B's leans (`ArisingMath.Lean`: survivors to the Bell on
  a fated quarter, `SaltBell`, or in a later age to the Wheel on a fated third, `SaltWheel`; a band led by one good with
  beasts to the Circuit, by a good shot to the Wardens). Nothing saved.
- **Release E: the Stormglass Conclave, the Mossborn, the Ashen Banner and the Kiln Guild** (`Tools/Tests/PeoplesETests.cs`,
  "peoples, release E: "; docs/design/peoples.md, the section of that name; the second four of `docs/design/peoples-next.md`).
  `Rimfolk_Stormglass` (industrial, outlander parent, calling `seers`), `Rimfolk_Mossborn` (tribal, `grovekeepers`),
  `Rimfolk_AshenBanner` (medieval, tribal parent, `mercenaries`), `Rimfolk_KilnGuild` (medieval, tribal parent,
  `artisans`), each arising in every age, from the player's active mods only. `PeopleAgeArms.apparel` (`AgeArms.Kit`): an
  age's kit worn with its arms, the Banner's one issued kit in every age. Callers (`Peoples/PeoplesE.cs`, `PeoplesE2.cs`,
  one job driver, `JobDriver_PeoplesE`): the Conclave's watch (a visit, kind `glassWatch`; `Patch_GlassHold`, a prefix on
  `Storyteller.TryFire`, puts a sky condition the storyteller sends into the game's own incident queue 18 to 30 hours on,
  a runner, kind `glassRunner`, at the gate with the warning; `GlassWatch.Ahead` into `FieldWeather.Forecast`), its rod
  (`Rimfolk_StormglassRod`; `Patch_GlassRodStrike` and `Patch_GlassRodExplosion` take the strike within 18 cells, no
  blast; a weather station in `WeatherDynamics`) and its lesson (`Rimfolk_GlassTaught`, `PeoplesEMath.Taught`); the
  Mossborn's saplings, grave's tree and Gauranlen tree pruned (`CompTreeConnection.ConnectionStrength`), and their
  ledger (`MossLedger`: `Patch_MossFelled` on `Plant.PlantCollected`, sown trees counted by `Plant.sown` and id, four
  counts in `ArisingBook`, reckoned every fifteen days from `RegionBook.Daily`, `WorldSituationWorker.Goodwill`, never
  below none); the Banner's squad (`BannerSquad`, a camp `Rimfolk_Camp_BannerSquad` with `fights` and work `contract`,
  `Camps/CampContract.cs`: a sentry at the gate by day, the wage an ask priced `wage` on the fifth and the tenth day,
  `Leave("unpaid")`), its deserter, its Roll at a grave; the guild's commission (`PlayMake.KeepMade`, `Callers.Commission`,
  collected only by `HappeningWorker_GuildCollects`: `Callers.Due` takes a filter now), its pay by quality, its bid. Two
  hosting asks (`HappeningWorker_MissionHost`): the apprentice's skywatch and the wander-year's bench, its piece by
  `ThingRoles` (`SmallArt`). The patch: four world events, the fortune teller and the art collector prefer them
  (`FortuneTeller` and `Collector` read `HappeningExtension.prefers`). Release B's leans (`ArisingMath.Lean`, 13
  arguments: a band led by a psycaster, a fighter, a crafter or a grower). Nobody hurt.
- **Release F: the Signal Line, the Deepwell Union, the Last Republic and the Hollow Fleet** (`Tools/Tests/PeoplesFTests.cs`,
  "peoples, release F: "; docs/design/peoples.md, the section of that name; the first four of `docs/design/peoples-third.md`).
  `Rimfolk_SignalLine` (industrial, outlander parent, calling `linesmen`), `Rimfolk_Deepwell` (industrial, `drillers`),
  `Rimfolk_Republic` (industrial, `citizens`), `Rimfolk_HollowFleet` (spacer, `crew`), each arising in every age, the
  three industrial ones rising toward the spacer age at 8, 11 and 9 years an age, from the player's active mods only; one
  kit for the Line's linemen, the Republic's Civic Guard (every age's issue in the same navy) and the Fleet's whole crew.
  The relay mast (`Rimfolk_RelayMast`, `CompRelayMast`, `RelayMast`): raised by a lineman on the colony's highest ground,
  worn by thunderstorms, quiet under half its strength; while it sings (and a Line is at peace) letters by a messenger
  or a bearer and their answers take half the days (`NeighbourLetters`, `PeoplesFMath.Relayed`), the post counts it as a
  mast near (`PostReach.Mast`), and `Patch_LineMastWarns` (a prefix on `Storyteller.TryFire`) holds a raid the
  storyteller sends in the game's own incident queue 2 to 4 hours behind the line's warning letter. Callers
  (`Peoples/PeoplesF.cs`, `PeoplesF2.cs`, one job driver, `JobDriver_PeoplesF`): the mast, the wire-trader (components
  at a fifth over their worth, or a caravan's news for fifty silver), the climb in a storm; the union's drill for a share
  (`deepResourceGrid`, two in five to the union; the colony's hand hurt one shift in twenty, `HarmKinds.UnionDrill`), the
  assayer's crate (set down by `Couriers.Loot`), the strike (a visit, kind `unionStrike`, called on a season's look in
  seven; `Patch_UnionStrikeCaravans`, `Patch_UnionStrikeVisitors`, `Patch_UnionStrikeTown` stall its trade; settled at
  the gate or after a month); the census walked bed to bed, the papers (a visit, kind `republicPapers`, a year of a
  citizen's terms by `Patch_PapersPawnTerms` and `Patch_PapersTownTerms`, six in a hundred), the conscript (a visit,
  kind `conscript`: a caravan of one there and back by the world's roads, the envoys' way), the radio once a season
  (`RepublicRadio`, heard at a comms console or the mast, `Rimfolk_Thought_RadioPraised`, `_RadioDenounced`); the
  Fleet's shuttle (Royalty's, else drop pods) with a casket to sell, its salvage (`PlayCarry.Salvage`; chunks cut where
  they lie), the sleeper woken too late. Four asks, the patch on four world events, release B's leans
  (`ArisingMath.Lean`, 17 arguments: survivors raise masts or keep a ship's watches, a band digs or votes). Their callers
  come and go at an errand's pace (`LordJob_VisitOnErrand`, `PaceVisit.cs`: the game's visit with its travel on an
  errand, used by `HappeningHelpers.Visit` for every caller). Nothing new saved.
- **Release G: the Helix Works, the Lattice, the Choir of the Spire and the Sunken Vault** (`Tools/Tests/PeoplesGTests.cs`,
  "peoples, release G: "; docs/design/peoples.md, the section of that name; the second four of `docs/design/peoples-third.md`).
  `Rimfolk_HelixWorks` (spacer, outlander parent, calling `editors`), `Rimfolk_Lattice` (spacer, `mechanitors`),
  `Rimfolk_Choir` (spacer with the archotech's flavour, `listeners`), `Rimfolk_SunkenVault` (spacer, `vaultfolk`), from
  the player's active mods only, the first three at the height already (paces 9, 10 and 16, falling back only when cut
  off), the Vault the first people with `ageDeclines` (an age about every 4 years unsupplied, floor medieval, its vault
  suit patched with each age's pieces in its kinds' `ageArms`). The Works' kinds the most varied of all (34 xenotypes,
  about six in ten not baseliners); the Choir without armour. Callers (`Peoples/PeoplesG.cs`, `PeoplesG2.cs`, one job
  driver, `JobDriver_PeoplesG`, which keeps the one worked on still with a forced wait; `PeoplesGMath`): the Works'
  sample (the colonist with the rarest genes, `PeoplesGMath.Rarity`, a draw of `HediffDefOf.BloodLoss` 0.08, paid at
  the gate), gene work (one of ten gentle genes the colonist lacks and conflicts with nothing, `AddGene` as a xenogene
  with the game's xenogerm mark), the vat-keeper's case (medicine and drugs, with or without Biotech), the batch gone
  wrong (`Rimfolk_GeneFault` on the Works' own vat-grown, tended with `OutsiderTend`); the Lattice's repairs (the game's
  `MechRepairUtility`), its lost mech (relinked and walked home by a link-warden, or kept by a mechanitor who can take
  it, `CanControlMech`, as its overseer, -15), its part-trader (`PlayCarry.MechParts`), its turret (a mini-turret
  raised at the gate, with or without Biotech); the Choir's listening (three hours in a ring at the gathering spot,
  then `Rimfolk_Thought_ChoirCalm` or `_ChoirUnease` for everyone at home by `PeoplesGMath.Felt`: psychic sensitivity
  and the void's stirring, `Find.Anomaly.Level`), its keeper of the hum (`PlayCarry.Art` for the Spire's goods); the
  Vault's last goods for components and food, the lost craft taught at the colony's bench (`learnedHere`), and the
  child who never saw a sky (`DilemmaEffect_Join`). The Vault's supply is the peoples' memory's `gaveLearning`
  (`VaultSupply.Noted`: its barter, a gift, a craft taught, its ask of power cells by `Patch_FactionMemory.MissionEnded`,
  kind `vaultcells`). Four asks (the Choir's listener's stay a `HappeningWorker_MissionHost`, an hour each afternoon
  beside someone at their work, `Rimfolk_Thought_ChoirFollowed`), the patch on four world events, release B's leans
  (`ArisingMath.Lean`, 20 arguments: a band led by a psycaster of four or more listens, by a surgeon edits, by a
  mechanitor links; survivors on a fated quarter, `SaltVault`, come up from a shelter). Their callers at an errand's
  pace (`PeoplesG.Errand`, `LordJob_ExitMapBest` at `Pace.Errand` home). Nothing new saved; no harm rolled.
- **The peoples' own events, round 1** (11 November 2026; released 0.213.0; `docs/peoples-events-proposals.md`, items 10, 5, 47, 83, 51, 1,
  19, 17, 34 and 95, approved in full; `Source/ColonyCouncil/Peoples/Events/`, the pure rules in `PeopleEventsMath.cs`,
  `Tools/Tests/PeopleEventsTests.cs`, "the peoples' events: "). The player: "I'd first like more faction specific events,
  interactions etc. like this event i had with these gene guys who gave my pawn a new gene", and "also some
  faction-specific camps can be included in the events". Each only from a people of its calling at peace with the colony
  (`PeoplesD.Friendly`), in the Visitors group at the touchpoints' rates (base chance 0.5 to 0.8, 20 to 60 days apart),
  every age in its own form, played out on the map. Rounds 2 to 10 stay on the to-do list.
  - **Shared shapes, for the later rounds.** *The visitor who works on a colonist* (`PeopleWorkOn.cs`): release G's gene
    work made general: a JobDef with `PeopleWorkJob` (where the colonist is while it is done: `here` a forced wait, `bed`
    laid in the bed, `beside` walked to the place, `sky` out under the open sky; its mark: the healing cross, sparks, the
    hum, the storm, earth turned; its `PeopleWorkDone` handler), `JobDriver_PeopleWorkOn` (to them, wait until they are in
    place, the work with a bar, the handler), `JobDriver_PeopleKeep` for the colonist kept at a place; the order kept as
    one of the events' visits (`pev:work`, its place a thing or a cell: `Visit.cell`, saved), a worker pulled away sent
    again four times, given up after its hours with any silver paid given back. *Goods held in trust* (`PeopleTrust.cs`):
    `TrustCrate` (a sealed crate of goods, `Rimfolk_TrustCrate`, its contents its own; opened by its own button, sold or
    destroyed, it notes how in its record as it happens; burned by harm told at once), `TrustRecord` in the book, the fetch
    a visit (`pev:trust`), the verdict `PeopleEventsMath.Verdict`. *A reading of what the map holds* (`OldPlaces.cs`): the
    old places (a fogged room holding an ancient danger's caskets, sealed crates, hives or sleeping enemies; the tile's
    landmark, the game's and Vanilla Landmarks Expanded's; Geological Landforms' landform by name in code), `Reading` (the
    contents counted exactly: mechanoids by kind, fleshbeasts, hives and insects, caskets and those in them, crates) and
    its words (`ReadingParts`), `Open` (the fog lifted, the dormant woken with `CompCanBeDormant.WakeUp`, the caskets
    opened). *The legend beast trigger* (`LegendBeasts`: release D's quarry rule, the nemesis optional, `Tameable`,
    `EdgeToward`). *A camp kind with ways of its own* (`Camps/CampWorker.cs`): `CampKindDef.workerClass`, a `CampWorker`
    (its land, its site, its start, hour, day and night jobs, its going, its farewell's marks, its placeholders, its own
    asks' needs) hooked beside the land kinds' in `CampKindsLand.cs`, `Camp.Format`, `CampLook.FarewellText` and
    `CampAsks.AskBlocked`, and `Camp.workState` (a `CampWorkState`, saved with the camp). The events' visits dispatch
    through one line in `HappeningTracker.VisitsHour` (`PeopleEvents.Owns`).
  - **Gifts** come once a colonist each and never within 20 days of another (`PeopleEventsBook`: `gifts` "kind:id", the
    newest 120 kept, `lastGift`). *A beast for a colonist* (herders): `HerdersBeast.KindFor` (the land's animals,
    `BiomeAnimals.Of`, fitting `BeastFits`, the base game's horse, yak, dromedary, muffalo and alpaca beside them; ridable
    ones twice as likely with Giddy-Up), a young beast just grown; nine tenths of its worth, or one of the colony's young
    beasts worth half (`OurYoung`, it joins their party); tameness and obedience trained, the game's bond and master, led
    home (`RopeToPen` for a roamer, else following), the rider's supper (`pev:supper`, `Hosting.Meal`). *A limb fitted*
    (order): `OrderLimb.Need` (the missing part's recipe by the order's age, `LimbRecipe`: peg leg or wooden hand before
    the industrial age, simple prostheses after, never bionics), the colony's bed (`Bed`), the surgeon of Medicine 10 to
    16; the wood carried out for a wooden limb; the doctor at the bedside; `RecipeWorker.ApplyOnPawn` with the surgeon
    (the game's own success and failure), the chance on the card from `SurgeryOutcomeEffectDef.GetQuality`; a deed `aid`
    (a debt of honour by `FavoursOwed`) or, with medicine sent back, `gift`. *Storm-sense* (Conclave): a thunderstorm now
    (a weather with lightning), the most sensitive (`Hears`), an hour out under the sky by the colony's rod (`sky`), a
    lightning flash, `ChangePsylinkLevel(1)` and `PsycastPaths.Follow` (Staticlord, Frostshaper), or without Royalty A
    RimWorld of Magic's `BookOfStormBorn` handed over; silver, or a vial (needs the colony's rod; a `gift` deed). *A
    mechlink* (Lattice, Biotech): the colony's best mind and hands, `MechlinkImplant` on the brain, the mech walked in with
    them (`StarterMechs`) made the colony's with the colonist its overseer; silver or two subcores; a tribal colony's
    `Rimfolk_Thought_MechlinkStrange` (-3, three days, its mood hint). *A Gauranlen seed* (Mossborn, the ledger warm:
    `LedgerWarm`): the spot chosen by the game's targeting with the seed's own `CompPlantable.CanPlantAt`, or hers (away
    from buildings within the tree's reach), planted together (`DoPlant`, `ConnectToPawn`); without Ideology a healroot
    grove of nine; the promise reckoned with the ledger (`MossLedger.Reckon` calls `MossPromise.Reckoned`: kept +2, broken
    -6 and `wordBroken`).
  - **Crates held in trust** (league): six to ten crates of its age's goods (`CrateGoods`), set down by the stores by its
    porters (by drop pod for a league of the spacer age), the fetch 20 to 30 days on; for the fee, a tenth of their
    worth, or free. Good ink: the fee, +6 (+10 free), `keptWord`, a year of +3% prices with every league
    (`Patch_TrustTermsPawn`, `Patch_TrustTermsTown`). Red ink: -15, `robbed`, no league caravans for a season
    (`Patch_TrustRedInk`). One open with the league at a time; with the league gone or at war the trust lapses.
  - **What lies in the old place** (society): an unread old place, two fellows at the gate; let measure, they become a camp
    beside it (`Rimfolk_Camp_ScholarsMeasure`, `CampWorker_Measure`, four days, measuring by day at its walls), then the
    reading told in a letter, research (`DilemmaEffect_Research`, a share 0.3, 1200 at most), the place noted read; let
    open, `OldPlaces.Open` as they go.
  - **The hostel** (pilgrims; `Rimfolk_Camp_PilgrimHostel`, `CampWorker_Hostel`): called by a beat of the great
    pilgrimage and the holy year (`Patches/Rimfolk_PeopleEvents.xml`, `WorldEffect_Camp`); by the road where the tile has
    one; travellers of any people at peace every 8 to 16 hours, four at most, a night or two (`Arrivals.Visit` to its
    fire), their news from the facts service told and its place marked (`OutsiderTalk.Heard`); bread asked once and then
    carried out each morning; the blessing (a gathering, the pilgrims' cough at 0.05 through the budget); feuding peoples'
    travellers (goodwill -20 or less between them, never at war) quarrel once a stay, a brawl at the camp brawl's rate.
  - **The lantern post** (Wardens; `Rimfolk_Evt_LanternPost` makes the camp, `Rimfolk_Camp_LanternPost`,
    `CampWorker_LanternPost`): at the edge nearest the beast, ten days at most; trackers watch it by day, a keeper by the
    lantern at night; a warning when it comes within 30 cells of the colony (every 12 hours at most); the meat ask (a new
    errand word, `PlayCarry.Meat`); the trail ask (two hunters under `LordJob_AssaultThings`, the colonist's hunt, a day at
    most, skinned by them if it falls); once a stay the beast at their fire at night (0.12 a night) or a hound lost on the
    trail (0.06 a day); the beast fallen or the trail cold, the lantern out.
  - **Kill it or win it over** (Wardens and Circuit): a legend or an alpha, tameable; the hunt (release D's
    `WardensHunt.Hunt` with only the Wardens), the taming (the game's `Tame` designation and job from its own work giver,
    the tamer beside a day, `pev:coach`), or the bout (`JobDriver_PeopleBout`, `WardenWins` by Melee); the tamer's own
    tries for the Circuit (`pev:tame`, every two hours, six at most, `TameChance` the game's, the beast's revenge at its
    `GetManhunterOnTameFailChance`). Passed over -5, sided with +4, a bout's loser -2; a news line on the roads.
  - Nothing else is hurt by Rimfolk: the surgery, the fights at the fire, the hunt and the taming are the game's own.
    Saved: `PeopleEventsBook` (gifts, trusts, the promise, places read; modelled in `Tools/save_estimate.py`) and a
    camp's `workState`. Dev actions "Peoples' events: ...". The Almanac's peoples' pages, *Of their own: gifts, trust and
    camps*.

### Peoples whose age changes

The player's words (8 November 2026): "different generations or time spans represented in factions, or that the
factions actually kind of scale also with time", on the two ways offered "also changing over time: do both", and "our
older factions should also be able to grow and develop over time to reach higher research levels". The first piece of
`docs/design/peoples-third.md`, "Ages that change over time". The game keeps a faction's def tech level for good;
Rimfolk keeps a people's age now beside it and reads that wherever it asks about a people's ways and means.

- **The record** (`Peoples/PeopleAges.cs`: `PeopleAgeRecord`, `PeopleAgeBook`, a game component of its own): one a people
  of Rimfolk's (the twenty-three and every one that arose in their ways), made the first time the region's day looks at it:
  its age now (0 tribal to 3 spacer), the age it began in (`Peoples.BeganIn`: its def's, or for one that arose the age of
  what it came from, as release B gave it), its progress (-1 falls back an age, +1 rises one, starting from a head start
  of up to a fifth by its id), when it was first heard of, looked at and last changed, the age before, and its heading
  and why. `PeopleAgesMath.MaxRecords` (40) kept, gone peoples dropped on saving; modelled in `Tools/save_estimate.py`.
  `Peoples.AgeOf` reads it (with the setting on); `Peoples.TechOf` gives Rimfolk's reads of a people's tech level the
  age's own whenever it isn't the def's.
- **The look**, once a season for each people on a day of its own (`PeopleAgesMath.LookDay` by its id), from
  `RegionBook.Daily` (no Sched slot): the one rule, `PeopleAgesMath.Season`, pure and tested (`Tools/Tests/PeopleAgesTests.cs`,
  "peoples' ages: ").
  - *Its own pace.* A season's way toward the next age is `fate * step / (pace * 4)`: `pace` the years an age takes by its
    ways (the def's `agePace`), `fate` its own 0.8 to 1.25 (by its id), `step` 1.2 from tribal, 1 from medieval, 0.7 from
    industrial (the climb to the spacer age is the longest).
  - *The colony quickens it* (`Boost`, times its own pace, at most 3): trade with it over the past year (up to +1 at 5000
    silver), gifts of books, techprints, components and tools as it remembers them (up to +0.6 at 1500 silver), teaching
    (+0.4 for each of theirs who learned at the colony this year, +0.2 for each of their masters who taught the colony's
    people: an exchange of learning teaches both, at most +0.8), and an alliance (+0.5; a trade pact +0.25).
  - *At its limit* (the def's `ageLimit`, never below the age it began in) it is settled in its ways, at the spacer age
    "at the height of what anyone knows"; progress lost comes back up to nothing.
  - *Cut off* (`CutOff`, three signs each 0 to 1 added): no trade with anyone for years (from 2 years, whole at 4; a people
    the colony traded with this year is not alone), its towns burned (each that fell in a fight in two years half a sign,
    its last town all of it), at war with most of the world (from half the world's peoples, the colony counted, whole at
    85%). At 1.2 or more it doesn't rise and loses ground (`Severity`: half a pace at 1.2, all at 3; an age in 5 to 10
    years), down to its floor (the def's `ageFloor`, else one below the age it began in).
  - *The Sunken Vault's way* (the def's `ageDeclines`, `ageDeclineYears`): never rises on its own, loses an age every
    so many years unless supplied (components and tools given or sold to it, `SupplyFull` 1500 silver a year holds it).
    The Sunken Vault's own (release G): an age in about 4 years unsupplied, never below the medieval age; its supply is
    the peoples' memory's `gaveLearning` (`VaultSupply.Noted`): the components and food of its barter, given or sold, a
    lost craft taught at the colony and its ask of power cells.
  - Past +1 it rises an age (never past its limit), past -1 it falls back one (never past its floor), and its progress
    starts again from nothing.
- **What the rule reads**, all of it what Rimfolk already records (`PeopleAges.Deeds`): the trade record's lines with the
  people's name or a town of theirs over the year, or at least 300 silver for each fair trade the history holds
  (`deed:traded`); the peoples' memory of the colony's gifts of learning (a new deed, `gaveLearning`: books,
  techprints, components or tools in a gift the game gives, by caravan, the trade window's gift mode or pod,
  `Patch_PeopleAgeGiftThing` on `FactionGiftUtility.GiveGiftInternal` and the two `GiveGift`s; weighed a point for 60
  silver, read back the same way as it fades); the history's deeds over the year: `learnedHere` (a new deed, noted when
  the Conclave's apprentice of the sky or the guild's wander-year ends well, `MemoryHooks.MissionEnded`) and `fostered`
  (a ward fostered), and `taught` (their master teaching the colony's apprentice, a lesson at the gate, a ward abroad);
  the game's alliance or a pact (`Pacts.With`); the last trade with anyone (the trade record, the history, a trade or
  road world event of theirs running or ended); the ledger's fight ruins of theirs in two years (`LedgerRuin.Fight`)
  against their towns standing; and the world's peoples at war with them (`Facts.Counts`, the colony with them).
- **Each people's pace and limit** (years an age at its own pace, the highest age; each def has a line of why):
  the learned society 6.5, spacer; the Stormglass Conclave and the road league 7, spacer; the Kiln Guild 8 (medieval),
  spacer; the Signal Line 8, spacer; the Last Republic 9, spacer; the Wheel 10, spacer; the Ashen Banner 11 (medieval),
  spacer; the Deepwell Union 11, spacer; the Circuit of Tamers 12, spacer; the spacer enclave 8, the Helix Works 9, the
  Hollow Fleet and the Lattice 10 and the Choir of the Spire 16, spacer (at the height already: the peoples that can't
  rise, they can fall back to the industrial age); the Sunken Vault 12, spacer (it falls by its ways, above); the
  hospitaller order 12 (medieval), industrial (their faith keeps the flesh as it was made); the Lantern Wardens and the
  river folk 13 (medieval), industrial; the pilgrims 16 (medieval), industrial; the Quiet Bell 17 (medieval),
  industrial; the herders 20 (tribal), industrial; the Mossborn 24 (tribal), medieval.
- **The numbers** (`PeopleAgesTests`, 400 worlds of the twenty-three, each its own fate and head start, looked at every
  season): by themselves none rises an age in 5 years and 5.5 of 23 in 10. In a typical game (the colony trades 3500
  silver a year with the road league and holds a trade pact, 1500 with the guild with a small gift of tools and a
  journeyman's wander-year, 1200 with the hospitallers and is allied with them, 800 with the river folk and the society
  with a gift of books and one of the society's masters teaching): 2.1 rise in 5 years, 4.1 in 7.5 and 6.8 in 10, and
  half a people in 10 years (0.45, the guild) goes two ages. With all the colony's help (5000 silver a year, 1500 of
  gifts, two journeymen a year, an alliance) the guild goes from the medieval to the spacer age in 10 years in every
  world and in 7 in 75%. The herders and the Mossborn rise in none of the worlds in 10 years.
- **What follows from it.** Everything that already took the form of a people's age follows `Peoples.AgeOf`: its
  kinds' arms and kits of the age (`PeopleKindExtension.ageArms`), its gifts of the age (genes only from the industrial
  age, `PeoplesGearMath.GenesAge`), its camps' kits and what its camps know how to build (`CampKit`), its words and the
  form of each feature with it (`Ages.Of` reads `Peoples.TechOf`), its messengers and their lines, its letters' means
  (radio or rider), its notables' travel and calls, ransoms by pod or at the edge, its visitors' and missions' lowtech or
  hightech words, its town's stores (`PeopleTowns`, the loot by the age) and its traders' goods (below). Some 60 reads
  of a people's def tech level in Rimfolk's code now read `Peoples.TechOf` (which is the def's own for every other people).
- **Every age whole.** A people reaches every age from the one it began in (or any its template arises in) down to its
  floor and up to its limit (`PeopleAgesMath.Reachable`). Its kinds' sets for an age (`ageArms`) may now be a kit alone,
  worn by everyone of the kind; a set's arms are of no later age than the people's where one is (a mod's spacer rifle
  under the game's Gun tag stays out of an industrial people's hands). New sets for nine of the first seven peoples'
  fighting kinds (the hospitallers' sworn guards in flak with guns and their archers, the pilgrims', river folk's and herders'
  archers with guns, the league's guards and outriders with crossbows and swords in the medieval age and charge rifles in
  the spacer age, the society's proctors with maces or charge rifles, the enclave's marshals in flak with rifles in the
  industrial age). And as a pawn of a people living in another age than its kind was made for is made
  (`AgeArms.ToAge`, after its set), what it wears of a later age comes off (`PeopleAgesMath.Later`: guns and flak among
  the tribes and the medieval, spacer gear in the industrial age; its people's signature piece and its set's kit stay)
  and a bare body gets the age's plain clothes (tribal wear, or a shirt and trousers); a weapon of a later age, or a
  fighter's bow in an age of guns, gives way to the base game's arms of the age within the kind's means
  (`FallbackArms`). The tests check every kind of the fifteen in every age it can reach against the player's catalogue
  (`docs/player-mods/`, active rows): armed by its set with a weapon of the age, a fighter at range with a gun from the
  industrial age on, or its weapons of another age replaced by the base game's; the age's plain clothes are the game's;
  a camp kit for every age.
- **The traders' goods** (`Patch_PeopleAgeStock`, a prefix and finalizer on `ThingSetMaker_TraderStock.Generate`, the
  one step every caravan's, town's and visiting trader's stock goes through): while a people's stock is made, each of its
  trader's stock generators' caps on what it makes (`maxTechLevelGenerate`, set for its own age) moves as far as its age
  moved (`PeopleAgesMath.ShiftedCap`: a cap left open stays for one that rose and closes at its age for one that fell
  back), and is put back at once.
- **Where the game's own tech level couldn't follow** (it reads the def's field inside its own methods, which only a
  transpiler could change): what its traders buy (`maxTechLevelBuy`, read at trade time), the stuff of its stock and of
  the game's own gear for its pawns (`GenStuff` by the def's tech level), its raids' arrival (drop pods from the
  industrial age, `PawnsArrivalModeWorker`), the game's own base when a town's plan doesn't fit the land, and quests that
  pick a people by tech level. The game's pawn generation reads its kinds' tags, not the faction's tech level, so a
  people's gear follows through Rimfolk's sets and the every-age pass. Their towns' plans are the same in every age.
- **Seen in play.** A letter for each change (`PeopleAgeWords.Tell`, through `Tell.Letter`, positive for a rise,
  neutral for a fall, looking at their nearest town): the colony's means of hearing it (`Ages.Form`, the founding's
  word), what they learned or lost by the age, their leader's words in their own voice by their calling (fifteen of each
  way), what of it was the colony's doing (its largest part) or why they fell back, and what the colony will see of it;
  and the history's line (`world:age`). Their card (`CardKind.People`, now) and the region's page of peoples give their
  age and heading with why ("medieval age, rising: trades with you, learns from you"; "industrial age, falling back: no
  trade with anyone for years"; "medieval age, settled in its ways"), and when they last changed. Their next visitors
  and traders show it in their gear and goods.
- **Setting**: `peopleAges` ("Peoples' ages change", the region's page, on). Off: every people lives in the age it began
  in, and nothing moves; the records stay for when it is on again.
- **Dev actions**: "Peoples: every people's age and progress (log)" (its age, floor and limit, progress, heading, pace
  and fate, everything the rule reads for it this season, and what the next season gives), "a people up an age now
  (testing)...", "a people down an age now (testing)..." (the letter as the years would bring it), "every people's
  season now (testing)".

### The colony's animals with powers

The player's pick "magic and powers" (7 November 2026, built without a proposal round): four parts that share one pass
(`Sched.RarePowers`, tick 227 of the 250-tick cycle; its hour on the pass at tick 227 of the hour, its day in the first
hour of the day; `Animals/AnimalPowers.cs`, timed as `Pass.RarePowers`) and one saved book (`AnimalPowersBook`, a
GameComponent). The numbers are pure (`Animals/AnimalPowersMath.cs`; `Tools/Tests/AnimalPowersTests.cs`, "animal
powers: "). No Harmony patch, no letter: news, the chronicle, journals, moods, glows and one-sentence words.

- **Pokémon types at home** (`Integrations/PokeWorldTypes.cs`; PokéWorld, types by `PokeWorldLink.TypesOf`). Only the
  colony's own, spawned on a home map, up and not in a mental state; counted once an hour by species (`MaskOf`), run
  every 250 ticks. "Rests" is not walking (`pather.Moving`). Fire: `GenTemperature.PushHeat` into the room it rests in,
  6 heat a second times its body size (0.5 to 1.5) through the pass, only while the room is under 21 °C and never past
  it (`AnimalPowersMath.HeatPush` stops at the mark: the game adds energy over the room's cells), nothing outdoors, two
  a room. Ice: the same, cooling a room over 23 °C, never below. Grass: crops (sowable, in a growing zone or a plant
  grower) within 2.9 cells grow a quarter faster by their own rate (`GrowthPush`: a quarter of `1/(60000 growDays)` times
  `GrowthRate` for 250 ticks), only while plants are awake (the game's own resting hours), one push a crop a pass.
  Electric: a battery of the colony's own within one cell (`CompPowerBattery.AddEnergy`) gets 100 W. Psychic: a colonist
  within 6 cells in its sight, under their minor break threshold or within 5 points of it, gets `Rimfolk_PW_Calmed` (+5,
  half a day); one in two days a colonist, one a day a Pokémon (`calmTicks`, by ThingID). Fighting: `JoyGiver_PokemonSpar`
  (`Gaming_Dexterity`, base chance 2): a grown colonist who can fight, not hurting, no danger on the map, goes to a free
  Fighting type (their own first) and spars 900 to 1,500 ticks (`JobDriver_PokemonSpar`: the game's lunge each way in
  turn, 15 melee experience a swing of theirs; the Pokémon holds still in `JobDriver_StayWith`); at the end
  `Harm.Roll(pawn, 1/25, HurtClass.Bout)` may land a bruise of 3 to 6 (`Harm.Injure`, under the shared cap), said and told
  at `Importance.Important`. Water: a fire within 2.9 cells takes 40 extinguishing damage a pass; an idle one jogs to a
  fire on the home area within 10 cells. Each shows a glow in view (the game's heat glow, a tinted lightning glow,
  micro sparks, a splash) and, once a day at most for each power on a map and by a chance of one in eight, the nearest
  colonist who sees it says a word (`Rimfolk_Pool_PW_Say*`). Settings `pokemonTypes` and its six parts.
- **Familiars** (`Integrations/MagicFamiliars.cs`; A RimWorld of Magic, read by its defs' names: `TM_Mana`,
  `TM_ArcaneWeakness`, the trait `Faceless`, checked against its 1.6 source). A mage is a grown colonist with an inner
  life and the mana need, not faceless. Bound by the council's answer (`Rimfolk_Wish_Familiar`, `WishWorker_Familiar`:
  promised, a `FamiliarBinding` waits) or the mage's own choice (a mage bonded to one of the colony's animals, one day in
  four). A binding begins when the mage is free for a play-out, from eight in the morning to nine at night, no danger, the
  animal awake and reachable; `JobDriver_BindFamiliar`: up to it, an hour beside it (`BindingTicks` 3,000; it stays
  facing them), a glow between them, then `Bound` (named if it had no name, news, the chronicle, a journal line, +3 for
  5 days). Dropped after 10 days or six tries. Every 250 ticks: the familiar glows faintly in view; within 12 cells of
  its mage, 0.0004 mana (`Need.CurLevel`, never above `MaxLevel`) and the hediff `Rimfolk_FamiliarNear`
  (`IncomingDamageFactor` 0.95, renewed while near, gone 700 ticks after). Its death: `Rimfolk_Fam_Died` (-12, 15 days),
  the mana emptied, `TM_ArcaneWeakness` +4, told at `Importance.Important`, the chronicle and the journal. One a mage;
  never an animal bonded to someone else, not flesh, or of the mod's own (its summoned creatures). Setting `familiars`.
- **Omen animals** (`Animals/OmenAnimals.cs`). Each hour, a colony animal on a home map born within two hours, not seen
  before: its sign now (`SignOf`: the game's Eclipse, then its Aurora, a shiny Pokémon, a calendar day falling today
  that is a tradition, the founding, the player's own or kept before), at most one in 20 days and three living in a
  colony, half the births on a kept day (by the animal's own seeded roll, so a reload doesn't roll it again). Named by
  its keeper (`HerdStory.Keeper`; half the time a name from `Rimfolk_Pool_Omen_Names` by its sign), the news, the
  chronicle, the keeper's journal, the name said over it and a word back from whoever is with them. While one thrives
  (alive, up, not ill or starving: a per-map cache each hour), `Rimfolk_Omen_Thrives` (+2, a situational mood named for
  it, `Thought_OmenThrives`) for its colony; its death `Rimfolk_Omen_Died` (-4, 5 days) for everyone on its home map,
  told and in the chronicle. Sold or released, let go without ill luck. Saved: the living ones (`omens`) and the last
  omen's tick. Setting `omenAnimals`.
- **Sacred animals** (`Animals/SacredAnimals.cs`; Ideology). The kinds are the colony's faith's `VeneratedAnimals`; the
  game's rules (hunting, slaughter, the meat, a tame one's death) stay. Each hour: a fresh corpse (dead within two
  hours) on a home map of an animal that wasn't the colony's, of a kind a colonist's own faith venerates, gives those
  colonists `Rimfolk_Sacred_Fell` (-2, 3 days, three at most), the news, and a word at the body (once an hour a map); a
  hunt designation on one seen by a believer in view gets a word. The council's cull (`DilemmaEffect_Cull`) leaves out
  any animal a faith of the colony's venerates (`SacredAnimals.HeldSacred`), as `PlayCarry` already did for hunts.
  `Rimfolk_Dilemma_SacredDay` (`DilemmaWorker_SacredDay`, a custom: spring to autumn, a sacred animal on the map, asked of
  a believer): food carried out to it (`DilemmaEffect_FeedBeast`) and a gathering round it (`PlaySpot.Stranger`), +3 for
  3 days; or the food only; or not this year. Kept, it joins the calendar as every custom does
  (`Calendar/CalendarCustoms.cs`). Setting `sacredAnimals`.
- **Dev actions** (Debug actions, "Rimfolk", "Animal powers: ..."): what each part sees now (the log), the Pokémon types'
  pass now, a spar, a binding begun now, a familiar's death, an animal born under a sign, the sacred animals' day asked.

### Alphas, nemeses, legends and great herds

The wild's alphas and bosses (the player's pick "D, alphas and bosses", 7 November 2026: built without a proposal
round). `Source/ColonyCouncil/Beasts/`, the pure rules in `BeastsMath.cs` (`Tools/Tests/BeastsTests.cs`, "beasts: "),
the words in `Languages/English/Keyed/Rimfolk_Beasts.xml`, the lines in `Defs/FlavorPoolDefs/Rimfolk_Pools_Beasts.xml`.
Animals are picked by what they are (`RaceProperties`: size, predator, herd animal, migration, insect, dryad, entity),
never by name; the land's own animals are read from each biome's own records (`BiomeDef.wildAnimals`, read once per
look in `GreatHerds.LandAnimals`), never `AllWildAnimals` or `CommonalityOfAnimal`, which a biome listing an animal
twice breaks. Each part has a rate on How much happens (`packAlphas`, `beastNemeses`, `regionLegends`, `greatHerds`,
0 to 200%: `BeastsMath.Rate`, `Gap` and `Chance`); presets at 50% and 125%. No Harmony patch of its own.

- **Pack alphas** (`PackAlphas.cs`). A pack is three or more of one hunting kind (`BeastsMath.PackKind`) within 14
  cells of each other, wild, up, seen and in no mental state (`FindPack`), none of it a story already (named, a
  nemesis, the beast the colony watches, a world event's). The day (`Daily`): with no alpha open at the home and 30 days
  since its last (`AlphaGapDays`), a quarter of the days a pack is there it gets one (`AlphaDayChance`). A big threat
  just come (`storyState.LastThreatBigTick`, looked at once within two hours, `WatchThreats`): a pack of the game's own
  manhunters gets one three times in ten (`ManhunterAlphaChance`, 15 days apart). The alpha is the best by
  `AlphaScore` (size, its prime, a male a little first), named from `Rimfolk_Pool_AlphaNames` in the voice of someone
  of the colony who sees it (a `NameSingle`, so the game draws it on the map), with `Rimfolk_PackAlpha` (incoming damage
  0.85, melee 1.15, meat and leather 1.25). The news for a plain pack (`CC_Alpha_Led`), a letter for manhunters
  (`CC_Alpha_LedManhunters`); a later letter once, when the pack threatens the colony (`Threatens`: manhunting, or a
  `PredatorHunt` job on one of the colony's people or animals). Every 250 ticks (`Rare`): dead, it is told (a letter if
  a threat letter went out, else the news), its pack scatters (`Scatter`: each of it up and wild, with manhunters every
  manhunter of its kind on the map, out of any mental state, each its own `LordJob_ExitMapNear` from where it stands),
  and its slayer (`BeastBook.Slayer`, the wounds' combat log) gets `Rimfolk_Alpha_Slain`, a journal line and the name
  `Rimfolk_Epithet_Packbreaker` (`EpithetTracker.Bestow`); tamed, its pack follows (`Follow`): from half a day after,
  one at a time (`FollowAfterDays`, then 0.6 to 1 day apart), the next of it on the map (or back from the world at the
  edge) walks to it (a Goto job re-given while it isn't there) and is the colony's within 7 cells
  (`InteractionWorker_RecruitAttempt.DoRecruit`, the alpha's master its own), six at most, one not in within two days
  passed over. Gone off the land, the news (flavor). Saved: `BeastBook.alphas` (`PackAlpha`, its pack by reference,
  `MaxAlphaRecords` 16, the ended first).
- **Animal nemeses** (`BeastNemeses.cs`), on the nemeses' own (`Strangers/Nemeses.cs`). Every 250 ticks a beast nemesis
  (announced or still being fought) up on a home map under 45% of its health (`BeastsMath.Flees`; never downed, dead or
  owned) leaves any mental state and runs for the nearest edge (its own `LordJob_ExitMapNear`, jogging); off the map it
  is kept in the world (`ForcefullyKeptPawns`) and comes back 6 to 16 days later at 100% (`ReturnDays`), twice at most
  (`MayReturn`), once healed to 60% and when the map has no threat on and none came in the last half day, at an entry cell; one time in three
  (`ForBlood`) it starts the game's own `Manhunter` state there, with a letter (`CC_BeastNem_Blood`); the nemeses tell
  the rest (`Returned`). Nemeses.cs names one that ran off unannounced as got away (`BeastNemeses.Fled`) instead of
  forgetting it, and never names a beast lying downed (`!x.Downed`). The hour (`Named`): a beast nemesis newly named
  (up, or away) that killed or maimed (`Grave`) gets `Rimfolk_BeastScars` (a mark, no stats), and three times in five
  (`OathChance`) the closest of those close to the one it hurt (`Close`: a partner or kin, a bond of 30 not a rivalry,
  an opinion of 60; grown, able to fight, not sworn already) swears (`Swear`): a line said aloud (`Rimfolk_Pool_BeastOath`),
  a message, the chronicle, a journal line, the spark "nemesis" for "settle the score", whose `CanHave` now counts an
  open oath (`BeastNemeses.Sworn`). While the beast is up on the sworn one's map, `Rimfolk_BeastOathFury` once a day.
  The oath ends (`Oaths`): kept (their own hand: `Rimfolk_Beast_OathKept`, the goal's counter), someone else's
  (`Rimfolk_Beast_OathOthers`, the counter too), tamed, vanished, or lapsed (the sworn one dead or gone); each a journal
  line. Saved: `BeastBook.flights` (`BeastFlight`, `MaxFlights` 12), `oaths` (`BeastOath`, `MaxOaths` 20), `noted`
  (`MaxNoted` 40).
- **Legends of the region** (`RegionLegend.cs`), the world event `Rimfolk_WS_Legend` (kind `legend`) with `LegendWorker`.
  Can start (`CanHappen`) when `BeastsMath.LegendDue` (the world's 40th day, 150 days after the last one ended at 100%,
  `BeastBook.legendEnded`) and a kind fits (`Kinds`: of each race its first animal kind, the dozen biggest beasts of 2.5
  or more whose comfortable warmth is within ten degrees of the home tile's, `LegendFits`; with PokéWorld its
  legendaries, read from its comps' attributes, once its own `LegendaryQuestsTracker` has a condition met:
  `PokeWorldLegends`). `Cast`: the kind by `LegendWeight` (its size squared), the beast made old (`AgeMin` to `AgeMax` of
  its years) with `Council_Legendary`, named from `Rimfolk_Pool_LegendNames` (a legendary Pokémon keeps its species'
  name), held by the event (`WorldSituation.Hold`); its ground's tile (`GroundTile`: land a settlement could stand on,
  nothing on it, 4 to 12 tiles off, within reach of the home, hills and woods first); a friendly people's nearest town
  for {PLACE} (flag `town`). `Begin`: its ground, a `Site` with no faction of the part `Rimfolk_LegendGround`
  (`SitePartWorker_LegendGround`: its name, the arrival letter's part looking at it; no detection raids, not an attack),
  labelled "{NAME}'s ground"; the start letter looks at it. The bounty beat (requires `town`) sets `bounty` and its
  {COUNT}, paid on the "slain" ending by `WorldEffect_Silver` from afar. `Daily`: every five to nine days its ground
  moves 2 to 4 tiles (`MoveMinTiles` to `MoveMaxTiles`), unless the site has a map or a caravan of the colony is on it
  or bound for it; a message with the direction looks at the new site. A caravan's arrival makes the map with the beast
  on it (`GenStep_LegendGround`, linked to the site part: a standable open cell near the middle, unfogged). `Hourly`:
  dead by a colonist's hand, "slain" ({B} the slayer, {ITEM} the trophy's words); dead otherwise, "fell"; the colony's
  (tamed, or caught), "befriended" ({B} its master); lost or someone else's, "gone"; back in the world with no ground and
  up again (the caravan left it there), its ground made again near the last, with a message. Time runs out: "moved".
  `Ended`: `BeastBook.legendEnded`, the site removed unless it has a map, for "slain" the trophy beside the body (its
  butcher products, horns or tusks, else a quarter of its leather, 10 to 60) and the name
  `Rimfolk_Epithet_GiantSlayer`, for "befriended" `Rimfolk_Epithet_BeastSpeaker`; journal lines. The "slain" ending
  sings of it at home (`DilemmaEffect_Bonfire` with music, `Rimfolk_Pool_LegendSong`) and gives `Rimfolk_Legend_Slayer`
  and `Rimfolk_Legend_Fell`; "befriended" `Rimfolk_Legend_Befriended` and `Rimfolk_Legend_Awe`.
- **Great herds** (`GreatHerds.cs`). The day: each new season (year and season, `BeastHome.herdSeason`) decides its
  great herd, spring and fall (`Migrates`) six times in ten at 100% (`SeasonChance`), on day 2 to 12 of it
  (`PlannedDay`); put off a day while a threat is on. `Start`: a herd kind (`HerdKind`: a herd animal that can migrate,
  never a predator, an insect or a dryad, 0.9 body or more, fit for the season's weather; a Pokémon only as
  `PokeWorldLink.Allows`), the land's own three times likelier (`HerdKindWeight`), `GreatCount` head (6 to 24, fewer the
  bigger, 60 bodies at most), spawned near an entry cell and walked to the farthest reachable edge
  (`LordJob_ExitMapNear`, walking), as `IncidentWorker_HerdMigration` does; a letter by the season and the hunting
  season (`Rimfolk_Evt_HerdCrossing` fired when its worker can, the council's own question). Every 250 ticks, each home
  map's groups of `LordJob_ExitMapNear` with four or more wild animals of one kind (the game's migrations too) are
  watched (unsaved `HerdWatch`): spooked (`Spooked`) by one of it hurt in the last 250 ticks (`lastHarmTick`) or found
  dead since the last look, a projectile within 9 cells, or a fire within 7 (once a herd), at `SpookChance` times the
  rate, it stampedes (`Stampede`: those not in a mental state, a new group sprinting for the edge cell nearest the
  point across the map from what spooked it, from the nearest humanlike drafted, hunting or fighting within 40 cells
  of the hurt one, a projectile's launcher, or the fire), told at once (`Tell.Message`, threat). For 1.2 hours
  (`StampedeHours`) each runner of 1.2 body or more knocks down someone smaller than half again its size whose cell lies
  within 1.3 of its way since the last look (`SegmentDistSq`; once a stampede for each, three at most): only with
  everyday hurts on, `Harm.May` and `Harm.Chance(TrampleChance)`, a blunt blow (`TrampleDamage`, 6 to 16 by its size)
  from the runner, `Harm.Note`, and for one of the colony or its guests a message; and plants of growing zones on its
  way, a fifth of them, twelve at most (`Plant.Destroy`), told in the news once it is over. A herd of six or more in
  view and no threat on (once a herd, looked at hourly): up to three of the colony within 32 cells with sight of it and
  at ease (no job, wandering, waiting, at leisure, hauling or cleaning, not ordered, in no group) take
  `Rimfolk_WatchHerd` (`JobDriver_WatchHerd`: face the nearest of it, 1,200 ticks, resuming what they were at), one says
  so (`Rimfolk_Pool_HerdPasses`), each gets `Rimfolk_Herd_Watched`. Saved: each home's season and the alphas' times in
  `BeastBook.homes` (`BeastHome`).
- **The clock** (`BeastBook`, a GameComponent; an older save gets an empty one): every 250 ticks at `Sched.RareBeasts`
  (193: `PackAlphas.Rare`, `WatchThreats`, `BeastNemeses.Rare`, `GreatHerds.Rare`, each cheap with nothing there), its
  hour on the same tick (`Pass.Beasts`: alphas' threats and sightings, nemeses' returns, oaths), its day in the first hour
  of the day (alphas and herds per home, the nemeses' flights pruned, the caps).
- **Harm** (`Tools/Balance --harm`, `BeastSim.cs`): about 0.019 hurts a colonist-year from stampedes and 0.007 from beasts
  come back for blood at 100%, 0.025 in all, beside a raid's 1.4 to 2.0 and Rimfolk's everyday hurts' 0.26 to 0.50. An
  alpha adds none of its own; a legend hurts only those who go to its ground.
- **Dev mode** (`BeastsDebug.cs`, "Beasts: ..."): a wild pack led by an alpha, manhunters led by one, the alpha tamed,
  its pack in now, a beast nemesis made here (maimed, sworn against), it flees now, back now; a legend now, it moves, it
  walks onto this map; a great herd now, the herd stampedes; what stands now in the log.

### Letters that arrive in days and bring something (the player's decision 12, 6 November 2026)

In the player's save Stace wrote three letters to notables in 18 days; each leg took 12 to 14 days (the towns are over
fifty tiles off, and a leg went at the other people's walking pace, twelve days at most), and the one answer was "Your
letter came. We are well enough, thank you." and "It changed little between the colony and Blash", 26 days after it was
written. Now (`World/LetterMath.cs`, pure and tested in `LettersPetitionsTests`; wired in `World/NeighbourLetters.cs`):

- **By the colony's means.** A letter goes by the colony's age (`Ages.Ours`, `LetterMath.MeansOf`): runners (tribal), a
  rider (medieval), a courier (industrial), a courier by shuttle (spacer); a call on the comms console is at once. Each
  leg is half a day plus 0.09, 0.06, 0.04 or 0.015 days a tile, at most six, five, four or two days (`LegDays`); the
  answer comes back the same way (`backDays`), and the courier tracker still brings it to the gate by a messenger of
  theirs (`Couriers.MailAnswer`). Before (by the other people's age) and after (by the colony's), a leg at 10, 25, 50 and 80 tiles: tribal 4.4, 10.4, 12, 12
  days before, 1.4, 2.8, 5, 6 now; medieval 3.7, 8.7, 12, 12 before, 1.1, 2, 3.5, 5 now; industrial 2.6, 5.9, 11.4, 12
  before, 0.9, 1.5, 2.5, 3.7 now; spacer 1.6, 3.4, 6.4, 10 before, 0.65, 0.9, 1.25, 1.7 now. The save's letter: 12 days a
  leg before, under three by courier. A letter carried home by one of their people at the colony goes at their means;
  a call's "how far they are" (when a guest or raiders could come) at theirs too. Letters already on the road keep the
  day they were given (`due`, `backDays` saved). The letters page says by which means it is on the road, never when.
- **What an answer brings** (`LetterMath.Brings`), for the purposes whose answer was words only: greetings answered
  warmly bring a token gift (50 to 100 silver's worth by the colony's wealth, `Loot.Make`) in the messenger's pack,
  kindly or coolly how their town is faring (`RegionFortunes.Line`, else a piece of news near them, else that the roads
  are quiet); condolences taken warmly or kindly are remembered by their people (the "mourned" deed, as before, now
  said); a warning heeded kindly or coolly is remembered ("warned"), heeded warmly it is a debt of honour (the deed at
  weight 10, `LetterMath.HeededWarmly`, made when the answer reaches the colony: `NeighbourLetter.owed`, saved, then
  `Owed`, through `FavoursOwed.Quietly` so the answer's own words tell it once), where debts of honour are kept
  (`CanOwe`; else remembered). Since 10 November 2026 a warning weighs what its threat was worth to them, one debt from
  warnings a season, and a greeting's token comes once a season from each notable (below, "Diplomacy kept fair").
  News, help, a visit and stage 2's purposes (a favour, a pact, a truce, a ransom, an envoy,
  a ward, a match, an oath, a feast) bring what they always did.
- **Regard in words.** The answer's last line says how far it moved them, from their regard before and after
  (`LetterMath.Move`: into another band, "civil before, friendly now"; a good deal, a shade, nothing, a shade less;
  `CC_LetterRegard_*`), the writer named on a warm answer, and their people's goodwill when it rose. It replaces the
  old tone line (`CC_Letter_Outcome_*`, kept for answers already written).
- **A refusal with a reason.** A curt answer or a refusal says why (`LetterMath.Why`: the heaviest of what counted
  against it in `NotableMath.Score`: a people at war first, then their regard of the colony or the writer, the writer's
  words, their nature, hard times on business, the same asked lately, a call, a great deal asked, else a bad day), and
  so does an invitation not taken up, or one taken up with nobody free to travel. A truce, a ransom, an envoy, a ward, a
  match and an oath give their own reasons (`LetterMath.OwnReasons`) and get no second one.

#### Where the colony and a camp meet (0.172.1)

After the player's report ("i decided to pay them and my pawn started walking to the other side of the map ... my pawn
should pay them once they are closer. these thoughts must be applied to all such kinds of events"): whatever the colony
carries to a camp (silver paid for an ask or a land work, meals, a supper, provisions, a gift) goes to the camp's fire
only while the camp is near (its fire within 35 cells of the colony's gate, `CampMeetMath.Far`). A camp further off sends
the one of its people nearest the gate to meet the colonist there (`Camps/CampMeet.cs`: a walk at an errand's pace and a
wait of two hours), and the errand waits until they come ("one of the camp is coming to the gate for it"); a camper
already at the gate, as the one who brings the colony's load of wood, takes it. The answers' words say "the gate, where
one of the camp meets them" for such a camp. Going to the camp to learn a craft, to visit or to help stays a walk to it.

### How fast Rimfolk's people go (0.171.1)

The game's "walk" urgency is half the ordinary pace and "amble" a third; the colony's own people go about their work at
the ordinary pace ("jog"). After the player's report ("some of the npcs you create, including the earlier couriers, seem
to walk only quite slowly on the map, never as fast as my colonists"), every errand and trip of Rimfolk's goes at the
ordinary pace (`Pace.Errand`): couriers and the post's riders, envoys, ransom, match, truce, fealty and feast parties,
wards, visitors and camps coming and going, people sent somewhere, someone freed or ransomed walking to the gate. Their
lords' travel uses `LordToil_TravelOnErrand` (the game's own travel, whose duty would walk at half speed, set to the
ordinary pace). Kept slower on purpose: a stroll or a dawn walk, a wander about a camp, browsing a market stall, a herd,
a pack or a pet on its own business, a group keeping together in a play-out, someone carrying another, the banished
walking out.

## The post: letters that travel with someone (the player's request, 8 November 2026)

The player: "the couriers it feels a bit weird being able to ... send a letter to some civilization and then a courier
just randomly appears out of nowhere ... It should be more opportunistic, I guess, dynamic", "visitors and other random
characters should perhaps also be able to take letters when going their direction", and the same day "i should also have
some sort of diplomatic range, right? until comms". Step 1 of `docs/design/post-and-letters.md`, in `Post/` (pure rules in
`PostMath.cs`, `PostTests`, "the post: ", 245 checks). Under **The post: letters travel with someone** (`post`, the
neighbours' section, on, needs the letters) and **The post's pace** (`postPace`: Seldom, As usual, Often).

- **The outbox.** A letter written goes in the mailbag (`Rimfolk_Mailbag`, a spot of the Misc tab drawn with its own post and bag
  (0.179.2, drawn at 1.5 its cell since 0.202.1), `Building_Mailbag`; the one nearest the gate counts; none placed, the
  gate cell, `PlaySpots.GateCell`) as a neighbour letter in the new stage `Outbox` (`Outbox.Put`). Since 10 November 2026
  the writer carries it there first (`Outbox.Bring` from `Written`, the job `Rimfolk_PostPutIn`; "The letter carried and
  read" below). Its pane lists each letter (to whom, what for, by whom, how it is likely to leave: `PostWords.Likely`; or
  that its writer is bringing it), the letters waiting at the gate for a go-between or a messenger, and the mail coming
  in; its buttons send one with the colony's own rider, take one back or read one. The old "three under way, one each" becomes one to
  each notable and `PostMath.MaxOpen` (12) open at once with the post: the outbox itself keeps letters from all leaving at
  once (NotableMath.MaxOpen, 3, without it).
- **Anyone going that way takes them** (`MailWatch`, every 250 ticks on the letters' own pass, `Sched.RareNeighbours`,
  only while there is a letter waiting, mail in or the post rider on a map). Any lord of a people at peace with the colony
  on a home map whose job goes about the road (`PostMath.CarriesMail`: not a raid, a war band, a siege, a gathering, a
  ceremony) is a carrier: traders, visitors and Hospitality's guests (`LordJob_VisitColony` by name), a camp
  (`LordJob_Camp`), pilgrims, travellers passing, a people's messengers and envoys (`PostMath.CarrierOf`, by the job's
  name). When one turns to leave (`Outsiders.Leaving`: its lord's exit toil, an exit duty, a job that leaves the map), the
  letters on their way are kept for one of them (not the trader, the nearest the mailbag), who walks there
  (`Rimfolk_PostTake`, two and a half seconds with a bar) and takes them; a lone outsider walking off does the same. The
  colony's own caravan forming (`LordJob_FormAndSendCaravan` while it gathers its goods) sends one of its people for the
  letters the way it leaves (`ExitSpot`); they go once the caravan is out on the world, and back in the bag if it never
  leaves. **On their way** (`PostMath.OnTheirWay`): their own people's towns; a town along the road to where they're
  going (near their destination, or no further and within 35 degrees of the way there); else within 60 degrees of the
  way they leave the map, read as a world heading from the map's middle to their exit cell (a map's north is the world's).
  A town at the door (under two tiles) is on everyone's way. The post rider takes every letter to the peoples the post
  serves (at peace, medieval or later) within range or by relay; a carrier by shuttle anything within reach.
- **Arrival.** Taken, the letter is on the road (`Travelling`) for the land's own days by the carrier's means
  (`PostReach.Days`, below), relayed when far, and read when it gets there (the old `Read`); the answer comes back over the
  same days. Who took it and how is kept on the letter (`carrier`, `carrierName`, `carrierMeans`, `relayName`) and said on
  the letters page and the cards.
- **A regular post** (`PostRider`, on the neighbours' hour). The post's age is what the colony and the best of the region's
  peoples at peace (a town within 40 tiles) share (`PostMath.PostAge`): none for a tribe; a post rider every 7 to 14 days in
  the medieval age, a mail run every 3 to 7 in the industrial, a shuttle every 2 to 4 in the spacer, times 1.5 seldom or
  0.6 often. It comes by day when the map is safe, from the nearest people of that age at peace: one of their people sent
  on the road, made new each time of a kind drawn from their range (`CarrierKinds.Person`; until 10 November 2026 one of
  their lighter caravan hands, `Couriers.PersonKind`), by the way in nearest the mailbag (a road a little preferred;
  until then a road at the edge wherever it was), with a mount drawn from their caravans' beasts of body size 1.2 or more
  that Giddy-Up lets be ridden and the land and season allow (`CarrierKinds.Mount`), else a horse, else on foot; in the
  spacer age by drop pod at the mailbag. With Giddy-Up 2 the rider sits on the mount as they come on the map, the way Giddy-Up brings its own
  riders in (`Integrations/GiddyUpMounts.cs`, since 0.202.2: the mount's obedience trained by the rider, then
  `GiddyUp.MountUtility.GoMount(rider, animal, GiveJobMethod.Instant)` found by name; the "Mount" job by name only where
  that can't be found, since the group's duties often cut that job off and riders walked beside their beasts);
  otherwise they lead the beast. **Porters and couriers ride too** (0.202.2, the player: "porters still frequently appear
  to come without mounts and being on them"): with Giddy-Up, a medieval or industrial people's couriers come on a mount
  each (`CourierMath.Rides`, `CarrierKinds.Mount`), kept on the trip as `mounts` (saved; `mounts[i]` is `people[i]`'s), never loaded with goods (the
  people and the pack animal carry), mounted as the group forms; a mount nobody sits on any more leaves with its own
  exit lord when the trip ends, a ridden one goes with its rider. **The letter's writer** is the colony's best with
  words by default (`NeighbourLetters.DefaultWriter`: the highest Social, the speaker first among equals; the
  choice menus list writers the same way, `ByWords`; the player: "it should also auto select the highest level social
  pawn to write the letter"). Feast invitations keep the steward first. `LordJob_PostRider`: straight to their place
  beside the mailbag, wait there while the mail is set down and the letters taken (from the saddle), then ride on at once
  by the nearest way (four hours at the most; until 10 November 2026 half an hour more round the bag, wandering); hurt or
  their people turned hostile, they leave defending themselves.
- **The colony's own rider** (`OwnRiders`). "By our own rider" in the letter's dialog (with who rides), or the mailbag's
  button: the colonist takes the letter from the mailbag (`Rimfolk_RiderSetOut`), walks to the edge with the colony's
  fastest animal big enough to ride following them (`FollowClose`), and sets out as a caravan of their own (with the mount
  if it kept up) straight to the town, as the envoy abroad does. At the town the letter is read (`ReadByRider`) and the
  answer, and what it sends, ride home in their pack after a few hours; it opens when they're back on the home's map, with
  "brought this answer home by hand". The range doesn't bind a rider; the road's length does. The roads' dangers are the
  game's own caravan events; nothing is rolled here. Turned back by the player, the letter is back in the bag; lost on the
  road, the letter is lost with them (said). Since 11 November 2026 they take supplies chosen with the send and gather
  them before they go ("Supplies for the colony's own rider" below).
- **Mail comes in the same way** (`MailIn`, `PostBook.incoming`). An answer of words only (`things.Count == 0`, not to a
  people at war) goes in the post from the day it reaches the region; so do the world's letters carried to the colony:
  a town's letter (`Colonies/TownsAfter.cs`), the colony's envoy's (`Diplomacy/EnvoysAbroad.cs`) and ward's
  (`Diplomacy/WardsAbroad.cs`) letters from abroad (`MailIn.FromAbroad`, timed by their people's means over the land). A
  group of outsiders seen coming in (within eight hours of first being seen) brings the mail from their way, by the same
  rule from the edge they came in by, or from their own people; the post rider brings all the post's; one of them walks it
  to the mailbag (`Rimfolk_PostDrop`) and each letter opens as they set it down, looking at them. An invited guest brings
  their own answer if it is still in the post. When nobody has come for longer than is reasonable for its kind
  (`PostMath.MessengerWaitDays`: urgent, help, a warning, a truce, a ransom, half a day; business three days; ordinary
  letters eight, twelve with a regular post), a messenger of the writer's people brings it (`Couriers.MailAnswer`, as
  before; the letter then waits for that trip). Sixteen waiting at most: past it the oldest goes by messenger.
- **The comms console** stays on demand, to peoples with radio: industrial and later by `Peoples.TechOf`, or a town within
  30 tiles of a town of the Signal Line (by its def's name, `Rimfolk_SignalLine*`, softly: the people is built in
  parallel) (`PostReach.Radio`). An aide takes a message as before; what a call promises in goods still comes by courier.
- **Writing takes a writer.** Those who can write are grown, free and can read by the game's own rule (`BookUtility.CanReadEver`);
  the writer sits at a table for about an hour as before. A tribal colony with the post gives a spoken message: no
  writing, the letter waits in the outbox as words (`spoken`), and when a carrier comes for it they wait at the mailbag
  up to an hour and a half while the speaker (or anyone free who can talk) walks over and says it (`Rimfolk_PostSpeak`,
  ten seconds face to face, a line each).
- **Diplomatic range until radio** (`PostReach`, `PostMath.RangeDays`, `Band`, `Relay`, `LegDays`, `TileDays`). Reach is the
  world's own travel time: a walking caravan's ticks over the game's path (the layer's `Pather.FindPath` with no caravan, timed by
  `CaravanArrivalTimeEstimator` at the default pace from now, as the route planner does: terrain, roads and rivers, the season
  and snow, night rests), cached three hours of the game, at most two new paths a
  frame from a window; then the carrier's means takes a share of it (on foot 0.8, mounted 0.5, a vehicle 0.3, half a day to
  start) and a shuttle goes by the straight distance (two days at most). `TileDays` models the game's per-tile cost (and
  stands in when the game's path can't be read). The range is five days by the colony's runners, seven by riders, nine by
  vehicles (a tribe with an animal to ride counts as riders), half again with a Signal Line mast near, none for a spacer
  colony's shuttles. Within it (`Near`) anyone going that way reaches them; beyond it (`Far`) a letter is handed on through
  the relay with the fewest days in all (a town nearer than theirs of a people at peace, goodwill 20 or more, within range
  of the colony and itself within range of the letter's town, a day at the relay), and a carrier takes it if the relay is
  on their way; out of reach (`Cut`: no relay, or no way by land) it goes only with their own people or someone whose
  road goes there. Letters by diplomacy's purposes follow it, being letters.
- **How to reach them now** (`PostWords.ReachLines`, a town's card under Who, the letter's dialog, the region map's
  tooltip): by radio; by shuttle; by someone of theirs here; at war, a go-between; within reach, about so many days on the
  road, by the next post, with their people on the map, or by the next caravan or traveller going that way; far, by relay
  through a town; out of reach until radio; and "or by your own rider, about so many days there". The region map draws a
  soft ring round a town far off (amber) or out of reach (grey) (`PostRing`, the hook for the diplomacy screen).
- **What moved to the outbox and what stayed.** Moved: every letter written to a notable by hand (all of
  `NeighbourLetters`' purposes, the diplomacy ones included: favours, pacts, truces with a people at peace, ransoms,
  envoys asked for, wards, matches, fealty, a town asked back); the answers of words only; a town's letter; the envoy's
  and ward's letters home. Stayed: letters to a people at war (a go-between under a white flag still comes for them, and
  their answers by messenger: a truce can't wait for travellers going into enemy land); answers that send goods (a token,
  the help asked, a debt paid: goods, not mail, by their messenger as before); a call's goods; someone of theirs at the
  colony carrying a letter home (Outsiders/, by hand); and the letters that tell what happened (a pact sworn or broken,
  fealty, a ward's arrival or death, an envoy's arrival, feasts): those are the game telling the player at once, not
  letters carried, and delaying them would let the map and the words disagree.
- **Old saves.** A letter waiting for a messenger whose trip never came or was settled goes in the outbox on its next hour;
  a messenger already coming takes it as before; letters on the road, and answers on their way by courier, come as they
  were. New fields load empty (`postId` -1). The post turned off: the outbox's letters get a messenger each, and the mail
  waiting goes by messenger.
- **Saved.** `PostBook` (a game component): `incoming` (16 at most), `rounds` (one a home), `rides` (one a letter with the
  colony's rider), `packs` (the supplies for each, since 11 November 2026), modelled in `save_estimate.py`; the letter's new fields. Nothing has a tick of its own: the watch rides on
  the letters' 250-tick pass, the rest on their hour.
- **Dev actions** ("Rimfolk"): the post rider now; a visitor group leaves now with the mail; every town's reach and the
  outbox (log); the mail waiting brought by a messenger now; the mail on the road here now.

### Asks answered (0.205.4)

The player: "the "asks waiting" information is really nice, but it should disappear once you have an answer ordered". A
world ask (`Dealings/WorldWrites.cs`) waits for the reply (purpose Dealing, topic "reply:ID"); now any letter of the
colony's to that notable under way since it opened (`WorldWrites.Writing`) also takes it out of the inbox's waiting
asks and holds off the silence, and a letter written to them since in another way means no silence penalty when the
answer days pass. The letter dialog opens on the reply when the notable waits for one (`WorldWrites.OpenAsk`), so the
answer is the first choice.

### The letter carried and read (the player's report, 10 November 2026; released 0.205.2)

The player: "i think i instructed a pawn to send a letter, the text appeared above but I can't find it in the mailbag? do
the pawns actually bring the letters to the bag also? i should be able to read the letter directly by clicking the
pop-up". Their letter was a warning to a people at war with the colony: by design it skips the mailbag (a go-between
under a white flag comes to the gate for it), but its message said only "a messenger will come to the gate", the
mailbag listed nothing, and a click on the message only jumped the camera. Letters that did go by the post went in the
mailbag the moment they were written, with nobody walking there. The pure rules in `PostMath.cs` (`Written`,
`WrittenKey`, `Bring`, `SectionOf`, `MayTake`, `GateHeadKey`, `GateLineKey`) and `Letters/LetterClickMath.cs`
(`HintKey`, `Opens`, `ClickMap`), linked; `Tools/Tests/LetterCarryTests.cs` ("the letter carried and read: ", their
save's case end to end).

- **The writer carries it to the mailbag.** A letter written for the post (`PostMath.Written`: at peace, the post on)
  goes in the outbox in its writer's hand (`NeighbourLetter.bringing`, saved, cleared once in): their next job from the
  table (queued after the writing, `Outbox.Bring`) is `Rimfolk_PostPutIn` (`JobDriver_PostPutIn`): they walk to the
  mailbag, or to the plain cell by the gate with none, put it in (a second and a half with a bar) and only then is it in
  the post (`Outbox.BroughtIn`, `Put`, with its "put the letter in the mailbag" message; the colony's own rider sets out
  from there). Until then the mailbag's list shows "Guido is bringing it" (`CC_Mail_Line_Bringing`), the letters page
  "is bringing the letter to the mailbag", and no carrier takes it (`PostMath.MayTake`; the watch counts only letters
  in, `Outbox.Any`). Cut off on the way (drafted, downed, gone from the map, a raid on), the letters' 250-tick pass
  (`Outbox.Bringing`, `PostMath.Bring`) sends them again once they're free; after four hours
  (`PostMath.BringFallbackTicks`; a walk under way finishes, at most eight), or at once when the writer is no longer the
  colony's, it goes in all the same, said without saying who did ("Guido's letter to Will is in the mailbag at the gate
  now", `CC_Mail_Msg_InBagLate`; an older save's letter moved to the outbox reads the same). Never lost, never stuck
  (tested over 2,000 writers drafted and cut off at random). A tribal colony's spoken message is as before: nothing to
  carry. The post turned off or their people turned hostile while it is carried: it waits at the gate as any other.
- **A letter that can't go by the post says why, and can be found.** Written to a people at war, "With their people at
  war with us it can't go with the post: a go-between under a white flag will come to the gate for it"
  (`CC_Letter_Msg_WrittenWar`; with the post off, `CC_Letter_Msg_WrittenWarNoPost`); with the post off, that it doesn't
  go in the mailbag and a messenger of theirs comes (`CC_Letter_Msg_Written`). Said once the go-between is on the way
  (none can come: the letter is let go with why, as before). The mailbag's pane gets a section "Waiting at the gate for a
  go-between:" (or "a messenger", or both; `PostMath.SectionOf`: waiting for a messenger, not to be handed to someone of
  theirs here), a line each with who comes for it or that they're at the gate now; its "Read a letter" lists them too
  ("(waiting at the gate)"), and shows with the post off. The letter itself still waits at the gate as before.
- **Click the pop-up to read.** The messages about a letter of the colony's written out in full ("has written", "put the
  letter in the mailbag", "is in the mailbag now", "handed to", "will come to the gate for it", the spoken message's
  "has the words ready") go through `Notify.LetterMessage` with the letter's id (through the teller as any other:
  `Tell.Message`'s `read`, `NewsItem.read`, not saved). As it is shown (`News.Show`), `LetterClick.Make` makes the game's
  message with "Click to read it." at its end, and `LetterClick.Shown` keeps it with the letter while it is on screen (a
  short-lived map by the message itself, 24 at most, let go once off the screen). `Patch_LetterMessageClick` (a prefix on
  `Message.Draw`, applied per class by `RimfolkPatches.ApplyAll`): the game draws each message on the root of the
