  interface before any window and answers its click later in the message's own small window; the prefix sees the left
  button going down on a kept message first, opens its exchange in `LetterReadWindow` and uses the event, so the camera
  doesn't jump. A right click still dismisses; any other message is the game's. Without the patch (not applied, broken,
  the deeper hooks off) the click jumps the camera as before and the message ends with where it can be read instead
  (`CC_LetterRead_Msg`, `_MsgPeople`). The on-screen panels' boxes behind the messages (`Hud/HudMessages.cs`) are drawn
  behind the game's own message, so a click there is the same click. Held for the evening's news, a message carries no
  hint (only one on screen opens anything).

### Straight to the mailbag, back in the saddle, a new face each time (the player's report, 10 November 2026; released 0.206.1)

The player: "the couriers that bring letters and material take an awkward routine around my base before delivering the
message a bit away from the base. if anything they should always walk to the mailbag directly, drop/pick up the message
or items. for the message they unmount and then they walk off map without remounting. i've been developing a lot of
letters with the stormriders, but the courier and mount looks always exactly the same. i'm not sure if this faction has
this uniform, but the courier should have look variety that makes sense within the faction, like for the other npcs they
create". The pure rules in `Couriers/CarrierMath.cs` (linked; `Tools/Tests/CarrierTests.cs`, "carriers: ", every one of
Rimfolk's peoples with the old rule beside the new); the game side in `Couriers/CarrierSpots.cs`, `CarrierKinds.cs` and
`CarrierLords.cs`, `Integrations/GiddyUpMounts.cs`.

What caused it:
- **The awkward routine.** A courier trip came in at a random edge cell (the game's own pick) and walked to the colony's
  gate cell (out from the colony's middle toward the nearest edge, up to a dozen steps past the home area), round the
  colony when it came in on the far side; the game's travel duty sends each of a group to a random cell within six of the
  spot and has them stand and wander in turn until the slowest is there; at the gate they wandered within three cells,
  and lingered half an hour more after their business (the post rider the same round the mailbag). With Giddy-Up, a rider
  given a job Giddy-Up doesn't know (setting mail or goods down, taking letters) within 25 cells of it "parks" first: in
  the colony's pen when one is within 50 cells, else a free cell near, dismounting there and walking the rest.
- **No remount.** The game's exit toil, as the group set off, cut every pawn's job short, the mount's "Mounted" job too,
  which sets its rider down; and Giddy-Up's own "mount up as the caravan heads out" asks the beast to have learned
  tameness, which a beast made for another people hasn't (only the colony's are made tame). So the rider walked off on
  foot, and the beast went its own way.
- **The same look.** Every carrier was already made new (`Arrivals.Make`, `forceGenerateNewPawn`; no world pawn came
  again, and nothing seeds the draw). The sameness was the kind: one of their caravans' lighter guards, which for many
  peoples is one kind (the League's guard, the Order's bowman, the Scholars' proctor) or none (the Enclave: always its
  ordinary member), often with their people's coat; and the beast: their caravans' beasts filtered by the land's
  pack-animal list, which in a temperate forest leaves the muffalo alone, else the horse every time.

What it does now:
- **Straight to the mailbag.** Couriers and porters, a go-between under a white flag (`LordJob_Courier`) and the post
  rider (`LordJob_PostRider`) do their business at the colony's mailbag (the one nearest the gate, `Outbox.Bag`), else the
  gate cell, else where traders leave goods (`CarrierMath.SpotOf`, `CarrierSpots.Spot`; the trip keeps `atBag`, saved).
  They come in by the way nearest it on foot (`CarrierSpots.EntryCell`: the game's flood fill out from the spot over
  walkable ground, so a wall or a river counts the way round; `CarrierMath.BestEntry`: the fewest steps, a road counted a
  fifth nearer; else the game's own random way in), walk straight to their own place beside it (`LordToil_CarrierTravel`, duty
  `Rimfolk_CarrierTravel`, `JobGiver_CarrierGoTo`: the `i`th place round the spot, `CarrierMath.RingOffset`, the cells
  beside it first, never the spot itself) and wait there (`Rimfolk_CarrierWait`, `JobGiver_CarrierWait`: a short wait
  facing it, looked at again; the courier's own duty ends in it). Goods are set down from their place onto the cells beside
  the bag, the nearest free one first, a pile of stacks going round it, never on the bag (`CarrierSpots.SetDownBeside`;
  an empty cell or one whose stack it tops up). Porters fetching from the stores walk there from the bag as before.
- **No lingering.** Their business done they leave at once (`CourierMath.LingerTicks` 0; a night's stay still keeps them
  to first light), by the nearest way off the map (the game's `JobGiver_ExitMapBest`). The waits that stay are the ones
  the business needs: handing over, a go-between waiting for the letter, an errand's courier waiting for what is carried
  out, porters waiting for the stores.
- **From the saddle at the bag, on foot into the colony.** Setting goods or mail down and taking letters are jobs Giddy-Up
  is told a rider may do mounted (`GiddyUpMounts.AllowInSaddle`: `JobDriver_Mounted.SetAllowedJob` by name for
  `Council_CourierDrop`, `Rimfolk_PostDrop`, `Rimfolk_PostTake`), so a rider rides up to the bag, sets it down and rides
  off, with no ride to the pen first (it also spares a trader's or visitor's rider Giddy-Up brought in, taking letters).
  Going into the stores or fetching someone is done on foot (`CarrierMath.OnFoot`): the rider gets off at the bag
  (`GiddyUpMounts.GetOff`: the beast's "Mounted" job ends, Giddy-Up's own end of it sets the rider down) and the beast
  waits in its place there.
- **Back in the saddle before leaving.** The group leaves by `LordToil_CarrierLeave` (the game's exit toil, but it never
  cuts short a beast carrying its rider or a rider getting on), duty `Rimfolk_CarrierLeave`: a rider not on their beast
  (`CarrierMounts.MountOf`: the trip's `mounts[i]` for `people[i]`, the post rider's beast) gets on at once beside it
  (`GiddyUpMounts.MountNow`), or walks over to it and gets on (Giddy-Up's own "Mount" job, `WalkAndMount`; the beast
  stands for them, `JobGiver_CarrierMountWait`), then rides off. On foot when the beast is gone (dead, downed, fled), out
  of reach, more than 60 cells off, or after an hour (`CarrierMath.Remount`, `RemountStep`); a beast whose rider can't
  come leaves by itself, never left on the map. Giddy-Up's own remount works again too: every arriving mount learns
  tameness as well as obedience (`GiddyUpMounts.Train`).
- **A new face each time, in the people's own range.** Who is sent (`CarrierKinds.Person`, `CarrierMath.KindPool`,
  `Pick`): drawn for each person of the trip from their people's caravans' guards (Trader groups) and their visitors,
  villagers and settlers (Peaceful groups), half and half, group by group as the game weighs them (commonality, then
  selection weight); light (combat power 75 or less; a people of warriors only sends its lightest and those within 30),
  grown, never a trader, a leader or a noble (the Empire keeps its titles); their ordinary member only when those give
  nobody. Their apparel, looks and weapons then come as the faction's own visitors' do (Rimfolk's peoples keep their one
  signature piece). On what (`CarrierKinds.Mount`, `CarrierMath.MountPool`): every beast of their caravans of body size
  1.2 or more that Giddy-Up lets be ridden (its mount list, read by name), never a predator, in season, that the land
  allows: a pack animal of this land, one that lives wild here (`BiomeAnimals`), or one wild nowhere (a farm beast);
  else the horse where the season allows, else on foot. The kind and the beast a people sent last count half as much next
  time where they have another (not saved). Rimfolk's peoples in a temperate forest, by the catalogue: the kinds a people
  sends went from two at most (three for the Ashen Banner) to three or more for 22 of the 23 (two for the Enclave), the
  beasts from one (the muffalo; none for the Pilgrims) to two or three for 18 of the 23; the Enclave, the League, the
  Order and the Scholars sent one kind every time before. A people whose range truly has one kind still sends someone new each time.
  Armed visitors of an event (Visitors/) keep `Couriers.PersonKind` as before.
- **Words.** The courier's messages say "by the mailbag" (`CC_Courier_ByBag`) and that a go-between or an errand's courier
  is "walking up to the mailbag" (`CC_Courier_ToBag`, `_ToGate`, `_ToColony`, as `{4}` of the four `CC_Courier_Arrive_Await*`
  keys); the setting's tip and the Almanac's couriers page say the mailbag and the nearest way out (keywords unchanged).
- **Older saves.** A trip already on the map keeps its spot (the gate) and sets goods down there as before; the groups'
  graphs keep their toils in the same order (travel, work, leave, flee), so a group under way carries on in the new ones.
  A trip's mounts are no longer packed together on loading (a gap stays a gap, so each rider's beast stays theirs).
  Nothing new is saved but the trip's `atBag`; no new schedule slot, no new setting.
- **Not run in the game** (none of it could be): the way in and the walk to the places beside the bag; Giddy-Up taking the
  three jobs as done in the saddle, and its "parking" no longer happening; the rider getting off at the bag for the
  stores and back on as they leave, by both ways; the tameness letting Giddy-Up's own remount take; goods round the bag;
  the variety of kinds and beasts on the player's own peoples and mods.

### Supplies for the colony's own rider (the player's request, 10 November 2026; released 0.210.0)

The player: "sending a colonist off to send a letter makes them just go off map without any supplies or preparation.
supply selection should be part of the initial decision." Until now `OwnRiders.SetOut` sent them with the fastest beast and
an empty pack, straight to the edge. The pure rules in `Post/RiderPackMath.cs` (linked; `Tools/Tests/RiderPackTests.cs`,
"the rider's supplies: ", 129 checks: the rules, every mix of facts, the seams); the game side in `Post/RiderPacks.cs` and
`Post/RiderPackWindow.cs`, `Post/OwnRiders.cs`.

- **Chosen with the send.** In the letter's window, "By our own rider" now has a row under the rider: **Supplies** (the
  supplies window) and a line on the food against the road ("Food for 9.4 days; the road there and back is 7.1 days"), in
  green, amber or red, with the whole list on hover (`RiderPackPart`, drawn by `Dialog_NeighbourLetter`, its why folded
  into the send's). The mailbag's "Send with our rider" asks which letter, then who, then opens the supplies window with
  Send and Cancel (`Dialog_RiderPack.ForLetter`). Both work on one `RiderPackModel`: the road, the suggestions, what is to
  hand and the verdict, looked at once a second, the road every half a minute or when the rider or the beast changes.
- **What is suggested** (`RiderPacks.Packing`, by the journey planner's rules). The trip is the road there by the game's
  own caravan reckoning for this rider and their beast with what they'd carry (`JourneyPack.Route`, as the planner reads
  it; `PostReach.RiderDays` only where no path is found), the longest wait at the town for the answer
  (`RiderPackMath.TownDays`: half a reply's days at most, the very rule `Arrived` rolls by, `TownWaitDays`), and as long
  back (`TripDays`). Food: the rider's own nourishment a day by the game's hunger rate, for the trip with the planner's
  margin (a quarter more and a spare day, `JourneyMath.FoodNutrition`), packed best first (`JourneyMath.PackFood`: what
  keeps through the trip, travel food first), only food they'd eat on the road (`RiderPacks.Eats`: the caravan's own rules,
  `RoadFood.RoadEdible`; the food policy they eat by on the road, `RoadFood.OnTheRoad`; no venerated animal; their beliefs,
  `Beliefs.FitForStock`). A little medicine (`JourneyMath.Medicine` for one: one, and one more for every eight days; never
  more than half the stores while anyone stays home), the plainer kinds first. Drugs for an addiction or a chemical
  dependency (`JourneyPack.Drugs`). The beast's feed (kibble, else hay, what it can eat) for the days it can't graze, by the
  share of the trip without grazing (`FeedNeedDays`; every day for a beast that doesn't graze). The player's own numbers,
  lines and lines taken off stay as they set them, as in the planner.
- **The supplies window** (`Dialog_RiderPack`, frame key `RiderPack`): the lines by kind (food, medicine, drugs, feed for
  the beast by name, anything else), each with its number to step (Shift 10, Ctrl 100), All, take off or put back, whose
  number it is, the days of food it gives, how many are to hand, and a warning when the rider won't eat it on the road;
  **Add from the stores** (the journey planner's own picker, `Dialog_JourneyPick`, here without the colony's stalls since
  the rider gathers from the stores only; it now takes the window it serves and whether to offer the stalls) and **Pack
  the recommended**; below, the food against the trip, the stores' word when they hold no more, the beast's feed, the
  medicine, and the load against what the rider (and a beast that carries) can carry, by the game's own mass rules.
- **When it falls short** (`RiderPackMath.Judge`, `MaySend`, `WhyKey`). Short of the road (the food, or the beast's feed)
  the send is greyed with why: the stores can't feed them for the road (`Why_Stores`), the supplies feed them for only so
  many days (`Why_Short`), the beast would go hungry (`Why_Feed`); **Let them go short, knowing it** (in both places) lets
  them go, said in amber ("goes short, knowing it: the food runs out after about 3 days, and then hunger on the road").
  More than they can carry is greyed always (`Why_Over`): a caravan that heavy can't move. No medicine is a word, not a
  reason to hold them.
- **Gathering before setting out** (`OwnRiders.Gather`, from the job). The rider takes the letter from the mailbag as
  before, then the game's own caravan forming takes over, the way the journey planner's caravans leave
  (`JourneyRun.Depart`): the rider and their beast, the lines not yet in their packs as its goods (`JourneyPack.Missing`,
  the nearest the gate first), gathered at the colony's caravan packing spot or the gate (`JourneyPack.Gate`), out by the
  edge toward the town (`JourneyPack.Exit`, `StartTile`), where the game makes their caravan and sends it to the town.
  The beast is led on its rope, a pack beast is loaded by the game's own rules, and with Giddy-Up the rider is in the
  saddle as it heads out. What the stores no longer hold is said ("The
  stores are short of 2 packaged survival meals for Guido's road to Emberford: they go without it"). Where the forming
  can't be had (no way out), they walk to the edge and go as before. The job's first toils keep their order, so a rider
  saved on the way to the edge goes on from there. Out on the world map (`Departed`, watched every 250 ticks on the post's
  own pass, `OwnRiders.Rare`, `Watching`), the message says the game's own days of food in their caravan against the trip
  by its own estimate ("with the letter and food for about 9 days; the road there and back is about 7"), or that they will
  go hungry on the road. Called away or the forming called off before they left: the letter goes back in the bag, as
  before, and what they gathered goes back into the stores by the game's own unloading.
- **On the road, at the town and home.** They eat from their pack on the road and while they wait at the town, by the
  game's own caravan rules (and the road's food policy); going short has the game's own consequences: its "ran out of
  food" message, hunger, then malnutrition, at the game's rate. Home again (watched within a few seconds), what is left of
  the supplies in their and the beast's packs is said ("Guido is home with what is left of the supplies (3 packaged
  survival meals and 1 herbal medicine), and it goes back into the stores") and unloaded by the game's own rule for a
  caravan come home. Lost on the road, the supplies go with them.
- **Every age.** The rider's forms are as before: on foot (a runner) or on the colony's beast; the supplies and the words
  follow ("rides to Emberford on Bess", "goes to Emberford on foot"). Vehicles are not a rider's form yet (no vehicle mod is
  read for the post).
- **Saved.** `PostBook.packs` (`RiderPack`: the letter's id, the lines taken, whether sent short knowingly, the trip's
  days), one a letter going with the colony's rider, from the send until they're home or the letter goes back in the bag
  (`RiderPacks.Prune`, hourly and on saving); modelled in `save_estimate.py` (`packs`, `lines`). A rider of an older save
  already getting ready, or a letter sent before, takes the planner's suggestions (`RiderPacks.DefaultFor`).
- **Not run in the game** (none of it could be): the row and the window in both places; the game's caravan forming for a
  lone rider and their beast (the rope, the loading, the wait, Giddy-Up's mount as it heads out); the messages as they
  set out and come home; the far town's wait on the pack.

## The diplomacy screen: the peoples beside their page (the player's request, 8 November 2026)

The player: "the diplomacy screen could be better displayed", "I don't really know which option best to choose from all
the ones. And they should kind of ... have some motivation to do them", and on the proposal "very good, all of it! i also
want to quickly see and sort by who's closest". Step A of `docs/design/diplomacy-screen.md` and points 10 and 11 of step 2
of `docs/design/post-and-letters.md`: Region → Peoples is a list of peoples beside the chosen people's page, every act
that fits a target says what it brings, how it travels and what it costs, and the kind letters wait for a reason. UI and
occasion rules only: every act runs through its own code path as before. In `UI/Region/` (`PeoplesView`, `PeoplesList`,
`PeoplePage`, `PeopleActs`, `PeoplesModel`) and `World/LetterOccasions.cs`; the pure rules in `PeoplesViewMath.cs`,
`PeopleActMath.cs` and `World/LetterOccasionMath.cs` (`Tools/Tests/PeoplesScreenTests.cs`, "the peoples screen: ").

- **The list** (`PeoplesList`, about 320 wide; 260 beside a narrower page; 200 with compact rows when the drawer is open
  at the standard window: `PeoplesViewMath.ListWidth`). At its top a search (name, kind, age, towns, the people the
  colony knows there; every word must be found), three filter chips with their counts (Neighbors: a town within the
  region map's reach of a home; Mail: a letter on its way in by the post, a call of theirs waiting on the colony, or a
  letter of theirs waiting in the letter stack for a choice; Dealings: ties or something under way in the diplomacy
  model), and the sort: Closest (the default), Regard, Name, Age (tribal first), ties by the closest then the name, the
  player's choice kept for the session (`RegionView.sort`, not reset by a new game). Then "All peoples" (what is owed
  each way and what each remembers: `DiplomacyPanels.Owed` and `FactionMemoryPanel`, the old view's top and foot), and
  the groups Allies, At peace and At war (a people at war with everyone always there), each folding. A row (40 high):
  the people's icon, name, its nearest town's days at the right, a gold mark for mail; under it the stance's dot and
  word, its age word, an arrow for this season's trend and a small regard meter (goodwill -100 to 100). The days are
  the post's reach rule (`PostReach.Of`: the world's own travel time at the colony's means), of the town nearest by the
  road among the three nearest in a straight line; they are worked out a couple of towns a frame and the list is put
  in order again as they come in ("no road" last). At its foot the web: the first fourteen peoples of the list round an
  ellipse, the colony in gold at the middle, green lines for allies and red for wars (the game's own relations between
  them, and the colony's own), a red ring for a people at war with everyone; a dot's name on hover, a click chooses it.
  It stays fixed at the list's foot on a 1080 screen and ends the list's scroll on a 720 one (`WebFixed`).
- **The page** (`PeoplePage`). The header: icon and name (a link to its card), "Show on the map" (the region map with its
  towns lit), its age as a chip with its heading and why (0.169.0, `PeopleAgeWords.Heading`) and its kind, its stance
  as a chip, the regard meter and goodwill, and this season's trend in words with the deeds behind it ("Warming this
  season: gave them a gift": its good turns against its wrongs in the last 15 days of the faction memory, by weight,
  `PeoplesViewMath.Trend`). The tabs (`UiKit.Modes`, with counts): **Overview**: what they want and fear (what a people
  of Rimfolk's honors and fears, what they hope for at a feast by their age, hard times on them, the threats to them the
  colony knows of, their wars, what they ask of the colony now; "little is known" when nothing is), how to reach them now
  (the nearest town and its days, the post's reach lines, who of theirs is at the colony), then "Do something with...".
  **Towns**: each town closest first with its size (hamlet, trading post, new town or their own word for a town, and its
  fortune), its days, its reach line and the post's range ring (`PostRing.Ring`); a click shows it on the region map
  (`Cards.ShowOnMap`), its act button aims "Do something with..." at it. **People**: whom the colony knows of theirs by
  name, closest town first (their regard in words, Write greyed with why, an act button), who of theirs is at the colony,
  and a link to Faces. **Dealings**: diplomacy's own body for the people (`DiplomacyPanels.PeopleBody`: their head, pacts,
  truces, fealty, debts each way, marriages, what is under way). **History**: what they remember of the colony
  (strongest first) and their timeline with the colony (the world's history of theirs that names a home, the player's
  people or one of its own), with "Their history" for the whole of it.
- **"Do something with..."** (`PeopleActs`): the targets the whole people, a town (its picker closest first, with days)
  and a person (a notable picker). The acts for the target, in sections: the letters by occasion (to their head, the
  town's head or whoever the colony knows there, or the person); the acts registered on that thing's card
  (`CardActs.registry.In`: for a people truce, pact, calling a defense pact in, fealty sworn or renounced, envoys asked
  and sent, a feast, a match, wards asked and offered, an exchange of captives; for a town an envoy sent to it, a vassal's
  levies and harvest, a former town asked or taken back, a journey; for a person a match proposed and a feast with them
  among the guests); the debts of honor to call in or answer (`DiplomacyModel.CallAct`, `AnswerAct`); and someone of
  theirs at the colony to talk with face to face ("Show them"). Each row: its words, its button (the act's own, greyed with
  its own check's reason), what it brings, and how it travels and what it costs. Built at most once a second; one or
  two columns by the page's width.
- **What each is for** (post step 2, point 11; `PeopleActMath.ForKey`, `CostKey`, `Way`, `Alt`; the words in
  `Rimfolk_PeoplesScreen.xml`): one line each, written from what the act does in code (the letters' `LetterMath.Brings`,
  `NotableMath.OpinionShift`, `GoodwillShift`, `Grants`; `EnvoyMath.EndRegard` 12, `WardMath.HomeRegard` 20,
  `PactMath.CartPayShare` four fifths, the rest from each act's own outcome; the tests hold the numbers to the code). Two
  read by a setting: a truce says it keeps raids away only with "Truces keep raids away" (and the deeper hooks), a
  warning says it makes a debt of honor only where debts of honor are kept. How it travels: a letter says the post's
  reach line for its town (by the post rider, by relay, out of reach, by radio; without the post, by their messenger or
  a call); an envoy or a journey by caravan with its days; a pact called in or levies from home at once; renouncing and a
  vassal's harvest at home; face to face here.
- **Letters by occasion** (post step 2, point 10; `LetterOccasionMath.Occasion`, `LetterOccasions.WhyNot`): asking for news
  always; condolences after a loss heard of and a warning when a threat to them is known (the letters' own topics, as
  before); an invitation when the home's feast with guests is planned or set, a day of the colony calendar kept with a
  feast, games, a bonfire, gifts or a custom comes within the week, or its guest beds (Hospitality's) stand empty with
  nobody from outside staying; asking for help when the stores hold food for under 6 days (where allies send food) or
  less than one medicine for each colonist; greetings in the last 3 and first 7 days of the year, or within 10 days of a
  gift the colony gave them (their memory's gift deeds). A letter open says why it fits now ("Now: after the death of
  Ana, their mayor"); one without a reason is greyed "No reason now: ..." with what would bring one, the same in the
  letter's window (`Dialog_NeighbourLetter` asks `LetterOccasions.WhyNot` and shows the reason beside each). The letters'
  own checks (`NeighbourLetters.WhyNot`) are unchanged, so a feast's invitations go as before. Setting **Letters by
  occasion** (`letterOccasions`, the neighbours' section, on, needs the letters); off, greetings, invitations and help
  go whenever their old checks allow.
- **The region map.** The people chosen on Peoples has its towns lit (`RegionView.lit`: a gold ring and its names; a
  chip at the map's top left says whose and lets them go); the post's range rings stay. The map's List has a "Closest
  first" chip (`RegionView.closest`, `RegionViewsMath.CompareClosest`): all its rows in one, nearest first.
- **Faces** stays the view's second mode: the people known by name across every people, old foes, those who left, the
  faces kept up with are not one people's, so they read cleaner on their own; a people's own notables are its People tab.
  `Peoples` and `Peoples/Faces` (and `Diplomacy`) still land where they did; a people's card opened in full chooses it
  in the list (`Cards.OpenInWindow`).
- **Saved**: nothing. The sort and the filters are the session's, the search, the people chosen, the tab and the target
  start afresh with a new game.

## Dealings with a whole people or town, pen friends and the world writing first (the player's request, 8 November 2026)

The player: "i want to be able to do some interactions with another base/faction as a whole, rather than contacting a
single person. like some business is just targeted at their whole base and they can receive it as such", and on letters
"when am I going to send a letter to another guy on the other side of the world just asking like to chit chat? ... the
options should have some motivation to do them". Step B of `docs/design/diplomacy-screen.md` (points 6 to 13) and points
12 to 14 of step 2 of `docs/design/post-and-letters.md`, approved by the player ("very good, all of it!"). In
`Source/ColonyCouncil/Dealings/`; the pure rules in `DealingMath.cs` (`Tools/Tests/DealingTests.cs`, "dealings: ").

- **One letter purpose for all of it** (`LetterPurpose.Dealing`, the last of the purposes so saved letters keep their
  places; `DealingLetters`, called through `DiplomacyLetters` as the other stage 2 purposes are). A dealing is a letter to
  the town's council (or a people's leaders, for a proclamation or a petition to them as a whole), received by the town's
  head (or whoever of theirs the colony knows there; for the people, their head: `Dealings.Receiver`), addressed in its
  words to "the council of Ashford" by their age (the elders of a tribe's town, the town council of an industrial one, the
  governors of a spacer one, the court at an Empire's town). Its topic keeps what it is (`deal:Supply:0:1234`: the kind,
  its sub-kind, the town or -1) and its help field the terms (`terms:RawCorn:75`). It is written by a colonist and goes as
  every letter does: the mailbag and whoever goes that way, the post, the colony's own rider, a relay, a chain of
  neighbours, a call on the console, a go-between for a people at war; the answer comes back the same way (in the post,
  with the rider, by their messenger when it carries silver). The purpose shows in the letter's window only when it was
  opened for a dealing; the general "Write" never picks it.
- **Offered** from a town's card (an act for each of the eight, `DealingActs`), a people's card (proclamations and
  petitions to their leaders) and so on Peoples, "Do something with..." (`UI/Region/PeopleActs.cs`, the section "With
  their council as a whole"; `PeopleActMath` has the eight acts and Reply, by letter, each with what it brings and costs).
  An act is greyed with the first reason none of its kinds is open (`DealingMath.WhyNot`, kept a second), or the letters'
  own (one letter at a time to each, too many open, the head at the colony). The letter's window lists every dealing open
  with that council under "What about" and the terms under "What is asked", each greyed with why.
- **Their answer** (`DealingLetters.Read`): agreed or refused by `DealingMath.Chance`: the dealing's own base, their
  head's regard (0.004 a point) and their people's goodwill (0.003), their ways (`DealingMath.Ways`: traders and brokers
  like contracts and stalls, mercenaries hire out guards, healers and pilgrims take in refugees, artisans like joint works
  and festivals; the Empire takes no charity and minds friendship, contracts, hires and amends), between 0.05 and 0.95.
  Agreed, the tone is never worse than cool; refused, a refusal. Their words are the council's own line for each kind,
  yes and no (`CC_Deal_Ans_*`), not a kind letter's quote; the letter's title "The council of Ashford answer". The
  dealing is written in the book when they read it (stage Asked), and starts when their answer is in at the colony
  (`NeighbourLetters.Owed` calls `DealingLetters.AnswerIn`): set down at the mailbag, brought by the rider, the messenger's
  trip settled, the call ended. A letter overtaken by events (the town no longer theirs, a war) is answered without a yes
  or a no.
- **What is open** (`DealingMath.WhyNot` over `Dealings.Facts`): not with the setting off; at war only a petition about
  their raiders or for amends; someone of theirs known by name there to receive it; a way to reach them; one of each kind
  at a time with them; not within 15 days of a refusal; goodwill 0 or more (relief any, a petition any, friendship 20,
  market rights 10). Each kind's own below.
- **A supply contract** (point 6): the colony delivers (its most plentiful goods, the trade pact's cart: `Pacts.CartGoods`,
  paid four fifths of their worth) or they deliver (by their age: potatoes, rice, wood, cloth; steel and granite blocks from
  the medieval age; herbal medicine, or industrial medicine and components from the industrial; a load worth 220 to 500
  silver by their age, paid eleven tenths of its worth). Four seasons, the first two days after the answer, then every 15,
  by day (8 to 15) and never with a threat on the map: the colony's goods are fetched from the stores by their porters,
  who bring the silver (`Couriers.CollectOrder`); their goods come to the gate and their porters take the silver
  (`Couriers.Exchange`); without the couriers, at once as before. Short at the season: missed (a letter); two missed in a
  row or three in all break it (goodwill -10, their memory's `contractBroken`); each season kept +1 goodwill and
  `contractKept` (merged by 20 days); kept to its end +6 and `contractKept`. Vanilla Trading Expanded's contracts stay its
  own (on its trading terminal; Rimfolk's trade screen only reads them, `Integrations/VanillaTrading.cs`), untouched;
  Rimfolk's contract is a dealing with a town by letter, its deliveries by porters at the gate, and its better terms are
  the game's price offset, beside the market value VTE moves.
- **Relief** (point 7): for a town in hard times the colony has heard of (a bad world event on their people, or the town
  struggling by its fortune: `Dealings.HardTimes`), the colony's most plentiful medicine (6), meals (15) or raw food (75),
  fetched from the gate by their porters. Once with them: their goodwill +6, the town's fortune +8 (half at their other
  towns, the cause "the colony's relief" on its panel: `RegionFortunes.Move`), and `hardship` in their memory (15: a debt
  of honor of theirs). The Empire seldom takes it.
- **Proclamations** (point 8): a fair day (the next gathering day on the colony's calendar between 3 and 15 days off, else
  6 days on): on its morning (7 to 12) their trader caravan comes (the game's own) and three to six of their folk walk in
  at an errand's pace and spend the day by the walls (`Dealings.Guests`: `Arrivals.Visit`, `LordJob_VisitOnErrand`); a
  threat holds it an hour at a time, past noon it is missed. Friendship declared: taken up, their goodwill +8, their head's
  regard +6 and `friendship` in their memory. The colony's trade terms posted: their caravan within 2 to 6 days, and for a
  season their traders give the colony 3% better terms.
- **Hiring from a town** (point 9): a crew of harvest hands (the camps' harvest hands, `Rimfolk_Camp_HarvestHands`, taken
  on by the letter, paid in silver when they ask; only with crops growing) or a guard detail (`Rimfolk_Camp_HiredGuard`:
  the Ashen Banner's contract, `Camps/CampContract.cs`, for any people; it takes up arms against what comes at the colony,
  keeps the gate by day, and asks its wage every five days, paid at its fire or met at the gate when far: `CampMeet`). Each
  walks in as a group and makes camp for the season beside any camps there (`Dealings.StartCamp`, `CampTracker.Start`
  with force). Its wage is about `PeoplesEMath.Wage` for four or five by their age. Left unpaid they walk (broken); at
  the season's end, kept. Builders and a caravan escort were left out: a camp can't build the colony's blueprints, and
  the game's caravans take only the colony's own.
- **Petitions to their council** (point 10): about their raiders (after a raid of theirs in 60 days): granted, their raids
  are kept away for two seasons (`Patch_DealingRaiders` on the game's choice of raiders, as a truce's); a raid of theirs
  all the same breaks their word (`brokeWord`). For amends (a wrong of theirs in 60 days: raids, the colony's dead, a
  raiders' camp): granted, 12 silver a point of the wrong by their age (100 to 600) comes with their answer and the wrongs
  are settled in their memory. To settle a refugee family camped at the colony with them: their camp packs and walks off
  (`sheltered` remembered by the refugees' people). To take in a family of theirs in hard times: their refugee family walks
  in and makes camp at the gate (the camps' refugee family, with its own asks).
- **Joint works** (point 11): a road, a well, a bridge, a watchtower. The colony's share (wood, then steel, for a road or a
  bridge; stone blocks for a well or a tower, wood for a tribe; a road's by its tiles, 80 to 300) is fetched from the gate
  by their porters, then the work takes its days (a road one for every two tiles, 5 to 15; a well 6; a bridge 8; a tower
  6). The road is the game's own road laid along the world's path from the colony to the town (`WorldGrid.OverlayRoad`, a
  dirt path, a dirt road or a stone road by the earlier of the two ages), drawn on the world map: the world's caravans and
  the post's days go by the game's own path over it (`PostReach` worked out again). A well or a bridge: their town's
  fortune +5, goodwill +5. Each built: `builtTogether` in their memory (12: a debt of honor of theirs, `FavourMath`). A
  watchtower toward their town: while it stands (the town theirs, at peace), a raid the storyteller sends of a people
  whose nearest town lies within 60 degrees of the way to it is held 3 to 5 hours in the game's own queue, and the word
  comes now (`DealingWarnings`, `Patch_DealingWarns` on `Storyteller.TryFire`): their messenger walks in with it, or over
  the radio when both have one. The raid's people is the game's own choice (its `TryResolveRaidFaction`), made now. Not
  while the colony's relay mast sings: the mast's own warning has it.
- **Market rights** (point 12): a fee (200 to 600 silver by their age) fetched from the gate; for 60 days their traders
  give the colony 5% better terms (`Patch_DealingPawnTerms`, `Patch_DealingTownTerms` on the game's own price offset, all
  of a people's dealings together at most 8%), and once a day a chance in ten of their trader caravan, six days apart.
- **A town invited** (point 13): to the colony's coming gathering (its feast with guests, a fair it proclaimed, a calendar
  day kept with a gathering, two days off or more): three to six folk of the town walk in on its morning and spend the day
  (as the fair's), and `feast` is remembered. Or the colony's entertainers to their festival: the invitation missions' own journey
  (`Rimfolk_Mission_Festival`, `HappeningWorker_MissionFestival`, never drawn by the storyteller): at least two by caravan,
  a day at their town, home with a gift, the colony's best at the arts leading; the mission keeps its own memory.
- **Pen friends** (post point 12, `PenFriends`): every letter of the colony's answered warmly or courteously (any purpose,
  `NeighbourLetters.Read`) is one of an exchange with that notable; three within 60 days with their regard at 30 make a pen
  friend (a letter says what it brings), which holds while a letter passes within 90 days and their regard stays at 15.
  A pen friend: their messenger walks in with word of a raid by a people whose nearest town lies within 20 tiles of
  theirs, the raid held 3 to 5 hours (once in 10 days); 2% better terms with their people's traders; their people
  introduce the colony's letters to peoples beyond its reach (below); and after a season, once in 60 days, a favor (since
  10 November 2026 the friend's own in person to the colonist who writes to them, `FavoursOwed.MakePersonal` of
  `DealingMath.FavourSize` 10, counting half: "years of letters between friends"; their whole people's debt until then).
  Twelve friends at most, the coolest lapse.
- **The world writes first** (post point 13, `WorldWrites`): once a day, with a notable at peace who thinks 10 or more of
  the colony, a chance of 0.06, 0.02 more for each pen friend, 0.14 at most, never within 6 days of the last and never with
  two waiting (`DealingMath.WriteChance`; simulated, a letter every 10 to 25 days). Pen friends write three times as often
  as others. News (their town's and region's, the facts service's), a small request by their age (3 medicine, 60 wood, 30
  cloth, 40 steel) or an invitation to their festival (where its journey can be made). It comes in the post from their
  town (`MailIn.FromAbroadId`) and opens at the mailbag; it waits for an answer, in the inbox ("Needs you"), on their card
  ("Answer their letter") and on Peoples. The answer is a Dealing letter (`reply:ID`), leaving with the next carrier going
  their way; read, their regard +4 (a request granted +6), and their thanks in, a request granted brings their porters
  for it (`favorDone`), an invitation accepted is the festival's journey. Unanswered 15 days, their regard -3.
- **A chain of neighbours** (post point 14, `PostReach.FindChain`): a town out of reach may be reached by introduction
  through a people at peace with the colony and with the far one, on good terms with the colony (goodwill 40) or with a
  pen friend among them (goodwill 0): their town within the colony's range, a day there to be introduced and a day further
  on, and on by their means within twice their own range (`DealingMath.ChainDays`: slower than a relay). The letter goes
  with whoever goes toward their town, or the post; its reach line says "by introduction through ...", the region map
  rings it amber.
- **Shown** on the Dealings tab ("With their towns as a whole": each in a line, what, with whom, its terms, where it
  stands, never a time left; `DealingActs.Draw`), counted in the tab and the Dealings filter; on the town's card; in the
  inbox's Under way. Every age: the councils, the goods, the roads and the words by the age; the Empire keeps its court.
- **Settings** (the neighbours' section, each on and needing the letters): *Dealings with a whole people or town*
  (`townDealings`), *Pen friends* (`penFriends`), *The world writes first* (`worldWrites`). The deeper game hooks off: no
  better terms, no raids kept away, no word of raids.
- **Saved** (`DealingBook`, a game component of its own: an older save starts it empty): the dealings (closed ones kept
  60 days, a work built kept while it stands, 80 at most), the pen friends (with their letters' ticks, eight at most each),
  the world's letters waiting (two at once). Modelled in `Tools/save_estimate.py`.

## Diplomacy kept fair: warnings, debts by their size, and the gates (the player's request, 10 November 2026; released 0.204.0)

The player: "if i got it right I can now share a warning with them about any kind of raider, and then just use "a debt
of honor" to have them deliver a variety of valuable things to me, right? this debt should definitely be possible, but it
should be balanced, appropriate to the debt i actually owe and not be repeatable all the time if not for good reasons.
also review the other diplomatic options for balance and "gameplay realism". offering a marriage match for example should
also only be possible when we have great diplomatic relations etc.", "also warning about raiders should only be an option
if the target colony is actually a potential target for these raiders and not too much time has expired", "is any
information that is generated in these talks also logged in the ledger/history/diplomatic screen?", and on the list: "please
go ahead with all of your diplomacy and other guest proposal". The pure rules in `World/WarnMath.cs` (new),
`Diplomacy/FavourMath.cs`, `MatchMath.cs`, `WardMath.cs`, `PactMath.cs`, `World/NotableMath.cs`, `Outsiders/OutsiderMath.cs`
and `OutsiderTalkMath.cs`, `Dealings/DealingMath.cs`; tested in `Tools/Tests/DiplomacyBalanceTests.cs` ("diplomacy balance: ",
every number and gate below, two years of warnings and calls, an older save, the seams).

1. **Warn only of a real threat to their town** (`World/Warnings.cs`, `WarnMath`). The threats to a people are worked out
   at most once an hour for each people from the map (`Warnings.Threats`, weightiest first), measured to the nearest of
   their towns:
   - Raiders: a people that struck a home in the last 5 days (`FactionMemory` "raided"), has a raid on its way
     (`happenings.raids`) or keeps a raiders' camp the colony found (`RaidersCamps.Known`), at war with them, not them,
     still standing (`WarnMath.RaidersWhy`), and in reach (`RaidersSize`): a town of theirs within 20 tiles
     (`DealingMath.WarnTiles`), a camp or a site of theirs within 12, their Faction Territories land within 30
     (`RaidersCampMath.TerritoryTiles`; a flood fill only with such a mod and only when nothing else is near), or the home
     they struck within 20. A people at war with everyone counts by the same rules.
   - A hostile site within 12 tiles of their town, not their own people's.
   - Wars and road troubles (`WarnMath.WarOrRoad`: a bad world event of kind war, roads or son: a warlord, the clans
     gathering, a war between neighbours, a bandit road, the warlord's son's band) whose attacker (its people, else its
     enemy) is at war with them and not them, within 20 tiles (its place, else its people's nearest town); never a war
     they are a side of. This ends the old bug that offered a warlord only to the warlord's own people.
   - Hardships that spread (`WarnMath.Spreading`: sickness, fire, locusts, blight) within 20 tiles, never to the people
     it falls on or one suffering the same: a lesser warning, memory and goodwill, never a debt.
   - The colony must know of it: raiders it saw (struck, coming, a camp found), a site within its region's reach of a home,
     a camp found, or anything heard of in talk (point 10). World events are always told as they begin.
   The letter's window lists, under its topic, the raiders the colony knows of that aren't listed and why
   (`Warnings.NotListedLines`: too far, too old, not their enemy, gone), and a warning with nothing to warn of is greyed
   with the first of them (`Warnings.WhyNone`). The topic texts name the town at risk ("the raiders of the Kotar, camped
   near Ashford").
2. **Recent or coming only.** A raid counts 5 days (`WarnMath.RaidDays`), a coming threat while it lasts. The topic is
   gone when the threat ends; a letter read after that (`Warnings.Heed`: not standing) brings thanks and the plain
   memory (`CC_LetterBring_HeededLate`, `NeighbourLetter.late`), never a debt.
3. **The debt's size by what the warning was worth** (`WarnMath.Size`): a war or a warlord's band near them 14, a camp or
   a hostile site within 12 tiles 12, raiders whose town is within 10 tiles 10, within 10 to 20 (or their land, or the home
   they struck) 8, a memory only. Only a warm answer makes a debt (`NeighbourLetter.owedSize`, saved, read by `Owed`); a
   warm answer that may not make one is remembered under a debt's size (at most 9), a cordial or cool one at the memory's
   own 6. "Warned" memories no longer merge (`FactionMemory.Kinds`), so kind answers never add up into a debt. When the
   threat strikes them (`CallsToArms.Attacked`, the same attacker) within 15 days of the warning, the debt grows by 4
   (`Warnings.Daily`, `Struck`, a line of news: `CC_Warn_Struck_Debt`), else a little more is remembered. No gift by
   regard beside a debt a warning made.
4. **Calling in by the debt's size and their means** (`FavourCalls.SizeOf`, `Worth`; `FavourMath`): goods worth size × 30
   × their town's fortune (0.75 to 1.25) × their means (`Means`: `DealingMath.TheirLoadValue` ÷ 400, tribal 0.55,
   medieval 0.75, industrial 1, spacer 1.25), so a warning's 10 brings 300 at a steady industrial town and refugees' 20 at
   a flourishing spacer one 937; a good word with a third people half the size in goodwill (its weight in the option's
   words: a kind, a warm, a strong one); help toward peace and fighters from 12, a colonist they hold from 15; a notable's
   personal favour counts half. Each greyed with why (`CC_Dip_Why_TooSmall`). The debt's line names its weight
   (`FavourMath.WeightOf`: "a small debt" below 12, "a debt", "a great debt" from 18), so the People page's act rows,
   the letter's topics and the panels say it.
5. **One debt per real threat, with gaps per people.** Each threat is warned of once per people (`NotableBook.warned`,
   saved: the people, the threat's key, when, its size, whether it made a debt, whether it struck, whose it was; 60 at
   most, kept 30 days or while the threat stands; a letter under way to any of them holds it too), so the 12 keys a
   notable keeps (`Notable.done`, now for losses only) can't bring an old threat back. One debt from warnings a season per
   people (`WarnMath.DebtAllowed`). One debt called in a season per people, by letter or face to face
   (`FavourCalls.CalledLately`: a debt of theirs or of one of their notables called in, or honoured or refused within
   `FavourMath.CallGapDays`, the ledger's own closed ties), greyed "a debt of theirs was called in this season already".
6. **The gates.**
   - Match (`Matches.SeekWhyNot`, `TermsWhyNot`; `MatchMath`): sought only with their head's regard 30 and their goodwill
     40, or 10 and 20 for two who courted (lovers, or sweet on each other face to face: the outsider pair's `court`);
     accepted 20% and 1% a point of regard above 30, 35% more for lovers, 10% more at goodwill 75 (5% less when theirs
     would move; 10% to 95%); one of their town made for it only at their head's regard 50; a season's wait with that
     people after a no (`DiplomacyMath.MatchRefused`, "dip:matchNo" in the history, which keeps it). The alliance's
     defence pact is made at the wedding and runs on only while a pact's rules hold (`Matches.PactHolds`,
     `MatchMath.AlliancePact`: `PactMath.Renews`, never the Empire); the town's seasonal gift only at goodwill 20
     (`TownGiftSent`; it waits). Their own offers keep their rules. A match stays between two persons, never houses.
   - Ward asked for: their head's regard 30 (`WardMath.MayAsk`, `Wards.AskWhyNot`, `CC_Ward_Why_Regard`); their send
     chance from there (0.6 at 30).
   - A truce they pay for: -40 (`PactMath.TheyPayScore`, -20 until now), offered by the colony only after a raid of theirs
     beaten lately (`TheyMayPay`, `Truces.BeatenLately`, greyed `CC_Truce_Why_TheyPayBeaten`), at half the colony's price
     (`TheirPriceSilver`, as their own offer always was).
   - Greetings: the token and the gift by regard once a season per notable, any purpose (`NotableMath.GiftAllowed`,
     `Notable.LastOf(NeighbourLetters.GiftKey)`; a warm greeting without one tells how their town fares).
   - Help: once in 20 days per people, whoever of them is written to (`NotableMath.HelpAllowed`,
     `NeighbourLetters.LastOfPeople`, `CC_Letter_Why_HelpPeople`).
   - A pen friend's yearly favour is the friend's own, in person, to the colonist who wrote to them last (else the one they
     think best of): `FavoursOwed.MakePersonal`, size `DealingMath.FavourSize` 10, half the goods (150 at a steady
     industrial town).
   - Something brought next time: free once a season per people, else its market price in silver from the stores when it
     comes (`OutsiderMath.BringFree`, `BringPrice`; the price in the tie's `number`, `Favours.PriceFor`; the menu and the
     promise say which; a paid one waits until the stores hold its price, then their courier fetches it).
7. **Heard news into the history.** `OutsiderTalk.Heard` writes the news as "world:heard" (as far news does,
   `FarNews.Kind`): at the colony, their people and town and the colonist told as its actors, the teller named in the
   line (`CC_Out_Heard_Hist`); the same news within 10 days once (`OutsiderTalkMath.SameNews`). It shows in the people's
   and the town's History.
8. **The People page** (`UI/Region/PeoplePage.cs`, lines made by `OutsiderHeard.Lines` with the town and the colonist
   as links): "Heard lately" in the Overview (their newest 3, any town or none); each town's newest line under its row on
   the Towns tab; a people with no town, its news under the empty list. The Overview's threats are `Warnings.Threats`
   (warned of or not).
9. **News naming a notable** (`HeardNews.notable`, `about`, saved; from the facts behind the line, `ill:`, `head:`,
   `notable:`, else a death among them by name) is on that notable's row on the People tab ("news heard of them", the line
   in its tip), and "Heard of them" lists the news naming theirs, the gone too.
10. **News of a threat makes the colony aware of it.** The facts behind a heard line (`TalkChoice.heardFacts`,
   `OutsiderTalkMath.KeepsFact`) that name a site or a world event (`WarnMath.FromFact`) go into `NotableBook.known`
   (saved, 40 at most, 30 days); a site known so can then be warned of.

Also: `OutsiderHeard.Draw` and `Height` (dead) and `TownView.heard` (built, never read) are gone; the comments about the
"World page" are fixed. **An older save:** each notable's warning keys move to their people's record at the first day's
look (`Warnings.Daily`), so a threat they were warned of stays warned of and no longer comes back to another of them;
letters under way keep their topic keys and are re-checked when read (a threat now gone, or no threat to them under the
new rules, is thanks and memory only); an older letter's warm warning with no size is a debt of 10
(`LetterMath.HeededWarmly`); open debts keep the size their good turn gave them (`terms.number`), one with none takes its
deed's weight (`FavourMath.SizeOf`); open "bring it next time" favours are free. Saved: `NotableBook.warned`, `known`,
`NeighbourLetter.owedSize`, `late`, `HeardNews.notable`, `about`, the outsiders' favour's price in its tie's terms
(modelled in `Tools/save_estimate.py`). Nothing new ticks: the warnings ride on the neighbours' day.

## Whom a letter goes to, and places heard of (the player's request, 10 November 2026; released 0.206.0)

The player: "i'm not yet sure how "writing the town" is differentiated from writing a person directly. i get the same
option menu, albeit options are greyed out so i don't know for sure. basically it should make sense what kind of messages
you can send whom, and which kind of messages are sent to the colony as a whole. for example warning them is for the whole
colony, or asking for some food or medicine. i'm not sure which kind of messages make sense to be sent to a member of the
colony, especially if it's not their leader who can speak for all of them. but this should be differentiated.", and "also
i'm not sure: if other colonies tell me about things that are nearby on their map, will these also be revealed on my own
map for reference?". Until now the town card's "Write to the town" opened the same letter window, with the same purposes,
as writing to anyone; only a town asked back and a dealing were the head's. The five points below were approved ("yes,
sounds great! start now"). The pure rules are `World/LetterAddressMath.cs` and `World/HeardPlaceMath.cs` (both new,
linked in Tools/Tests); the game side `World/LetterRoutes.cs` and `World/HeardPlaces.cs` (new). Tested in
`Tools/Tests/LetterRouteTests.cs` ("whom a letter goes to: ", about 2,000 checks: every purpose's scope, who answers it for
every kind of addressee, the ways, passing on and the word, the words, an older save, the places' rules, the map links,
the seams).

1. **The town's matters go to whoever speaks for the town** (`LetterAddressMath.ScopeOf`, `WhoAnswers`). Each purpose is
   one of three scopes:
   - Personal (anyone): greetings, condolences, news, an invitation, a match (the head's gates of 0.204.0 stand), a favor
     owed in person (a debt's topic whose tie is personal), and an answer to a letter they wrote first (a dealing's topic
     "reply:ID"). The retired council's business counts as personal and is never offered.
   - The town's (its head, `NotableRole.Head` of their town, `LetterRoutes.HeadOf`): a warning, asking for help, their
     people's debt (and the colony's word on their call), captives and ransom, their envoy, wards, a dealing with their
     council, asking for a town back.
   - The whole people's (a pact, a truce, fealty): their leader when the colony knows them by name (`LetterRoutes.LeaderOf`:
     the notable whose pawn is `Faction.leader`), else the head of their town nearest the colony (`FavourCalls.HeadOf`),
     who sends it on (`SpeakerOf`).
   A debt and a dealing are both: their topic decides (`Mixed`, `PersonalTopic`). Nobody known speaks for the town (a face
   met whose town has no head the colony knows): the town's matters are greyed, "Nobody the colony knows speaks for ... yet:
   its head comes to be known once the colony deals with the town (meeting their people, their news)", which is how towns
   are staffed (a town the colony deals with is among its neighbours, `NotableBook.Towns`).
2. **Personal letters go to anyone**, by their own checks as before (`NeighbourLetters.GeneralWhyNot` and `PurposeWhyNot`,
   the old `WhyNot` split in two; `NeighbourLetters.WhyNot` and `LetterOccasions.WhyNot` now ask `LetterRoutes.WhyNot`, so
   every caller, the town card's act, the People page's "Write", "Do something with..." and the cards' own acts, greys a
   letter for the same reason).
3. **A town's matter written to someone else is passed on** (`LetterWay.PassOn`; a council's dealing is not passable,
   `LetterWay.HeadOnly`: "Only the town's head can answer this: write to ..."). The letter keeps whom it is written to
   (`NeighbourLetter.notable`, the post routes it to their town as before) and whom it is for (`passTo`, saved; its
   `toName` "Golakath, reeve of Karond-Keth 2, by way of Acraeraes"). When it reaches them (`NeighbourLetters.Arrive`, from
   the road, the colony's rider and a call alike; `LetterRoutes.Passes` and `Pass`):
   - it goes on: a day more within their town, else the leg between the two towns by their people's means
     (`LetterMath.LegDays`, `LetterAddressMath.PassDays`, a day at least), `passed` set and the answer's way back worked
     out from the head's town; a call is passed on and the head calls back some hours later (`PassCallHours`: 3 to 8 within
     their town, 8 to 22 from another); with the colony's own rider, the rider rides home and the answer comes in the post
     ("... took the letter on to Golakath, whose answer will come with the post");
   - the one who passed it on notes it ("Passed Guido's letter on to Golakath."), a message says so, and its status reads
     "Acraeraes passed Guido's letter on to Golakath: it is with Golakath now";
   - the head reads it (`LetterRoutes.Reader`) with the go-between's word in the score (`NotableMath.LetterInput.word`,
     `LetterAddressMath.Word`): by the go-between's regard of the colony, 6 (60 or more), 5 (30), 3 (10), 0 (civil), -3
     (cool), -6 (wary), -9 (hostile); the heir's or an envoy's good word doubled, and 2 when only civil. Everything else is
     the head's: their regard, the waits and gaps of 0.204.0 (one at a time to them too, `OpenTo` counts `passTo`; the wait
     for the same thing on them, "The colony wrote to Golakath for this only lately"), the debts, the gift once a season;
   - the letter's form shows it: the head's answer begins "Acraeraes brought me your letter." (words given by mouth, a call
     passed on, a medieval hand's own: `LetterAddressMath.PassLineKey`, `LetterRoutes.PassLine`, put before the heart in
     `LetterForm.Answer`, quoted after the intro in the short form), and the colony's own letter is addressed to the head
     (`NeighbourLetters.ForWhom`), the narrator adding "Given to Acraeraes to pass on to Golakath." The exchange is kept
     with the head (`LetterBook` by the letter's id), and the message's click hint names them.
   - The one who passed it on gone afterwards doesn't call it off (`NotableBook.Drop`); the head gone (or the leader
     changed) does, as for any letter to them; the head changed before it reached them, it goes to the one who heads the
     town now.
4. **The letter's window makes it clear** (`Dialog_NeighbourLetter`, `World/NeighboursPanel.cs`):
   - under their name, who they are and whether they speak for the town (`LetterRoutes.Header`: "Acraeraes of Karond-Keth
     2, a trader who called: personal letters. For the town's matters, write to Golakath, reeve."; the head "speaks for the
     town, and takes personal letters too"; the leader "leads ..., and speaks for the town and the whole people"; and "For
     matters of the whole people (a pact, a truce, fealty), write to ..." when someone else speaks for them), with a button
     "Write to Golakath" that turns the letter to them (the purpose kept if it can go to them);
   - the purposes in two sections, "To the town" (for someone who isn't the head "To the town: ask Acraeraes to pass it
     on", each row noted "passed on to Golakath, reeve") and "To Acraeraes", the section of what they answer themselves
     first; a debt is in both ("A debt of honor" for their people's, "A favor they owe in person"), an answer to their
     letter is "Answering their letter"; each greyed purpose says why in words, the row's tooltip in full;
   - under the purposes, for a letter passed on, the route: "Acraeraes will give it to Golakath, reeve, in Karond-Keth 2: a
     day more." or "... will send it on from ... to ..., ..., at ...: the road between the two towns more.", and their word
     ("Acraeraes thinks well of the colony, and their good word goes with it." / "is their envoy: their good word goes with
     it, and counts for much." / "passes it on with no word for or against it." / "thinks poorly of the colony, and their
     word tells against it."); the outlook is the head's, with the word;
   - a town's card (its Who, `LetterRoutes.SpeaksFor`: "Golakath, reeve, speaks for Karond-Keth 2: write to them for the
     town's matters.", or nobody known) and its row on Peoples' Towns tab ("speaks for it: Golakath, reeve") name who speaks
     for it; the card's "Write to the town" tip says so.
5. **Places heard of are marked** (`World/HeardPlaces.cs`, `HeardPlaceMath`). A place a piece of news names that is a real
   world object or tile (the facts "site:ID", a site by its world object, and "ws:ID", a world event by its place, a town
   or a tile) becomes a `HeardPlace` (saved in `NotableBook.places` as "heardPlaces", `HeardPlaceMath.Max` 24, the oldest
   go; one mark a place, brought up to date by the newest telling; modelled in `save_estimate.py`): its card's key, the
   news line, who told it, through whom and when.
   - From talk (`OutsiderTalk.Heard`, the facts the piece named): at once, "Acraeraes of Karond-Keth 2 told Guido of it, 3
     days ago (5 Aprimay 5501)", and the heard news keeps the place (`HeardNews.place`, saved).
   - From a letter's news (`Facts.NewsNear` now records the fact behind each line, `FactSet.newsFacts`; the lines told
     by the answer's tone, or the town's news one brings): waiting on the answer (`HeardPlace.waitLetter`) and marked when
     it is in (`NeighbourLetters.Owed`, which every way an answer comes in passes through), "Told in a letter from Golakath
     of Karond-Keth 2, answering Guido's letter passed on by Acraeraes, ...". An answer that never comes lets it go.
   - Drawn on Rimfolk's region map (`RegionMapView.DrawHeard`: a small letter on a dark disc above and left of the tile,
     so it never covers a town's or a site's own mark; hovered, its tooltip with the land; a town's or a site's own
     tooltip lists it) and, as the least intrusive way onto the game's world map, an overlay drawn after the world's
     interface (`Patch_HeardPlacesWorld`, a postfix on `WorldInterface.WorldInterfaceOnGUI`, behind the deeper hooks: the
     layer in view, the planet's near side, `GenWorldUI.WorldToUIPosition`); nothing is added to the world itself.
   - It fades over the last fifth of the news's own keep time (`HeardPlaceMath.KeepDays`, 60 days, as heard news,
     `OutsiderTalkMath.HeardDays`), to a quarter at the faintest, and goes then or with the place (`HeardPlaces.Daily`).
   - Heard news lines (a town's card, the people's page) end with "Show on map", a link that shows the place on the region
     map (`LinkTextMath.WrapOnMap`, the mark "@" before the thing; `LinkText` then calls `Cards.ShowOnMap`).
- **An older save.** Open letters keep their addressee. A letter already written to someone who doesn't speak for the town
  about a town's matter is passed on when it reaches them (`LetterRoutes.Passes` works out whom from the rules then), the
  head answering it; one already answered stays as it was. Places start empty and are marked as news is heard.
- Not run here (none of it could be): the window's new layout at its height (860) and the header's button; a letter passed
  on in the game, by the post, the colony's rider and a call; the head's line in a written-out answer of each shape; the
  marks on the region map beside a site's own; the world map overlay (its position beside the game's icons, the far side,
  another layer in view, a tooltip over the planet) and with mods that draw on the world map; "Show on map" from a heard line.

## Letters that read like letters (the player's request, 9 November 2026)

The player: "letters exchanged from and to pawns should also read like actual letters, make a varied selection of
interesting letters that read well and can also crack a joke sometimes, or be serious"; then, of their tone, "they don't
necessarily have to be warm, just according to the situation and motivation"; of who writes, the writer's race and
culture shape the tone and style, medieval writers in medieval English ("the player loves it"), "how a stupid bandit could
not spell words correctly etc", and "you can also be experimentive with grammar, writing style, formatting, phrasing etc
if it makes sense, like strange races or cultures". In `Source/ColonyCouncil/Letters/`: the pure rules `LetterFormMath.cs`
and `LetterCultureMath.cs` (linked in Tests.csproj; `Tools/Tests/LetterFormTests.cs`, "letters: "), the game's side
`LetterForm.cs`, the kept letters `LetterBook.cs`, the reading window `LetterReadWindow.cs`; the pools
`Defs/FlavorPoolDefs/Rimfolk_Letters_*.xml`; keys `Rimfolk_LetterForm.xml`. Setting **Letters written out in full**
(`lettersInFull`, the neighbours' section, on, needs the letters): off, the short form as before and nothing kept.

- **The form** (`LetterFormMath.Compose`), shared by every letter a person writes, both ways: a heading now and then (the
  place and the date as the writer would put it, `DateStyleOf`: a tribe by the season, a line of the When pool, "when the
  geese came back"; the medieval age and the Empire in the court's words, "the 7th day of Decembary, in the year 5501",
  the Empire's "Given at"; the industrial plainly; the spacer age by the standard date, "5501.2.05"; always from a council,
  the Empire or the ancient, seven letters in ten otherwise, four at war or when curt), a salutation, an opening, the heart
  (what the letter is for), sometimes an aside (`Aside`: a joke, an everyday detail or a serious line), the closing and the
  signature in kind (`SignOf`: a person with their title and town, a council "by the hand of", the Empire's titled, the
  colony's "for all of us at" the colony, a mark for one who can't write their name, "written down for them by" a helper,
  a hive's many), sometimes a P.S. (`PSChance`, `PSKind`). The narrator's lines go under it, after a mark of their own
  ("* * *"): in answer to which letter and how it came, what it brings, gifts set down, news told, why it went badly, how
  far it moved them, a threat. Never inside the writer's words. A call reads as its transcript (`Call`: the log's head in
  the console's age, "Comms log" or "Link record", and "Name: words" lines; called back, or a message left on the console);
  words passed on by mouth as the carrier's ("Hessa bids me tell you this", the sender's words in quotes). Neither is
  shaped as a letter.
- **The tone follows the situation** (`Tags`, `ToneTag`, `Warmth`, `Business`, `Motive`): how they took the colony's
  letter (warm, cordial, cool, curt, refusal) or, for the colony's own, how the two stand (`Stance`, by their regard: 40
  warm, 5 cordial, -25 cool, else curt); at war; what the writer wants (`LetterMotive`: a pen friend or a neighbour who
  thinks a good deal of the colony, 50, writes as a friend; a council, the Empire and the business between two peoples,
  pacts, truces, ransoms, envoys, wards, fealty, a town asked back, a dealing, as a duty; one who thinks little of the
  colony, under 5, or trusts nobody, persona trust -30, sounds it out; one whose pride is 40 or more won't ask outright; a
  trader, by their role or a people of traders or brokers, angles for business); hard times at their town. A warm
  register ("warmly") only for a warm letter that is no business, nor wary, nor proud, nor at war, or a courteous one
  between friends (the colony's kind writer too, never its abrasive one); a warm answer that is business, wary or proud
  reads courteous. Lines carry their register (warmly for a chatty, personal line; warm|cordial courteous enough for
  either; cordial, cool, curt, refusal) and their motive (m:trade's pitches, m:duty's office, m:wary's caution, m:proud's
  standing); a cool, curt or businesslike letter draws no warm line (tested over every purpose, tone, motive, address and
  speech). Jokes: a warm letter jokes most (0.45 of its asides, by the writer's persona humour, -100 to 100, a fifth either
  way), a courteous or cool one a dry remark now and then (0.2), the Empire half as often, a curt letter, a refusal, a
  condolence, a warning, help asked, a truce, a ransom, war or hard times never. A council writes no aside.
- **Who writes shapes how** (`LetterCultureMath.Read`, every name an active def of the player's in `docs/player-mods`,
  tested): their age (w:tribal...), their people's ways (their:herders...), their ideoligion's memes as culture tags
  (c:pious, c:raider, c:proud, c:loyal, c:nature, c:herd, c:together, c:free, c:transhuman, c:tunnel, c:dark, c:pain,
  c:guilty, c:highlife, c:preach, c:craft, c:trade, c:peace, c:sea, c:tea, c:coffee, c:cannibal; Ideology and the meme
  mods), their xenotype's kind (x:hulking, x:refined, x:martial, x:underground, x:toxic, x:fiery, x:cold, x:pig, x:sea,
  x:space, x:elf; Biotech and the race mods). Anyone else writes plainly.
- **Each writer's speech, drawn from alone** (`SpeechOf`, the pick's partition: a line's olde, u: or sv: tag against the
  writer's): a strange voice of their own first; then an unschooled hand; then a medieval writer's English; else plain.
  - *Medieval English* (`olde`): a medieval people's notables and the colony's own in its medieval age (`Ages.Ours`, the
    colony's tech level), never a tribe (their own plain, image-rich voice) nor the Empire (its formal, titled style).
    Authored as their own lines (thou for the subject, thee for the object, thy before a consonant, thine before a vowel
    or standing alone; thou art, hast, wilt, dost; he hath, she doth; -eth sparingly), every part and every purpose and
    tone, with their own hearts (`HeartSpeech`). Tested both ways: no "you" in a medieval line, no thee or thou in a plain one.
  - *Schooling* (`SchoolingOf`): Intellectual skill, four less for an outlaw people (the pirates, bandits and savage
    kingdoms of the player's factions), three for a slow learner, one for the tribal and medieval ages, six more for one
    too smart or a scholar; 0 and under not at all (`u:none`: many slips, no capitals, a word crossed out and written again,
    "gold" spelled two ways, a mark for a signature, a threat that undercuts itself), 1 or 2 barely (`u:some`: a slip or
    two). A council and the Empire have scribes. Theirs a third of the time, the colony's half the time, written down for
    them by someone a little better (`Helped`: the colony's free colonist of Intellectual 6 or more who writes best). The
    misspellings are deliberate, written into the lines, never a corruption of text; the test only asks each such line to
    show it, and no other check is loosened.
  - *Strange voices* (`LetterCultureMath.Voices`, by xenotype or race, then meme): sv:machine (androids: a stamped record
    for a head, numbered points, "END OF LETTER.", an addendum), sv:hive (insectors, hivelings, Korg, a gestalt: "we",
    clipped, no salutation, signed as the many of their town, hearts of their own), sv:beast (lycans, wolfmen, saurids,
    the awakened apes, Paws of Interest's: smells, tracks, seasons), sv:green (plant folk and fungoids: light and roots),
    sv:fey (fairies and wood elves: a formula said first and said again at the end), sv:ancient (sanguophages and their
    kin, the forsaken, high elves, archons, A RimWorld of Magic's spirits: a dated, overly literal register, always headed,
    and a postscript longer than the letter), sv:deep (mind devourers, eldritch cults: words in an order of their own).
    Readable, purposeful, never mockery; each drawn only by its own writers (tested).
- **Their answer** (`LetterForm.Answer`, from `NeighbourLetters.Body` when written out): the answer pool's line
  (`Rimfolk_Pool_NeighbourWrites`, its tags unchanged: purpose, tone, their age, Rimfolk's peoples, war, the facts' ties
  and history) is the heart; a council's answer, a reply's thanks, a medieval, unschooled or hive writer take theirs from
  `Rimfolk_Pool_LetterHeart` (a council's yes or no and the dealing's kind, `DealingLetters.HeartTags`). The opening,
  aside, closing and P.S. are drawn around it. Everything the old body said below the quote becomes the narrator's lines.
- **The colony's own letter** (`LetterForm.Ours`), composed as its writer finishes it (`NeighbourLetters.Written`; a
  tribal colony's spoken message as it is given, `Send`): the writer's voice (`Voice`: blunt with Social 4 or less or
  abrasive, eloquent with 12 and Intellectual 6 or 15, plain otherwise; kind, abrasive, cheerful or gloomy by persona
  outlook or natural mood, learned at Intellectual 10, proud at persona pride 40; humour), the purpose and its topic (a
  loss, a threat, food or medicine, the dealing's name, a ward asked or offered, a captive, a pact, an envoy, a reply's
  yes or no), the colony's age, and what the facts service says is true at home (colony:harvest, colony:children, the
  newcomer, the cook, a raid, hunger) with the season and the weather as it is written. Nothing claims a thing happened at
  the colony that didn't; their jokes are about their own town and life. A call has no letter of the colony's.
- **The world writing first** (`LetterForm.First`, from `WorldWrites.Write`): news, a request or an invitation by what the
  writer wants (a trader's, a wary neighbour's, a proud one's "we do not, as a rule, ask anything of anyone", a duty, a
  friend's), the old lines under it. **A friend's word** (`LetterForm.Friend`, from `PenFriends`): a pen friend made, their
  favor, word of raiders in haste.
- **Kept and read** (`LetterBook`, a game component of its own; an older save starts it empty): one exchange a letter of
  the colony's or a first letter of theirs, its pages in order (the colony's letter and their answer; theirs first, the
  reply and their thanks; a call's transcript; a friend's word), three at most, each capped (`LetterFormMath.MaxKept` 2400
  characters, the narrator's `MaxNote` 900); the newest `MaxPerNotable` (8) with any one notable and `MaxExchanges` (60)
  in all; a letter called off before it left is let go (`Dropped`). Modelled in `Tools/save_estimate.py` (about 160 KB at
  most). The teller's letter is matched to the page it tells by its words (`Told`, from `Tell.Letter`). Read: the answer's
  event card offers "Read Stace's letter" (`ReadAct`, an act on the card's first page; the card stays open); the Diplomacy
  screen's People lists each notable's letters newest first under "Letters with ..." (`With`), a click opening both sides;
  the mailbag's "Read a letter" (those waiting at the gate too); the messages about it ("has written", "in the mailbag",
  "handed to") open it when clicked, "Click to read it." (since 10 November 2026: "The letter carried and read" under the
  post), else say where it can be read. The reading window
  (`LetterReadWindow`, frame key "LetterRead", 420 by 360 at least, several at once): each letter on a sheet of cream
  paper with dark ink in either look, who wrote it and when above, the narrator's lines in a quieter hand under theirs.
- **No repeats**: a part's line never one this session drew lately (`Flavor.Memory`, the LineMemory window for the part)
  nor, while another fits, one already written in a kept letter, so a load forgets none.
- **The library** (counted by the tests; about 1,870 lines): 240 salutations, 260 closings, 350 openings, 380 asides, 150 postscripts,
  190 hearts of theirs and 190 of the colony's, 27 tribal dates, 56 call lines and 23 carriers' frames; of them about 450
  in medieval English, 150 unschooled or barely schooled, and about 20 for each strange voice.
- **Not changed**: what each answer does (tones, regard, goodwill, gifts, help, debts, threats, the post's carrying); the
  colony's envoys' and wards' letters home and a town's letter (narrated, as before).

### Letters of many shapes (the player's request, 10 November 2026)

The player, after 0.202.0: "i really like a lot of text variety, also someitmes the letters can be longer, with some
stories or stuff that is told by the different pawns or factions. some might include poems, detailed stories of raider
attacks, ideological ramblings and all kinds of different things. they don't all always fully have to follow the same
structure, some could be several pages long, some just boiled down to the necessities etc. I just want a lot of variety,
content and interesting writing that makes reading every letter a fun or interesting experience." Released 0.203.0. Round 2, part 1: the
shapes, how they are chosen, the rules that keep the words true, reading long letters, the setting and a first library; a
second content pass fills the same shapes. In `Source/ColonyCouncil/Letters/`: the pure rules `LetterKindMath.cs` (linked
in Tests.csproj; `Tools/Tests/LetterShapeTests.cs`, "letter shapes: "), the game's side `LetterFormShapes.cs` (a partial of
`LetterForm`), the pools `Defs/FlavorPoolDefs/Rimfolk_Letters_Note`, `_Lead`, `_Story`, `_Raid`, `_Poem`, `_Sermon`,
`_Chronicle`, `_Set`, `_Hands`, `_Enclosure`, `_Diary`, `_Part` (each documents its tags in its header, for the next pass).
Everything of 0.202.0 is kept: the tone by situation and motive, the writer's people and kind, medieval English, the
unschooled hand, the strange voices. The heart (what the letter is for, which says what the game does) is never replaced:
a shape's pieces come after it.

- **The shapes** (`LetterKind`): the usual letter of 0.202.0; a bare note (a name for a salutation now and then, a word to
  start, the heart, a word to end, the name alone: `SignStyle.Short`); a long letter in parts (three or four, four or five
  at Long and storied: the news first when the facts hold some, everyday life, a story, a short verse, a raid's account,
  each now and then under a heading); a story told (a theme's opening, turn and ending, a moral or a joke now and then);
  a raid's account (how they came, who stood where, what burned, who fell, how it ended, after); a poem or a song, whole;
  a sermon or a tract, whole; a chronicle (a masthead in the writer's age, up to four items each about one real thing, a
  notice or two, its foot); a petition with signatures; a list or an account; a recipe or a remedy; a riddle (its answer
  kept with the letter and given in the writer's next P.S.); a letter by several hands (one to three of the others at home
  add a line each, "Pell adds: ..."); an enclosure described under the signature; a diary page (two or three days dated
  in the writer's way, `DiaryDays`) or a letter broken off and taken up again the next day. A call and words passed on
  keep their own shape.
- **Who gets which** (`Fits`): only a written letter, in a speech the shape has pieces in (`Speeches`, `PieceSpeech`: a
  barely schooled hand draws the plain pieces); never from a council, in the business between two peoples, or in a
  refusal; at war only the usual letter, a note, or a raiding people's boast of their raid on the colony. Long, storied
  letters (a long letter, a story, a diary) from pen friends, the warm, the lonely, the zealous and the talkative, in a
  letter about nothing in particular (`Chatty`: greetings, news, an invitation, a friend's word, their thanks, a letter
  written first that asks for nothing), warm or courteous; a story also from a tribe, the merry, the beast-folk and the
