  `RowLit` (the chosen row with the accent's edge down its left) and `RowHover`; and the scrollbars, whose game styles
  take a slim rounded thumb on a faint track while a window draws in the look and are put back after. Every control
  draws the game's own when the look is off, exactly as before, so a page calls one thing in either look.
- **The tokens have two values** (`UI/UiKit.cs`): each is a property, the game's value (as before) or Rimfolk's own
  (the mockup's palette, `SkinMath`: ground #17191b, panels #212427 and #2a2e32, edges #3a3f44, text #ece8df, secondary
  #b0aa9c, the accent #e0a845 as Gold, allied and friendly blue #6aa6dc as Warm, hostile orange #e08a45 as Sour, with Soon,
  Danger, Done, World, Cool and Link to match), chosen by `UiKit.BeginOwn`/`EndOwn` around a framed window's contents
  (always in a finally). So everything a framed window draws through the tokens and the kit (headings, rows, chips,
  modes, meters, cards, links) takes the look, and everywhere else (the council's windows until stage 2, the on-screen
  panels, the previews, the game's panes) the game's. Every text colour is at least 4.5:1 on the window, a panel and a
  card (tested), and colour still never stands alone: every stance and state has its word or icon beside it. New tokens
  for the frame and controls: WindowGround, Panel, Raised, RaisedHover, Pressed, Edge, EdgeStrong, Accent, AccentHover,
  AccentPressed, AccentInk, ShadowInk.
- **Type**: the game's fonts only (the only ones it loads): the window's title Small in ink beside its icon, a view's
  title Medium, everything read Small, what is glanced at Tiny in the secondary ink; numbers right-aligned (the trade
  window's columns of numbers and their headings in the look).
- **The region window in the look**: the title bar on the dark ground; the four views as tabs that read as tabs (the
  lit one a raised panel joined to the body, rounded at the top, the accent along it; the others quiet words that lift
  under the mouse, shrunk alike or to their icon where the window is narrow, `WindowTabs.DrawOwn`); the body a rounded
  panel. The map's lens bar and Map or List as raised pills and a segmented control in a dark well, the map's corners
  rounded into the panel with a faint edge, its zoom buttons on dark plates, the legend on a rounded strip; the List's
  rows with the chosen one lit by the accent's edge; Peoples' search as one rounded field with its icon, the filter
  chips as pills, the sort as a segmented control, the chosen people lit with the accent's edge, the page's tabs
  segmented, the acts as flat buttons greyed with why; the drawer a raised card with rounded corners (its soft shadow when
  it lies over the view). Wider, more is shown: Here and away and Peoples' Faces in two columns from a view of 1100
  (`RegionViewsMath.Columns`), Peoples' list 380 wide from a view of 1400 (`PeoplesViewMath.ListWider`) and the acts in
  three columns on a page of 1180 (`ActColumns`, `ActColumnWidth`); the map grows with the window, the drawer beside the
  view from a content area of 900 as before. The least is 720 by 480 (the drawer over the view).
- **The trade window in the look** (`Trade/Window_RimfolkTrade.cs`, a `FramedWindow` remembered as "Trade", least 980 by
  560, a dialog that may cover the bottom bar): "Trade with ..." in the title bar (the top keeps the negotiator's line and
  the buttons, the game's screen as a quiet button), the search as Rimfolk's field, the kind chips as pills (their words
  made once a trade now, not each frame), "only in the deal" as a switch, Sell and Buy as the kit's tabs, the columns of numbers and their headings
  right-aligned, the rows zebra-striped and lifting under the mouse, the side a raised card, the silver box (0.173.1's) a
  raised card with its soft shadow, washed and edged in the danger colour with its words when the colony can't pay;
  Accept the primary (accent) button, Reset quiet, Cancel, Fill and Clear flat. The game's own count control stays the
  game's.
- **Settings** (the How you're told page, beside the window size): `ownLook` ("Rimfolk's own look", on; off draws the
  game's look as before) and `windowsMove` ("Rimfolk's windows move and resize", on; off: the region window is the tab
  at the screen's foot again and the trade window opens as it did), and the action "Put Rimfolk's windows back"
  (`windowPlaces`). Keys in `Languages/English/Keyed/Rimfolk_OwnLook.xml`. Saved: nothing in the game (the places are the
  settings file's, modelled in `save_estimate.py`).
- **Tests** (`Tools/Tests/RimfolkLookTests.cs`): the frame on fourteen screens at five scales (opens in the middle,
  never off the screen, the least, large about 92% and back, dragged past every edge, sized from every edge and corner
  keeping the opposite one), the grips, the place written and read and refused, fitted to a smaller screen and large
  again; every text colour on every ground at 4.5:1, the accent's word on the accent; the rounded shapes (filled, cut,
  symmetric, smooth, a ring, a tab's top), the shadow, the 9-slice tiling any rect exactly with its UVs inside, the tabs
  sharing their row; the layouts at the least, standard, the old large and 92% of 1080p and 4K (the drawer, Peoples'
  page and list, the columns, the title bar's room, the trade window's foot); the seams (the settings, the keys, the
  region button's worker, Pages, the trade window, nothing made per frame where the kit draws, each control's game look).
  `LookTests` reads the tokens as two-valued now.
- **Not verified without the game**: the drag and the sizing by polling the mouse (a window that should never lag or
  stick), the scrollbars' styles swapped and put back (if the game's skin refuses, its scrollbars simply stay), the
  9-slices' look at interface scales other than 1 and 2, the floating window beside the game's tabs and the inspect pane
  (which is on top when), the text field's focus with the game's own key handling, the corner mask matching the panel.

#### Rimfolk's own look, stage 2: the four windows float, the Almanac and Rimfolk's dialogs in the frame (docs/design/rimfolk-look.md)

The player's request (8 November 2026) is stage 1's; stage 1 made the frame and the kit and put the region and trade
windows in them. Stage 2 is the rest of Rimfolk's windows: the council's, Planning and Defenses float as the region
window does, the Almanac and every dialog of Rimfolk's are in the frame, the pages draw with the kit, and the layouts
grow with the window. The existing behaviour stays: every address (`Pages.Open`), other mods' region pages, the drawer,
Escape, the corner, the keys and the settings work as before, floating or as tabs.

- **The four windows float** (`UI/FloatingWindows.cs`). `RimfolkFloatingWindow` is the region window's stage 1 pattern
  made common: a `FramedWindow` of the game's interface layer, not closed by a click outside it, letting the camera
  move, its title bar the window's icon, name and the corner, Escape a card's drawer first. `Window_Council`
  ("Council"), `Window_Planning` ("Planning"), `Window_Defenses` ("Defense") and `Window_Region` ("Region") each draw
  their tab's contents through one static draw the tab calls too (`MainTabWindow_Council.DrawCouncil`,
  `MainTabWindow_Planning.DrawPlanning`, `MainTabWindow_Defenses.DrawDefenses`, `MainTabWindow_World.DrawRegion`; the
  tabs' lists of tabs are static now, shared by both); the council's opening and closing (`Opening`: the page last
  looked at, or This week by the setting, unless a button asked; `Closing`: the page kept in the settings) are shared
  the same way. The least sizes: Region 720 by 480, Council and Planning 680 by 460, Defense 640 by 440 (the title bar's
  title, corner, large and close, a view's header and a page); each first asks for the windows' size (the setting
  "Window size").
- **The registry**: `FloatingWindows` makes each of the four once (by `RimfolkWindow`) and keeps it; `Showing`, `Shown`
  (the open one's place, for the on-screen panels), `Open`, `Shut`, `ShutAll`. One of the four at a time
  (`FramedWindowsMath.ToClose`, pure and tested for every set of open windows): opening one closes the other floating
  three; a window opening for the first time (no place of its own yet) takes the place of the one it turns the page
  from, so the corner still feels like turning a page. `Pages` asks it and names no window: `Showing` (floating or the
  tab), `Show` (floating where the windows move, closing any of Rimfolk's tabs; the tab otherwise, closing the floating
  ones; open already, brought to the front), `Close`, `OpenOrClose`, `OpenOrCloseSection` (the council section's close
  through `Close`), `LeaveForMap`, and the new `WindowOfButton` and `GoToGameTab`. A tab of the four opening closes the
  floating windows (`RimfolkTabWindow.PreOpen`).
- **The buttons**: one worker for the four (`MainButtonWorker_RimfolkWindow`: the floating window while the windows
  move, closed when it shows; the tab as before otherwise); the council's (`MainButtonWorker_Council`, with its count)
  and the region's (`MainButtonWorker_Region`) derive from it, and the defense and planning buttons take it in
  `Defs/Misc/Council_Misc.xml`, their tabs kept. The council alert's click opens the council through `Pages.Show`.
- **The tabs** (with "Rimfolk's windows move and resize" off) share one frame in Rimfolk's own look (`RimfolkTabWindow`:
  margin 0, no game background, the frame's title bar fixed at the screen's foot with the corner in it, the contents
  through `DrawContents`); `WindowTabs.DrawFor` draws a window's tabs in the look it is in (the own look's tabs, or the
  game's with the corner beside them unless the title bar has it).
- **Off to the map** (`Pages.LeaveForMap`): the floating windows close, and the open tab (the inspect pane kept: a jump
  picks who it shows). Every caller that closed the tab before a jump, a plan put down or a pick on the map uses it now
  (twenty-three: the council's `Jump`, This week's colonist, the people table's "show on the map", wishes and making's
  build buttons, the plan's ground plan, the ahead steps, the base's mini map, the defense page's map and its "Show",
  the Almanac's room plans, the room, defense, line-spot, save-room and rearrange designators, the defense lines'
  review, the mood view's and the bar badges' jumps, the landing from the game's menu), so no jump leaves a floating
  window over the map. A page sending the player to the game's research, quests or work tab goes through
  `Pages.GoToGameTab`: the window gives way, as the tab did.
- **The kit in the pages and dialogs**: `UiKit.Button` (now with the game's quiet mouseover where a page asked for it),
  `TextField` (the game's maximum length and validator overloads in its look; refused keys kept out in Rimfolk's),
  `Toggle` (disabled, and near its word, by the game's own overloads in its look), `RowHover`, and two new: `ListRow` (a
  choosable row: the game's highlight and gold edge, or the lit row with the accent's edge) and `Section` (a list's or a
  page's ground: the game's menu section, or a rounded panel). Every `Widgets.ButtonText`, `TextField`,
  `CheckboxLabeled` and `DrawHighlightIfMouseover` in Rimfolk's pages and dialogs is one of these; in the game's look
  each draws exactly what the page drew before. Left the game's on purpose: the mod settings, the inspect pane's story
  tab, the game's trade screen, the menu's landing option, the on-screen panels and their settings rows, the bar's own
  pin, the guest tab's button, the slow-time buttons, the docked room and defense planners, and Peoples' list's
  game-look search (it draws Rimfolk's in its own).
- **The colours follow the look**: the 69 `static readonly Color` copies of tokens (MoodView, HeartView, DecreePanel,
  AlmanacPanel, DefenseLinesPanel, the world's panels, the journey planner, the on-screen panels' kit and others) are
  properties (`static Color X => UiKit.Y`), so a page in a framed window draws the own look's values. A card's model is
  built for the look it is drawn in (`Cards.Model` keeps one set for each), so the same card in a framed window and in
  an on-screen panel each have their own colours. The self check makes its report outside the window's drawing, so its
  colours and its count of what needs a look are the same in either look.
- **The Almanac** (`Almanac/Window_Almanac.cs`, "Almanac", least 560 by 400): a `FramedWindow` that places itself the
  first time beside Rimfolk's windows (`OwnFirstPlace`), then where it was left between games; with the windows not
  moving it is the game's movable window as before, where it stood kept for the session. Its header keeps clear of the
  game's close cross only without the frame; its pages keep their own text sizes (`TextScale`), its search, switch,
  lists, panels and buttons the kit's.
- **Rimfolk's dialogs in the frame** (`FramedWindow(key)`, the key's least size and bottom bar from
  `FramedWindowsMath.Keys`): the letter window ("Letter", 580 by 740), the journey planner ("Journey", 760 by 540) and
  its picker ("JourneyPick", first beside the planner), the camp ("Camp"), the market ("Market", 820 by 400: its
  columns), the stall counter ("Stall", 980 by 560), the founding window ("Founding"), the floating card ("Card", its
  card's name in the bar), the feast, the journal, the news (the letter itself stays the game's), a calendar day, the
  clock, the self check, the bar's arranger, the guest check, the newcomers (the game's own pawn editor inside), the
  landing, the hand-over, the scenario start, naming a defense line and a room, a shelf's reserves and its picker, the
  floor picker (first beside the room planner), the ground plan and rearranging a room (first at the screen's right), a
  gift for an outsider and a panel's options. A dialog's least is the size it was made for where its contents don't
  scroll, smaller where they do; the frame's smallest is 360 by 160 now (a name asked for in a field and its OK). Their
  titles go in the title bar and are not said twice: `TitleTop` (the game's Medium title, or the contents just under the
  bar), `TitleAndLine` (the title and its quiet line, or the line alone) and `UiKit.DialogHeader` (the page header, or
  only its line and stat over the divider). The game's own close cross, close button, dragging and sizing a dialog asked
  for give way to the frame's while it shows (`FramedWindow.WindowOnGUI`; the close button drawn in the kit at the
  foot's middle, where it was) and come back with both settings off; a window's own margin is `UnframedMargin` and its
  own first place `PlaceUnframed` (both sealed in the frame), so the frame always places it. The primary act of each
  dialog (Send, Confirm, Found the colony, Choose, Put it to the meeting, Go ahead) is the accent's button.
- **Wider shows more** (the rules in `FramedWindowsMath`, tested from each least to 92% of 4K): This week in three
  columns from a page of 1500 (`WeekColumns`; two from 700 as before); the journey planner's overview of who goes 45% up
  to 640 from a planner of 1400 (`JourneyWhoWidth`), the founding window's 46% up to 600 (`FoundingWhoWidth`), the
  hand-over's to 600 and the scenario list's to 420 likewise; the camp's acts and switches up to half again as wide in a
  camp window twice its usual width (`DialogActWidth`); the market's goods' names take a wider window's room (up to 320
  more). The rest of the pages already lay out by their width (the people table's columns, the drawer beside or over,
  the Almanac's three columns, Peoples' list and acts from stage 1).
- **Previews and the search**: a name's preview takes Rimfolk's own look when the window its link is in draws in it (the
  look at the link is kept per level: rounded on the own look's raised panel, its hover rounded), and the game's from
  the game's panes and the on-screen panels; the corner's search opened from a window in the look is drawn in it (a
  rounded popup, the kit's field, the one lit with the accent's edge), the game's from its key. Both stay where they are
  (a preview at its link, the search under its icon).
- **Left as they were**: the on-screen panels and their edit bar (the map's layer, their own options; the panels take the
  look in stage 3, point 3), the room
  and defense planners docked above the architect menu (placed and sized to their content every frame: a frame would
  fight them), the search popup (a popup, not a window that moves), and the game's own windows (the mod settings, the
  inspect pane's tabs, the game's trade screen, choice letters: Rimfolk's own open as its event cards since stage 3).
- **Settings**: none new; "Rimfolk's own look" and "Rimfolk's windows move and resize" now cover every window above
  (their words in `Rimfolk_OwnLook.xml` say so). Saved: nothing in the game; the new windows' places go in the settings'
  `windowPlaces` by their keys, as stage 1's.
- **Tests** (`Tools/Tests/RimfolkLookStageTwoTests.cs`, "Rimfolk's own look, stage 2: ", some 1,700 checks): one of the
  four at a time for every window opening with every set of the four open (64), each key's least size on screens from
  1024 by 768 to 4K at scales 1 to 2 (opens on the screen, no smaller than its least there, large keeps it), the four
  windows' title bars at their least, the layouts above from each least to 92% of 4K, and the seams (Pages asks the
  registry and names no window, one worker on the four buttons, no jump closes only the tab, every Rimfolk window framed
  but those left as they were, each framed window's key in the table, the game's buttons giving way, the Almanac framed
  with its text sizes, no game widget left in the pages and dialogs, the kit's controls drawing the game's own
  overloads, no token copied at load, previews and the search in their window's look, the rules pure and linked).
  `RimfolkLookTests`, `PagesTests` and `LookTests` read the new seams.
- **Not verified without the game**: the four floating windows beside the game's tabs and the inspect pane (which is on
  top when; Escape going to the topmost); a page turned from one floating window to another (the closing one's place
  handed to the opening one); the game's close button drawn at a framed dialog's foot in the room the dialog left for
  it; the letter window at its least on a short screen (its contents don't scroll); the dialogs' text fields' focus in
  the frame; a preview's look following its link through two levels; the market's columns with and without Vanilla
  Trading Expanded at the window's least.

#### Rimfolk's own look, stage 3, point 1: event cards (docs/design/rimfolk-look.md)

The player (9 November 2026), asked which of Rimfolk's other screens could take the new look: "like the events, assuming
they still pop up the same way like normal game events do? i mean on the right side." So Rimfolk's letters arrive
exactly as the game's do (the letter stack on the right, its sound, its colour, its arrival, right-click and timeout as
before), and only the window that opens when one is clicked is Rimfolk's: an event card in the frame and the kit.

- **Which letters.** Every choice letter class of Rimfolk's (28: the dilemma, the council's meeting, a calendar day, the
  election, Rimfolk's events and the world's situations, the camps', the region's hamlet and raiders' camp, a journey,
  the founding and town letters, every diplomacy letter: calls to arms, envoys, ransoms, vassals, wards and hostages,
  matches, feasts, favours, fealty, pacts and truces; the colony news with no lines, the welcome and What's new) derives
  from one base, `RimfolkLetter : ChoiceLetter` (`UI/EventCards/EventCards.cs`), whose only change is `OpenLetter`: the
  card while the cards are on, else the game's own `ChoiceLetter.OpenLetter` as before. The colony news with lines keeps
  its own window (`Dialog_News`). Rimfolk's plain letters are the game's own `StandardLetter` (the teller's `Tell.Letter`,
  178 callers, with the game's kinds, and Rimfolk's own world-news LetterDefs): for these alone one patch, a prefix on
  `ChoiceLetter.OpenLetter` (`Patch_EventCardPlainLetter`) that acts only when the letter is exactly `StandardLetter` and
  Rimfolk's (its def from Rimfolk's content pack, or its ID kept by the teller), off with the deep hooks. The teller now
  makes the letter with `LetterMaker.MakeLetter` (what `ReceiveLetter` did inside) and keeps its ID
  (`EventCards.Mark`) in `EventCardsBook`, a small game component: the newest 400 (`EventCardMath.MaxPlain`), those no
  longer on the stack or in the History tab let go at each save (modelled in `save_estimate.py`). The game's own letters
  and other mods' are never touched; a death letter (the game's `DeathLetter`) stays the game's.
- **Built on the letter's own data.** When the card opens it takes the letter's first page as the game's own window does
  (`new DiaNode(Text)` with `Choices`, made once) and a hidden `Dialog_NodeTree` of the game's (`EventCardTree`, never
  added to the window stack) as the options' owner: an option chosen runs the game's own `DiaOption.Activate` (found once
  with `AccessTools`, the same steps written out if it can't be found), so its sound, the window closing (the tree's
  `Close` closes the card), its action and the page it leads to are the game's own; a page an option leads to is shown on
  the card. Disabled options keep their reasons; the letter's close, postpone and reject, its quest's page, its jump to
  the place and its links to info cards are recognised by the game's own words for them (`EventCardMath.RoleOf`, the
  answers' log's list) and drawn where they belong. Expiry, archiving and quests are untouched: the card, like the game's
  letter window, pauses the game and holds the map (`forcePause`, `absorbInputAroundWindow`), the History tab opens it
  through the same `OpenLetter`, the quest's button is the letter's own option. Its close button and Escape put it off
  (the letter stays on the stack, as "Postpone" does), except on a letter's last tick, when the game opens it for an
  answer and the card has no close (`EventCardMath.Closable`; `FramedWindow.FrameClosable`).
- **The header**: a picture of who or what it is about (the people's portraits from the game's cache, up to three
  overlapping, ringed in the letter's colour; else the thing in `UiKit.ItemPortrait`; else the people's emblem; else the
  kind's mark in the letter's colour), the title in the large type, the letter's kind as a chip with the letter's own
  colour beside its word (`EventCardMath.Kinds`: every LetterDef of Rimfolk's and the game's kinds its plain letters use,
  26 words in `Rimfolk_EventCards.xml`), the people it comes from with their stance and goodwill, and the jump to the
  place (the letter's own "Jump to location", else "Show on the map" where the camera can go). The title bar says
  "Letter" and when it came, so the title is said once.
- **The answers**, each a card: its words, the line under it as the setting "What each answer does" has it (the flavour
  line, the hint in words, or the numbers), what it costs and risks (the answer's costs and its gamble, in words or in
  numbers by the same setting, at most three and two lines, the rest named and all of it on hover), why it can't be
  chosen now; the whole card answers. `DiaOption_Impact` keeps its own words apart from the line (`bare`) and the
  answer's `OptionImpact` (`impact`), so the card reads what the letter read. On a dilemma that is a custom of the
  colony's, the answer that keeps it is marked "The colony's custom" with how it stands (a tradition, or kept so many
  years).
- **Who is involved**: the people the letter names (its class's own, `RimfolkLetter.Describe`: a question's two, the
  stranger, the second person, the pet, those who came; the meeting's proposers; the two of a match; the camp's one;
  a hand-over's going; then everyone its look targets name), up to eight, each with their portrait, their mood on a bar
  coloured by how near a break it is (the game's break thresholds), the heart's band as the colonist bar colours it
  (`HeartView.BandColor`, the good side's own colour), or who they are to the colony (a prisoner, a slave, a guest's
  people, an animal). A click goes to them on the map (the card closes, the letter stays).
- **What the council leans to**, only where it has a view: the meeting's votes (`EventCardMath.Lean`: the idea most are
  for, or a split room, in the meeting's own words) with each idea's backers on its card, and a hand-over's vote
  (`LeanForAgainst`). The dilemmas have no council vote, so none is made up for them.
- **The plumbing.** `EventCards.On`: Rimfolk's own look and the setting "Rimfolk's event cards" (`eventCards`, on, on the
  How you're told page under the look). Off, or a card that can't be read or drawn, the game's own window opens as
  before (`EventCards.OpenInGame`). The card is a `FramedWindow` with the key "EventCard" (least 520 by 440): it moves,
  sizes, goes large and opens where it was left; wider, who is involved and what the council leans to stand in a column
  beside the text (from a body of 760) and the answers go in two or three columns (`EventCardMath`, pure and tested).
- **Speed**: portraits from the game's cache; the letter's choices, the people's mood and heart, the words and the
  answers' lines are read once when the card opens (`EventCardModel`), the heights once a width; drawing is all a frame
  does.
- **Keys** in `Languages/English/Keyed/Rimfolk_EventCards.xml`. **Tests**: `Tools/Tests/EventCardTests.cs` (every
  LetterDef's kind and its word, the options' roles, closing without an answer, the council's lean, the layout from the
  least to 4K made large, the plain letters kept, the seams: one override, one patch on the plain class, the game's
  Activate, the setting, nothing read per frame); `OneRecordTests` reads the letters on their new base.
- **Not verified without the game**: the hidden node tree as the options' owner through every letter (the election's
  menu pages above all), the jump and quest buttons, the card's look with a long letter at its least, the portraits of
  people not on a map, the timing of a letter the game opens on its last tick, a plain letter from before this version
  (not kept, so it opens in the game's window until it leaves the stack).

#### Rimfolk's own look, stage 3, point 2: the Story tab at a glance (docs/design/rimfolk-look.md)

The player's words (9 November 2026): "story tab sounds great", to "The Story tab, done like the new Mood tab: at a
glance, life goal with a progress bar, current wish, quirks, standing in the colony, closest friends and rivals; the full
history below in folding sections." Built on the Mood tab's pattern (`MoodGlance`): a summary built with the tab's model
and drawn first, then folding sections remembered between sessions. The pure rules are `UI/StoryGlanceMath.cs` (linked
in the tests); the summary is `UI/StoryGlance.cs`; the tab and the page are `UI/ITab_Pawn_Story.cs` (`StoryView`). No
saved data, no Harmony patch, no Sched slot.

- **Who they are, in one line**, under their name in the tab's head, where the name the colony knows them by stood
  (`StoryView.Who`, kept two seconds): the name they're known by, the office they hold or the game's title for them,
  their age, and where they come from in the Culture tab's words ("a founder", "born here", "won over by Bo", "once among
  outlanders"; "a prisoner of the colony", "a slave of the colony"; `CultureView.RecruitedBy`, now internal). "The Healer
  · Steward · age 34 · a founder". Its tooltip has each in full: the "known as" line, the office, childhood and
  adulthood, years in cryptosleep, how long with the colony. The "In the council" button is as wide as its word.
- **At a glance** (`StoryGlance`), at the top of the scroll view, a row each, without scrolling at the inspect pane's
  usual height:
  - their character in words (it led the old overview; the Character section keeps the bars);
  - **their life goal**: "Wants to master cooking", how long they've held it ("held 12 days"), a gold bar for how far
    along, and its progress in the goal's own words with the share ("cooking 12 of 15 · 80%": what's next); the tooltip
    has the goal and why or since when they set their heart on it. A free colonist without one: "No life goal yet.";
  - the story they're living, with a dot for each stage (as before);
  - **their wish before the council**: their own first (the one nearest its last call, then the oldest), else one asked
    for them ("Bo wishes for ..."); how long they've waited, what fulfils it (or its progress), promised or last call,
    "(+1 more)" when there are others; its tooltip the wish in full (the words, the scene and quote, why, what fulfils
    it, progress, reward, the petition's names). Its acts are the wish cards' own: "Show me" (`MainTabWindow_Council.Jump`
    to `Worker.LookAt`) and "Promise" (`CouncilGameComponent.Promise`, greyed "Already promised."), beside the words at
    the tab's width, under them where the width is short (`StoryGlanceMath.WishLine`). Never a time left. A free
    colonist without one: "No wish before the council.";
  - **quirks** (and keepsakes, vendettas, nemeses) as the kit's tags, what each does in its tooltip (`QuirkEffects.Tip`);
  - **standing in the colony**: trust in the council on a small meter from -100 to 100 with ticks where its words change
    (-45, -15, 25, 60: `PawnStanding.LevelFor`), "Trust: trusting 38" in its colour, its tooltip the trust record and
    what moved it lately; then as tags the office they hold, their name as a doctor or how they're mending, and how the
    colony regards them ("Liked by 5", "Disliked by 1": colonists whose opinion of them is 20 or more, -20 or less, named
    in the tooltip);
  - **closest friends and rivals**: up to three each, a row each, small portraits (`UiKit.Portrait`, the game's
    `PortraitsCache`), name and opinion ("+45" warm, "-30" sour), the rest counted ("+2", named in its tooltip). A friend:
    the colonist's opinion at the game's friend line (20) or above, or an announced bond of friendship, fighting side by
    side or teaching and not against them now; a rival: -20 or below, or a bond of rivalry and not for them now; never
    both; closest first by opinion, then the bond's strength (`StoryGlanceMath`). Among the colony's people (free
    colonists and slaves, not babies or lodgers). The tooltip: their opinion both ways, the relation (flavour only:
    "Bo is her husband"), and Rimfolk's line about the two (`SocialColumn.PairNote`, worked out only on hover). A click
    selects them in the Story tab, as the game's Social tab does (`CameraJumper.TryJumpAndSelect`; their card when not on
    a map or in a caravan), and opens their card elsewhere. With nobody either way: "No close friends or rivals yet.";
  - **the newest line of their history** (`History.Of`, a season's summary passed over), how long ago, its names as links.
- **The sections below**, in order of use, each folding (`UiKit.FoldTitle`), remembered between sessions in the tab
  (`Folds.Remembered("story.sections")`, kept with the settings through `PageMemory`), their story and their wishes open
  at first, the rest folded:
  - **Their story**: the newest ten lines of their history, each with its day (a link to the entry's card) and its names
    as links (`CardWords.HistoryLine`), "Its whole history (N)" opening the region window's History on them
    (`WorldHistoryPage.ShowFor`), and the stories they lived through (`ArcView.Past`, moved here from "Life so far");
  - **Wishes**: each before the council now that they asked or that is for them (what fulfils it, progress, how long
    waited, promised, last call), then what came of the earlier ones (the history's granted, lapsed or taken back,
    refused or set aside, and petition lines, the newest eight), and "Every wish" to the Wishes page;
  - **Life goals**: the one under way in full (progress, how long held, why), the goals reached and the knacks they
    won't lose (as "Life so far" had them);
  - **Quirks and keepsakes**: each quirk with how it came, what it does and how long it lasts; the keepsakes', vendettas'
    and nemeses' lines;
  - **Friends and rivals**: every one, a row each (face, name, opinion, what they are to them, their opinion back), each
    clickable as above; then Rimfolk's bonds and those lost while the Social tab's column is off (the old "Bonds");
  - **Family**, **Recent dreams**, the **character page's** sections, **Across the years**, **Secrets** (while the column
    is off) and **From the journal**, as before ("Read the journal" now an act at the section's foot in the kit).
- **Kept**: every piece the tab showed. The family's portraits that led the old overview gave way to the friends and
  rivals (the colony is the family); the family tree's section has everyone with their faces, and its lines the family
  name and who they're named after. The overview's standing pills (trust, office, health) are the standing row.
- **Both looks**: drawn with the kit (`UiKit.Bar`, `Pills`, `RowAct`, `RowHover`, `Portrait`, `ActButton`): the game's
  look in the inspect pane, Rimfolk's own on a colonist's card, which draws the same page (`StoryParts.Card`, its own
  folds, all open). The family tree's rows light with `UiKit.RowHover`.
- **Speed**: the glance is built with the page's model, at most twice a second for each place it shows (again after a
  promise), and drawn only from it: nothing translated while drawn (the few fixed words translated once), the
  opinions, the history and the wishes read only when it is built, Rimfolk's line about two people only on hover.
- **Tests**: `Tools/Tests/StoryGlanceTests.cs` (friends and rivals at every opinion and bond, their order, the portraits
  that fit, the trust meter, the rows from 200 to 900 wide, what the glance shows and from what, nothing worked out or
  translated while drawn, the sections' order and folds, every piece the tab showed still there, the words).
- **Not verified without the game**: the glance's height at the inspect pane's usual height in both looks (that it fits
  without scrolling with a long wish and two rows of people), the who line's width beside the button, the wish's acts
  (Show me leaving for the map, Promise greying at once), a friend's click selecting them with the tab staying open on
  them, the portraits' rings, the tooltips' order, the trust meter's ticks at 8 high, the card's narrower width in
  Rimfolk's look, a prisoner's and a slave's page.

#### Rimfolk's own look, stage 3, point 3: the on-screen panels (docs/design/rimfolk-look.md)

The player (9 November 2026): "on-screens overall look great now, but if you can improve them further, go ahead! perhaps
keep the current setup as a backuip somewhere." So the panels and the hover card take Rimfolk's own look, aimed at a
glance during play (less text, more shape), and the panels as they were stay behind a setting as the backup.

- **The backup.** "Classic on-screen panels" (`hudClassic`, off, under On-screen panels; put back with the panels'
  reset): on, every panel and the hover card draw through the code they drew with before, unchanged. The look is drawn
  only with "Rimfolk's own look" on and the classic panels off (`HudLook.Refined`); with the look off they are always
  the classic ones. Each panel is one class in two files: the classic file keeps its drawing as it was and branches to
  the look at the top of `DrawBody` (and of `Measure` where the look's rows differ), and the look is in
  `Hud/Look/<Panel>Look.cs` (`partial` classes). `HudPanel.Contents` branches to `ContentsLook` the same way, the hover
  card's `CardFor` to `CardLook`. Places, sizes, options, clicks, menus, the edit bar and the layout are shared, and a
  panel's saved state (`HudPanelState`) has nothing new: saved layouts are the same in either.
- **Decided when a panel gathers.** `HudPanel.RefreshNow` latches the look (`look`) and whether the title row is inside the
  card (`inline`: the look and not compact) before `Refresh` and `Measure`, so a panel's size and its drawing always
  agree; gathering runs in the look's colours (`UiKit.BeginOwnColours`, new: the look's tokens without the scrollbars'
  styles), so the colours a panel keeps and its tooltips' inks are the look's. `HudLook.Watch` (once a frame from
  `HudManager.Update`) marks every panel to gather again and the hover card to be built again when the look changes (the
  setting, Rimfolk's own look, a timing run).
- **Cards** (`HudLook.Card`): the look's rounded fill (`UiKit.Round`, radius 8) in its panel colour (the darker and clear
  looks in its window ground), as solid as the panels' look says (`HudLookMath.CardAlpha`: dark 0.95, darker 0.97, clear
  0.72, times the panel's own opacity, fuller under the mouse) and its edge only while the mouse is on it (nine more draws
  a panel every frame otherwise). A full card has a **title row** (16 at scale 1) with the panel's icon (`HudIcons.For`)
  and name in the heading's ink; while the mouse is on the panel (or they are arranged) its right end holds the bar's
  buttons (the panel's own, compact or full, the background, options, hide), the rest of the row drags it, a right-click
  opens the menu, and nothing pops out over the panel (`frame` is the body). Compact panels keep the bar over them as
  before, drawn as a quiet rounded strip. While arranging, an accent edge round each card. A card sits on whole pixels.
- **Severity by form.** An urgent row has a stripe down its left edge (3 at scale 1) in the colour of how much it matters,
  pulsing for life and limb, and its icon in that colour; no wash over the row (the danger red's words would fall under
  4.5:1 on a reddened row over a bright map). Alerts: the stripe in the priority's colour (pulsing for critical), the
  warning icon on critical and high ones, the count small at the right, the flash of a new one kept.
- **Bars, not numbers, where a value has a range** (flat: a bar this small shows no corner, and a rounded one costs nine
  draws): the mood with its break lines and where it is heading (`HudLook.MoodBar`), the number small beside it in the
  bar's colour at full strength (`HudLook.MoodInk`); the heart's line under it (`HudLook.HeartLine`: strain in its band's
  colour, strained's faintly below it, the marks where strained, worn down and near breaking begin once strain has reached
  the first, the good side in its own colour under it; the heart's meters' colours and marks, `HeartMeterMath`); health as
  their summary health under the name (a thin, muted line since 0.201.1, the illnesses under it in the main font with wider bars first: the player, "the illness should have more prominence than the health bar"); food, rest and recreation as three short bars one over the other, a low one in the
  danger colour; on the vitals, days of food against the warning line (its middle) with the bad line, medicine against
  the advisor's two a colonist, the research under way; on the council, trust either side of nothing (`HudLookMath`:
  `FoodFill`, `StockFill`, `TrustBar`); on the inventory's essentials, the meals' days of food. The numbers stay small
  beside the bars and in the tooltips.
- **Rimfolk's newer marks on a colonist's row** (`Hud/Look/HudLookFacts.cs`, gathered with the row at most twice a
  second, the words made only when what they say changed): the heart's band (the heart's line, and the heart mark from
  worn down), a day off or a bad afternoon under way (`HudIcons.DayOff`, new; its tooltip `HeartTimeOff.UntilText`; on
  work and idle a chip in the idle mark's place, so their idling is explained), an empty slot in their weapon kit
  (`HudIcons.KitGap`, new: read from the colony's kept choice, `WeaponPick.Current` and `Picks.Kit`, again only when the
  choice was made again, never made here; "No melee weapon. Their gear tab says what the colony has for it."). On the
  inventory a weapon the colony keeps carries the rating's badge (the best one in storage, `WeaponLive.Of`, read again
  every five seconds at most; in its band's colour, `WeaponUi.RatingColour`), and the grid's tile a line in it.
- **The panels.** Mood board: portrait ringed by the mood's line, the name as a link, the marks at the line's end (a
  break, the heart from worn down, time off, an empty kit slot, a wish, faith wavering), the mood bar, its number, the
  heart's line, what drags them down; compact cells with the mood filled light enough under the initials, the break
  lines and the heart's band along the foot. Mood trend: the latest average and lowest beside a dot in each line's
  colour, the values under the mouse (made for every point when the samples change), the part under the minor break
  line washed once and the line drawn once (the classic's dashes were some thirty draws). Vitals, council and Following:
  icon, words, the bar and the value. Alerts as above. Health: the stripe, the name and how they stand, the health bar,
  the conditions as before (the classic's chips and lines, laid out once a gathering). Work and idle: the colony's lines
  with their stripe, the rows with their chip and the three bars. Inventory (at the classic's sizes): the game's icons on
  whole pixels, the change as a small arrow and number, the badge, grouped headers as quiet bands. The hover card:
  rounded, portrait, name (a link in the corner), the mood small, the mood bar and the heart's line across, what matters
  most with its stripe and icon, what would help beside or under it, time off and an empty kit slot, what they are doing.
- **Icons tidied**: one size a row (`HudLook.IconSize`, 13 at scale 1; the marks 12), drawn square and on whole pixels
  (`HudLook.Snap`, `ScaleMode.ScaleToFit`); five new glyphs in `Tools/make_icons.py` (Trend, Vitals, Stock for the title
  rows; DayOff and KitGap for the marks), the same weight as Rimfolk's set.
- **Readability**: the look's type scale (the title Tiny in the heading's ink, names and values in the panels' main font,
  what is secondary Tiny in the faint ink) and contrast: every text colour holds 4.5:1 on the card over bright snow for
  the dark and darker looks and over the game's soil for the clear one, on the row under the mouse too, and a compact
  cell's initials on the mood's fill (tested). Coloured words never sit on a tint of their own colour (work's chips carry
  their word in ink).
- **Sizes and places.** The lines and alerts' rows are 18 (the classic's 20) and work's 18, so the cards, title rows and
  all, still start clear of one another and of the game's interface where Rimfolk places them at 1080p and 1440p (the
  classic test's typical sizes, in the look); the inventory keeps the classic's sizes, the mood board's rows are 36 (the
  heart's line under the bar). A colonist's row is laid out by `HudLookMath.LayMoodRow` at every scale (0.75 to 1.5)
  with nothing on top of anything else.
- **Speed.** These draw every frame, so in the look: every word, number and percentage is made when the panel gathers
  (twice a second) or from tables made once (`HudLookFacts.Percent`, the inventory's counts), a text's width is measured
  once and kept (`HudLook.Width`), tooltips are made only while they show by a maker kept with the row (no delegate a
  frame), words are drawn on repaint only, and the window skips the layout pass (the classic ran all its drawing code for
  it as well). Counted from the code for the default panels and ten colonists: the classic makes some 240 objects
  (percentages, "-8 No bedroom", counts, tooltips' delegates) and measures some 80 texts in each pass, and it runs two
  passes a frame where the game sends the layout pass; the look makes none and measures none once its words are known, for
  some 760 draws a frame against the classic's 670 (the cards' rounded fill, the title rows, the heart's line and the
  bars, less the trend's thirty dashes). **The clock** (`HudLook`, `HudLookMath.Clock`): every panel's
  painting is timed for the look it was drawn in (two stopwatch readings a panel), and the debug action "On-screen
  panels: time the classic and refined drawing (log)" paints 300 frames in the look, then 300 classic, and writes both
  in the log ("... painting time so far" writes them at any time).
- **Keys** in `Languages/English/Keyed/Rimfolk_HudLook.xml`. **Tests**: `Tools/Tests/HudLookTests.cs` (contrast on every
  card over the map and under the mouse, the compact cells, the card's solidity, the cards starting clear at 1080p and
  1440p, a colonist's row at every scale, the bars, the clock and its timing run, the setting and its words, the classic
  kept and branched from, the look latched when gathering, the layout pass skipped, nothing made in any drawing method of
  the look, the kit read from the kept choice only, the marks, the icons, saved layouts untouched).
- **Not verified without the game**: the look itself at every scale and look (dark, darker, clear) over real maps; the
  timing (the debug action gives it); the title row's buttons and dragging by it; the layout pass skipped (that nothing
  of the game's needs it, the inventory's search box above all); the heart's line at 2 pixels a side at small scales; the
  day off and kit marks with a real day off and a real empty slot; the rating badge (the game's resource count includes
  weapons only where a mod or the game counts them as resources); the compact bar in the look; the hover card in the
  corner with its link.

#### Rimfolk's own look, stage 3, point 4: the colonist card (docs/design/rimfolk-look.md)

The player's words (9 November 2026): "colonist card would be cool!", to "A colonist card: one window per colonist with
portrait, heart bars, mood, skills and passions, kit (weapons and armour with ratings), wishes, life goal, standing side by
side; from the colonist bar and Rimfolk's windows." The window is `UI/ColonistCard/ColonistCardWindow.cs`, its model
`ColonistCardModel.cs`, its rules `ColonistCardMath.cs` (pure, linked in the tests), the ways in from the game's own
interface `ColonistCardEntry.cs`. No saved data, no Sched slot; two Harmony patch classes, each applied on its own.

- **What it replaced**: "the colonist's card" was the small card of the card system (`UI/Cards/`, `CardKind.Colonist`:
  a head, the Story page with the card's own parts and the sections other parts register, `HeartCard`'s meters, lines and
  advice among them), shown in a window's drawer or the floating `Window_Card`. **A colonist's card is now the colonist
  card**: `Cards.Open` sends one of the colony's own, alive (a colonist or a slave, `ColonistCardWindow.Fits`), to it,
  so every way it opened before opens it (every name link and portrait in Rimfolk's windows, the People table's rows, the
  Moods page, This week, the Defenses page, the on-screen panels' names, the Story glance's friends and rivals, the Social
  tab's column, previews, search). Prisoners, the dead and everyone else keep the small card. The small card still opens
  for a colonist through "Whole story" (`MainTabWindow_Council.OpenPerson`: the drawer beside the People table, with
  their whole story), and has an act "Their card" back. The setting "Rimfolk's colonist card" (`colonistCard`, on, How
  you're told, beside the event cards) off: everything as before.
- **The window** (key "ColonistCard", least 460 by 440, first 1100 by 740, beside play above the bottom bar): one per
  colonist, several open at once (`onlyOneOfTypeAllowed` off). **Each card moves and sizes on its own; they share one
  remembered place**: a new frame of its own for each card (`WindowFrame.Own`, known to "Put Rimfolk's windows back" while
  open), where the last one was moved, sized or made large remembered under the key; a card opened while others are open
  steps a title bar's height down and right of any already there, so every title bar shows (`ColonistCardMath.Cascaded`).
  Not per colonist: a colony's thirty would each leave a line in the settings file, and colonists' ids change from game
  to game. Opening a colonist whose card is open brings it to the front. **The arrows** in the title bar step to the
  previous or next colonist in the colonist bar's order (round the ends), past any whose card is open in another window,
  so it stays one card per colonist (`ColonistCardMath.Step`); their tooltips name who.
- **The header**: their whole figure as dressed from the game's portrait cache (100 by 140, a tile in the look); under
  it the heart's line as the colonist bar draws it (strain in its band's colour, the good side in green, each as long as
  it is full, from the bar's threshold; its tooltip the heart's line in words); their full name; who they are in the
  Story tab's one line (`StoryView.Who`: the name the colony knows them by, office or title, age, where they come from;
  in full on hover); chips for a break, downed, drafted, their role in the ideoligion (Ideology, in its colour and icon),
  the Empire's title (Royalty: the Empire keeps its own titles and honour), and where they are (a caravan, away, another
  map).
- **At a glance**, in columns that fit the width (`ColonistCardMath.Columns`: 240 wide at least, one to four; which part
  goes in which column fixed for each count, so nothing jumps as a part grows: one stacks them, two put Now and Skills
  left and Kit and Life right, three keep Skills under Now), the body scrolling as one:
  - **Now**: the Mood tab's bar with the break lines and where it heads (`MoodView.DrawBar`), then the Mood tab's glance
    as it is (`MoodGlance.Draw`: the heart's two meters with the day off's place, "Give a day off" or the day off or bad
    afternoon under way with "End it early"; the mood's sentence; what weighs and lifts most, three each; what the bands
    do; the top advice with its buttons).
  - **Skills**: every skill in the game's order (`listOrder`), a bar out of 20 with the level, the passion's mark (the
    game's, or Vanilla Skills Expanded's own from its passion defs, read softly by name: `Passions`), those they can't
    do marked "can't" and greyed; "Best at ..." names up to three at 6 or more (a burning passion before an interest at the
    same level), shown in gold. The tooltip: level and the game's word for it, the skill's description, the passion and
    how fast they learn it, the experience to the next level, an aptitude.
  - **Kit**: the weapon in hand, the off hand (Dual Wield) and the weapons carried (Simple Sidearms' sidearms named so),
    each with its picture in its quality's frame (`UiKit.ItemPortrait`), the rating's badge (`WeaponLive`), what it is to
    them and its rating for them (`WeaponLive.ForColonist`) or that they can't use it; the kit's gaps and better weapons
    as the gear tab has them (`WeaponPick.Standing`, the gear tab's heads, acts and tooltips: Equip, As sidearm, a trade),
    and an empty slot nothing in storage fills; then the apparel by slot (head, body, legs, hands, feet, belt; a piece
    covering the body listed with it, a belt's layer first: `ColonistCardMath.SlotOf`), each with its picture, badge
    (`ApparelLive`), its rating for them (`ApparelLive.ForColonist`) and what is left of a worn piece; and whether they
    are dressed for the season ("no warm coat": the game's comfortable range as dressed against the season's coldest
    and hottest where they are, `ApparelLive.Climate`, a degree's leeway). A click on any item opens Rimfolk's weapon or
    apparel card for them, the game's card for an item neither rates. **A hook for the apparel suggestions**
    (`ColonistCardHooks.KitLines`): lines under the apparel with an act each, built with the kit; not used yet (the
    apparel suggestions are another piece of work).
  - **Life**: the Story tab's glance as it is (`StoryView.Glance`, built alone without the page's sections: their
    character in words, life goal with its bar, the story they're living, the wish with "Show me" and "Promise", quirks
    as chips, standing with the trust meter, closest friends and rivals with portraits, a click opening their card,
    the newest line of their history); then the lines other parts add to a colonist's card (a ward, a ransom, a match:
    `CardSections` of `CardKind.Colonist`), less what the card shows its own way (the heart's lines, the name).
- **The foot**: Mood, Story, Gear and Health (select them, the camera going to them, and open the game's tab: the Needs tab
  where Rimfolk's Mood tab is off; greyed with why for someone away), "Go to them" (the camera only), "Select", "Whole
  story" (the council window's People table with their whole story in the drawer), and "More" when other parts let the
  colony do something from a colonist's card (a ward's guardian, an envoy recalled; each greyed with why not), the day
  off left to the Now part's place. Two rows when narrow (`ColonistCardMath.FootRows`).
- **The ways in from the game's interface**, each leaving the game's own clicks as they are:
  - **The colonist bar: Ctrl and a click on a portrait** (Command on a Mac). `Patch_ColonistCardBarClick`, a prefix on
    `ColonistBarColonistDrawer.HandleClicks` beside the badges' own: it takes only a left press with Ctrl on a colonist's
    portrait (`Event.Use`, so the bar neither selects nor starts a drag from it) and never skips the game's method. A
    plain click still selects, a double-click still goes to them, the right button's drag still reorders, Shift and a click
    still adds to the selection. A right-click was not taken: the bar reorders by dragging with it. Setting "Ctrl-click
    on the colonist bar opens the card" (`colonistCardBar`, on, needs the card and the deeper hooks).
  - **The inspect pane: a small card button by the name** of a colonist selected alone. `Patch_ColonistCardPaneButton`,
    a postfix on `MainTabWindow_Inspect.DoInspectPaneButtons(Rect, ref float lineEndWidth)`: the button left of the game's
    own buttons there (the info card, the response to danger), counted in the line's end so the name makes room for it, as
    the game's own do. Not a gizmo: the player asked for the day off to leave the colonist's command bar. Setting "A card
    button on the inspect pane" (`colonistCardPane`, on, needs the card and the deeper hooks).
  - **An event card's "who is involved"**: a small card button at the right of each colonist's row
    (`ColonistCardEntry.RowButton`); the rest of the row still goes to them on the map.
  - The drawer's small card for a colonist: "Their card".
- **Speed**: the model is built when the card opens, its live parts twice a second (the mood and its glance, the heart's
  line, the header's chips, the arrows' neighbours), its heavy parts every three seconds (who they are, skills, kit with
  its ratings and suggestions, life, the other parts' lines and acts, the foot's tooltips) and at once after an act on the
  card or a promise anywhere (`StoryView.Staled`); before the window draws, once a frame at most. Drawing reads the model:
  nothing translated, rated, read from the map or the history while drawn (the words translated once). The ratings
  themselves are the weapon and apparel readers' own caches (an hour each).
- **New icon**: ColonistCard (a card with someone's head and shoulders and three lines; `Tools/make_icons.py`, only that
  PNG written). **Keys** in `Languages/English/Keyed/Rimfolk_ColonistCard.xml`. **Tests**: `Tools/Tests/ColonistCardTests.cs`
  (the columns from the least to 4K made large and which part goes where, the header and the foot at the least, building
  twice a second and every three, the arrows' step, eight cards open apart and on every screen, the heart's line, the
  skills' bars and best, the worn pieces' slots, dressed for the season, every colonist's card opening it, several at
  once in frames of their own, the ways in that leave the game's clicks alone, nothing made while drawn, what it reuses,
  the settings and every word).
- **Not verified without the game**: the card's look in both looks at its least and made large; the portrait's size and
  framing from the cache; the heart's line under it; the inspect pane button's place beside the game's own (that the
  game's buttons count themselves in the line's end in 1.6 and 1.7 as their code reads, and other mods' buttons there);
  the Ctrl-click on the bar with every other click unchanged (and on a Mac); several cards open, moved and made large, the
  remembered place and the step down; the arrows across maps and caravans; Vanilla Skills Expanded's passion marks; the
  tabs opening from the foot for someone on another map; the weapon and apparel rows, badges and suggestions on real
  colonists (Simple Sidearms, Dual Wield); the season's verdict on a real map; the event card's button.

#### Rimfolk's own look, stage 3, point 5, step 1: the item card for food, drink, drugs and medicine (docs/design/rimfolk-look.md)

The player (9 November 2026): "also like item card for everything, although i fear that would take a lot of
ressources?" They were told it is built only when opened and kept, costs nothing in play, and comes in steps: food,
drink, drugs and medicine first, then materials, art and the rest. Step 1 is built. Released 0.198.0.

- **Which things** (`Items/ItemCardLive.KindOf`, the rule in `ItemCardMath.KindOf`): an item (never a weapon, apparel, a
  corpse, a building or a creature) that is medicine; a drug, which is a drink when it is drunk (beer, tea, go-juice) and
  a drug otherwise; food that is drunk (a mod's juice, milk) is a drink; anything else that feeds is food (meals, raw
  food, animal feed). Everything else opens the game's card as before.
- **The card** (`Items/ThingCardWindow.cs`, key "ItemCard", least 440 by 460, on `UI/ItemCardWindow.cs`, whose head now
  draws without a rating's badge, `HeadFacts.NoBadge`): the thing's own picture large in its quality's frame
  (`UiKit.ItemPortrait`, as it really is), its label with the stack and quality, what kind it is and its worth ("Meal,
  fine · $20 each, $200 the stack"), "All the game's stats", and **a line in plain words** on what it is good for
  here (`ItemCardMath.Plain`: "Fine meal: lifts the mood (+5), keeps 4 days, enough for 2 colonists' supper." "Herbal
  medicine: fine for a cut or a cold, risky for surgery." "Yayo: a hard drug, lifts the mood (+35) for 18 hours, can
  overdose, addictive."). Then its **tags** as the weapon card's chips (`WeaponUi.Chips`, the shared six categories of
  `WeaponTagMath`), each with why in its own numbers or Rimfolk's own rule, at most eight, the first strength and
  weakness kept (`ItemCardMath.Tags`):
  - **Strength**: *Nutritious* (a meal's worth, 0.9, in a piece), *Keeps long* (never rots, or 20 days or more), *Mood
    lift* (the game's thought for eating it, or the thought on a drug's high), *Potent* (medicine at least as potent as
    industrial), *Recreation* (a dose gives joy).
  - **Weakness**: *Spoils fast* (rots within 5 days above 10 °C), *Raw* (the game's "ate raw food" eaten as it is, and a
    recipe of the colony's cooks it), *Bad taste* (another bad thought: paste, kibble), *Risky for surgery* (medicine
    under industrial potency: surgery fails more often, tending stops lower).
  - **Risk**: *Of a person* (human meat or made with it), *Overdose risk* (a dose adds toward an overdose, the range and
    the chance of a large one named), *Addictive* (the game's chance a dose, and the tolerance it needs first), *Food
    poisoning* (the stack's own chance from its cook and kitchen, its kind's for people, certain once it rots; half a
    percent or more, by the storyteller's factor), *Forbidden to some* or *to most* (the colony's grown people whose
    faith, diet or nature rules it out, named with why: Wishes/Beliefs.cs), *Insect meat*.
  - **Special**: *Feast's dish* (`ThingRole.Feast`: a fine or lavish meal, what the Empire's guests expect), *Toast's
    drink* (`ToastDrinks.IsToastDrink`: alcohol, or a drink a teetotaler may have for those who don't drink), *Gift for a
    people* (`ThingRole.Gift`: a fine drink worth 15 silver or more).
  - **Role**: *Provisions* (`ThingRole.Provisions`, the journey planner's road food: first when it never rots), *Trade
    good* (keeps, and 50 silver a kilogram or more), *For serious care* or *For minor wounds* (with medicine by what is
    treated on: `MedicineChoiceMath.NeedsCare`, herbal for the minor, better for the serious), *Needed now* (the colony is
    under the trade advice's ten days of food, or under its medicine floor), *Spare to sell* (more than twice the ten
    days, or more medicine than the trade advice keeps).
  - **Needs**: *Cooking* (raw food a recipe the colony has unlocked makes a meal of, its bench named), *Drug policy*
    (how many policies at home allow it), *Freezer* (it spoils fast and the colony keeps nothing cold).
- **As food** (food, and a drink that isn't a drug): nutrition a piece, the stack's and its colonist-days (1.6 a day), or
  how many make a meal's worth; how it keeps (its kind's days above 10 °C, slower in the cold, never at or below 0 °C,
  and this stack's days left where it lies by the game's own `CompRottable.TicksUntilRotAtCurrentTemp`, or kept cold, or
  rotting); the game's thought for eating it; food poisoning (the stack's own `CompFoodPoisonable.PoisonPercent`, its
  kind's `FoodPoisonChanceFixedHuman`, or for a kind of meal the colony's surest cook's `FoodPoisonChance`); the road (the
  journey planner's order, `ThingRolesMath.TravelRank`, and what it doesn't pack); a feast's dish. **Who at home eats it**:
  each colonist with the mood it gives them (`FoodUtility.MoodFromIngesting`), or why they won't (their nature or title,
  `FoodUtility.WillEat`; their food policy; their beliefs, `BeliefMath.WhyNotEat`: meat, alcohol, paste, fungus, insects,
  fine meals only; a bad thought of their own from a precept or a trait, by name, such as eating human meat). The shared
  raw or rotten mood is no refusal.
- **What it does** (drinks and drugs): each hediff its doses give with how long one lasts (its severity over its fall a
  day, or its own time to go), the game's own words for its stage (`HediffStatsUtility.SpecialDisplayStats`) and the mood
  of its thought; needs a dose moves; recreation; addiction (the chance a dose, the tolerance first); tolerance (a dose's,
  and its fall a day); overdose; the toast; a gift; how it keeps where it rots. **Who may take it**: each colonist's drug
  policy for it (for recreation, on a schedule, only for an addiction, not allowed, not in the policy), their beliefs, an
  addiction; each faith at home with its precepts on drugs and alcohol.
- **As medicine**: its potency and the best tending it allows, the medical care that allows it, how it keeps (herbal
  medicine rots in 150 days), what Rimfolk's medicine by what is treated gives it to (or the game's rule with that off),
  and surgery's risk under industrial potency. **The doctors**: up to five, the best first, with their tending with it
  and without any (`TendUtility`'s rule: the doctor's tend quality times the potency, held at the medicine's best;
  `ItemCardMath.TendQuality`), and how much better industrial medicine would do for them.
- **The colony's stock**: how many the colony holds (on the map, not forbidden, and in its people's packs); for food the
  days of food in all (`MapFacts.FoodDays`) and this kind's share, short or spare by the trade advice's rules
  (`TradeAdviceMath`); for medicine every kind together against the floor and reserve; for a drug who is addicted. **Where
  it is made**: each recipe that makes it, its bill on a bench (a click goes to the bench and opens its bills), a bench
  that could take one, the bench to build or the research it waits on; crops that grow it, a click going to the field.
- **Trade**: its worth (each and the stack) and a kilogram's; the kinds of trader who deal in it (`TraderKindDef.WillTrade`),
  who asks the least and who pays the most where the game's price types differ; Vanilla Trading Expanded's market for it
  read as the trade window reads it (`TradeMarket.MarketLines`), and the colony's own last prices (`TradeMarket.RecordLines`).
- **Open it first** (`Items/ItemCardFirst.cs`): the weapons' one prefix on `WindowStack.Add` (`Patch_WeaponCardFirst`) asks
  the item card first (its kinds are never weapons or apparel), then the weapon and apparel cards as before. Its own
  let-through for "All the game's stats"; navigation inside the game's card stays the game's
  (`WeaponCardFirst.insideGameCard`); a postfix on `Dialog_InfoCard.DoWindowContents` (`Patch_ItemCardButton`) draws
  "Rimfolk's item card" at the foot of the game's card for these kinds, so the way back is always there. Setting
  `itemCardFirst` "Open Rimfolk's item card first" (How you're told, Items; on; needs the deeper game hooks).
- **Speed.** Nothing is read while the card is closed, and nothing in play. A kind's own numbers (rot, taste, drug,
  effects and their thoughts, potency, roles, the recipes and crops that make it, the traders) are read once when its
  card first opens and kept for the session (`ItemCardLive.PartOf`). The card's model (`ItemCardModel`) is built when it
  opens: the thing's live parts (the stack, how long it keeps where it lies, its poisoning) are read again at most once a
  second, the colony's (who eats or takes it, the doctors, the stock, the bills, the market) at most every ten seconds; the
  window draws only from the model's finished words.
- **Text:** `Languages/English/Keyed/Rimfolk_ItemCard.xml`; the tags' labels and reasons and the line in plain words are
  English from the pure rules, as the weapon and apparel tags are. **Tests:** `Tools/Tests/ItemCardTests.cs` (some 400
  checks): the kinds; the sums (colonist-days, suppers, a meal's worth, tending, short and spare, poisoning odds, the
  words for shares, days and moods); the tags and line of the base game's fine, simple and survival meals, pemmican,
  potatoes, raw and rotting meat, a cooked stack, kibble, hay, human and insect meat, beer, a fine wine, tea, yayo, herbal,
  industrial and glitterworld medicine, the colony short, spare, minding and without a cold store; the vocabulary, the cut
  to eight, clean words; the seams (the hook and its pass-through, the button back, the setting, the frame, the head
  without a badge, the model built once and refreshed rarely, nothing read from the game while drawing, every key).
- **Not verified without the game**: the card's look at its least width and the head without a badge; the drug effects'
  words from `HediffStatsUtility` for every base and modded high, and their durations from the hediffs' comps; the
  thoughts on highs found by `ThoughtDef.hediff`; `FoodUtility.ThoughtsFromIngesting` and `MoodFromIngesting` for a kind
  with no thing in hand; a fridge mod's stack read as kept cold; the game's price types per trader; the jump to a bench
  and its bills tab, and to a field; the swap through the shared hook and "All the game's stats" coming back; how long the
  first card of a kind takes to read with the player's mods (the recipes and traders are looked through once).

#### Rimfolk's own look, stage 3, point 5, step 2: the item card for materials and art (docs/design/rimfolk-look.md)

The second step of the item card for everything (the player, 9 November 2026: "also like item card for everything, although i
fear that would take a lot of ressources?"): materials and art. Released 0.200.0. The rest (books, body parts, techprints,
trainers, genepacks, one-use artifacts, shells, minified furniture) is step 3, below.

- **Which things** (`ItemCardLive.KindOf(def, thing)` reads an `ItemSort`, the rule `ItemCardMath.KindOf(ItemSort)`, step 1's
  kinds first): **art** is anything with the game's art comp (`CompProperties_Art`), an item or a building, held, minified
  (read as the piece inside, `GetInnerIfMinified`, the picture the crate as it lies) or placed; a grave whose art shows only
  once it is full (`mustBeFullGrave`) only while full and its art active. A **material** is an item that is stuff, or that the
  game files under raw resources, manufactured goods or chunks (`IsWithinCategory` of `ResourcesRaw`, `Manufactured`, `Chunks`,
  `StoneChunks`, so the mods' own categories under them come in), and is not a thing to use, read, install or fire (a shell,
  a body part, an unfinished thing, a techprint, a trainer, anything with a use comp, a book, a genepack, a xenogerm or an
  embryo: step 3's, `ToUse`). So metals, wood, stone blocks, cloth, leathers, wools, the mods' stuffs (beeswax, synthamide,
  a mod's metal), stone chunks and slag, components, chemfuel, neutroamine, shards, silver and gold. Weapons, apparel and
  pawns are never the item card's; step 1's food, drink, drugs and medicine keep theirs.
- **The card** keeps step 1's head (picture in its quality's frame, label, kind and worth, "All the game's stats", the line,
  the tags). The kind's words: "Metal, things are made of it" for stuff, the game's own filing otherwise ("Manufactured",
  "Stone chunks"), "Art, excellent, of marble" for art.
- **A material** (`Items/ItemCardMaterials.cs`):
  - **What it does to what is made of it**: a small table of the game's own numbers on it (`StuffNumbers`, read once a
    stuff): armour against sharp, blunt and heat and insulation against cold and heat (its stuff powers; only for apparel
    stuff), hit points, beauty, an added beauty, flammability, work to build and to make (its stat factors and offsets), the
    blows of blades and clubs (its damage multipliers; only for weapon stuff), worth and weight a unit. Beside it two others
    (`ItemCardMath.RefsFor`): the colony's most held stuff of its kind (the plan ahead's hourly stock), then the base game's
    usual, steel and wood for a hard material (granite blocks, plasteel after), cloth and plainleather for a soft one
    (devilstrand after), never itself. Its own value in good ink where it beats both, bad where it trails both. Its stuff
    kinds named.
  - **What the colony can make of it now**: every building and floor it is the stuff of or a part of, and every recipe that
    takes it (`RecipeDef.IsIngredient`), looked through once a kind; by research done (a building's own, a recipe's and its
    bench's), in four rows (buildings and floors, apparel, weapons, other things), the best first by worth (its own, else
    the game's sum: the stuff, the other ingredients and the work at `StatWorker_MarketValue.ValuePerWork`), three named and
    "N more"; how many more research would open and the research that opens the most.
  - **The colony's stock and what waits on it**: what it holds (on the map, not forbidden, and in packs); what the blueprints
    and frames still need (`Making.BuildingWants`, the trade advice's own reading); the bills that take it, each a line going
    to its bench and its bills (a batch's need, the bill's count; finite bills summed; one that can't start for want of it
    marked); repairs for components (the colony's machines that break down, the game's mean days between one machine's
    breakdowns read from `CompBreakdownable`, components a season); fuel (the buildings at home that burn it switched on,
    `CompRefuelable`'s rate over its fuel multiplier, those that burn only while used named apart, the colony's record of use
    where it has one, the days the stock lasts); the verdict by the trade advice's rules (`TradeAdvice.KindOf`,
    `TradeAdviceMath.Need`/`Keep` with the record of use): short for the plans, short of the need, more than the colony
    keeps, enough, or no count kept.
  - **Where it comes from here**: rocks on the map that yield it and aren't fogged, with about what they give mined (their
    yield, the drop chance for chunks, the storyteller's factor) and a click to one; a deep drill (where a ground-penetrating
    scanner is active, the spots it shows and how much); trees on the map and what they give cut now; the crops that grow it
    and the recipes that make it (step 1's lines, a click to the field or the bench and its bills); the colony's animals that
    give it shorn, make it, or would give it butchered, and the wild ones on the map; the colony's buildings made with it and
    what taking them down gives back; trade (step 1's part).
- **A work of art** (`Items/ItemCardArt.cs`):
  - **As art**: its beauty (the thing's, or a kind's in its stuff at normal quality), by quality (the game's stat for each
    quality in its stuff), its worth, material and flammability.
  - **Its story**: the art comp's title and artist, the tale's own name, the one it is about and its date (the tale through
    the art comp's private reference), and the game's own description of the image.
  - **Where it stands**: a placed piece is judged in the room its own cell belongs to, indoors when the room is a proper one
    and not outdoors in the mind. The room's beauty and impressiveness with it are the game's own (`Room.GetStat`); without
    it, the game's sums (`ItemCardMath.Without`: the piece's beauty over the room's beauty divisor, the game's own cell-count
    curve read once from `RoomStatWorker_Beauty`, and its worth out of the wealth; space and cleanliness kept), and the
    impressiveness as the game's number less the difference the game's formula gives (`ItemCardMath.Impressiveness`, the
    game's `RoomStatWorker_Impressiveness`), so the room's own number is never second-guessed. The verdict is the game's
    impressiveness stage (`RoomStatDef.GetScoreStage`), with and without; what the room's impressiveness does by its role
    (bedroom, barracks, dining room, recreation room, throne room, hospital, prison cell). Outdoors or not placed, it lifts
    no room: the card names the colony's rooms whose impressiveness gives a mood where it would do most, each with the piece
    added by the same sums, a click going to each. Nothing is moved.
  - **Keep or sell**: its worth against what the room loses ("Keep it: worth $1,400 to a trader, but the dining room would
    fall from very impressive to slightly impressive without it."), the room better without it (poor work), or where to place
    it.
  - **Who cares for it**: a noble's throne room or bedroom it stands in (Royalty's `RoomRequirement_Impressiveness` of their
    title, met with it and without it), a faith at home with precepts or memes about art (by their names' words: Alpha Memes'
    artist, art quality and art desired; `ItemCardMath.ArtRelated`), the artistic meditation focus and the psycasters at home
    who use it; small art Rimfolk's peoples carry and give (`ThingRole.SmallArt`).
- **The tags**, step 2's in the one vocabulary (`ItemCardMath.Vocabulary`, step 1's first; at most eight, the first strength
  and weakness kept), each from its own numbers against what it is compared with or Rimfolk's rules:
  - **Strength**: *Strong armour* (a sharp armour power of 100% or more, above steel's 90%), *Sturdy* (half again steel's hit
    points or more), *Fireproof* (a flammability of 5% or less), *Beautiful* (twice steel's beauty or more, or two beauty
    added; a work of art's beauty), *Warm* and *Keeps cool* (20 degrees of insulation or more; cloth gives 18), *Light* (a
    unit 60% of steel's weight or less: hard stuff and chunks, never the precious), *Sharp blades* (a tenth harder than
    steel's), *Hard blows* (a fifth harder), *Lifts the room* (a piece that raises its room a stage, or would raise one of the
    colony's once placed).
  - **Weakness**: *Soft* (70% of steel's hit points or less, hard stuff), *Burns* (as flammable as wood or more; a piece of
    50% or more), *Heavy* (160% of steel's weight or more; every chunk), *Slow to work* (half again the work or more),
    *Ugly* (a piece whose beauty is below nothing).
  - **Risk**: *Explodes in a fire* (the game's explosive comp: chemfuel), *Of a person* (human leather).
  - **Special**: *Precious* (`ThingRole.Precious`), *Gift for a people* (`ThingRole.Gift` for a material, `SmallArt` for art),
    *Masterwork* (masterwork or legendary), *Tells a story* (a tale is shown), *Valued by a faith*, *Meditation focus*.
  - **Role**: *Money* (silver), *Building material* (buildings the colony can build now take it), *For clothes* (apparel the
    colony can make is of it), *Fuel* (something at home burns it), *For repairs* (machines that break down), *Raw material*
    (a recipe turns it into stuff), *For a noble* (a noble's room it stands in), *Needed now* (the blueprints and bills want
    more than it holds, a bill can't start for want of it, or a stock the colony uses is under the advice's need; a count under
    the floor alone is said, not tagged), *Spare to sell* (beyond the advice's keep and the plans' share; a piece no room would
    rise with), *Trade good*.
  - **Needs**: *Research* (nothing of it open yet, the research that opens most), *A bench* (the bench that makes it, or turns
    it into stuff, isn't built), *A room* (a piece in storage, the room it would lift most).
- **The line** (`ItemCardMath.Plain`): a material's lead (the money; mends the colony's machines; fuel for its burners; made
  into what at which bench; the sturdiest of its kind there is; a precious one; a metal, timber, stone, fabric, leather or
  wool for building, armour, clothes or weapons; an ingredient of so many things), two strengths and two weaknesses at most,
  then its stock and what waits on it ("Plasteel: the sturdiest metal there is, light and fireproof, but slow to work; 340 in
  store, the blueprints need 60 more."). A work of art's beauty where it stands and its worth, then what selling it would do
  ("Grand sculpture, excellent: beauty 300 in the dining room, worth $1,400; selling it would make the room merely slightly
  impressive."), or where it would go.
- **Open it first**: the same hook (`Patch_WeaponCardFirst` asks `ItemCardFirst.Swapped`, now by the thing's own kind so a
  minified piece and a full grave count) and setting (`itemCardFirst`, its words naming materials and art); the button back on
  the game's card for these kinds too. The weapon and apparel cards are untouched.
- **Speed.** A material's stuff numbers, everything made of it (every building, floor and recipe), what yields it (rocks,
  trees, animals, the recipes that turn it into stuff) and what burns it are read once a kind and kept for the session
  (`PartOf`); recipe benches come from `Avail.RecipeUsers` (remembered; step 1's lines use it too now). A work of art's tale
  and its beauty by quality are read once a card. The colony's part (what it can make by research done, the stock, the
  blueprints and bills, the buildings, the deposits and scanner, trees and animals, the room with it and without it, the
  rooms it would lift, nobles, faiths) at most every ten seconds; the live parts at most once a second; the window draws only
  the model. No saved game data, no Sched slot.
- **Text**: `Languages/English/Keyed/Rimfolk_ItemCard.xml` (the table's rows `CC_ItemCard_Stuff_`, the rooms' roles
  `CC_ItemCard_RoomDoes_`); the tags and the line in English from the pure rules. **Tests**: `Tools/Tests/ItemCardStepTwoTests.cs`
  (458 checks): the kinds; the comparison (what each is compared with, the table's rows, values and tones); the sums (worth of
  what is made, repairs, fuel days, short, needed and spare, words); the tags and the line for steel, wood, plasteel, uranium,
  gold, silver, jade, cloth, devilstrand, hyperweave, plainleather, granite blocks, a granite chunk, components, advanced
  components and chemfuel, on their own and at home; the game's room sums (the factor, the yard, the space's cap, the divisor,
